properties.name: clinicalReportId
properties.description: The report the row was built from, in the same mixed id shapes as clinical_report.id; resolved by equality only.

properties.name: clinicalStage
properties.description: The report's own harmonised stage, not a pair-level maximum; all 13 codes occur, WITHDRAWAL and PHASE_4 included.

properties.name: drugId
properties.description: The ChEMBL molecule id of the drug the report names; all non-null values resolve in drug_molecule.id.

properties.name: drugFromSource
properties.description: The drug name as the source wrote it, with case and leading spaces unnormalised.

properties.name: trialWhyStopped
properties.description: The registry's free-text stop reason, verbatim; null on labels, approvals and warnings rather than on a stopped trial with a lost reason.

properties.name: trialStopReasonCategories
properties.description: Classifier labels read from the stop reason, in PascalCase codes; a null list means the report is not a stopped trial.

properties.name: studyStartDate
properties.description: The report's study start date as source text; null for labels, approvals and warnings.

properties.name: evidenceDate
properties.description: The earlier of publicationDate and studyStartDate as source text: the first date at which the evidence existed.

properties.name: publicationDate
properties.description: The oldest publication date among the cited literature, as source text; not the report's own date.

properties.name: literature
properties.description: PubMed ids the report cites, as strings; a null list means the report cites nothing.

properties.name: score
properties.description: The stage's rank value, halved once when Negative or Safety_Sideeffects is present; 14 discrete values from 0.005 to 1.0 and not comparable with another source's score.

properties.name: directionOnTrait
properties.description: Always 'protect'; an assumption of therapeutic intent emitted with every disease id, not a measured direction.

properties.name: directionOnTarget
properties.description: LoF or GoF translated from the drug's mechanism action type; null when the action type falls outside both lists, and the same value on every target row of the drug.

properties.name: clinicalStage
properties.description: The release's harmonised development-stage code, computed from phaseFromSource, source and trialOverallStatus; one of 13 codes including UNKNOWN, APPROVAL, PHASE_4 and WITHDRAWAL.

properties.name: reportType
properties.description: The document class the build assigned from clinical_report.type: INDICATION for a report stating a drug-disease use, SAFETY for a warning record. The property is named reportType because `type` is the record kind in the graph's file format.

properties.name: origin
properties.description: The source family the build assigned: CLINICAL_TRIAL, CURATED_RESOURCE, DRUG_LABEL or REGULATORY_AGENCY.

properties.name: source
properties.description: The reference the report was read from, for example ClinicalTrials.gov, TTD, DailyMed, ATC, EMA, FDA or PMDA.

properties.name: provider
properties.description: The pipeline that supplied the record: AACT, ChEMBL, EMA, PMDA or TTD.

properties.name: trialSponsor
properties.description: The sponsor name the registry recorded.

properties.name: trialSponsorAgencyClass
properties.description: The sponsor's registry class: INDUSTRY, NIH, OTHER_GOV, NETWORK, FED, INDIV or OTHER.

properties.name: phaseFromSource
properties.description: The stage string exactly as the source stated it, before harmonisation (for example PHASE2, phase 1/phase 2, withdrawn, black box warning).

properties.name: trialPhase
properties.description: The registry's own phase code (PHASE1, PHASE1/PHASE2, PHASE2/PHASE3, PHASE4, EARLY_PHASE1); null on non-registry rows and where the registry recorded none.

properties.name: trialOverallStatus
properties.description: The registry's recruitment and availability status (COMPLETED, TERMINATED, RECRUITING, ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING, UNKNOWN, ...); not a study result.

properties.name: trialWhyStopped
properties.description: The sponsor's free-text reason for ending the study.

properties.name: trialStopReasonCategories
properties.description: Classifier labels assigned to a stopped study, up to three per row; Uncategorised is the classifier's fallback, not a sponsor's reason.

properties.name: countries
properties.description: The markets a drug warning was issued in, split from the warning's own semicolon string; filled on the 2,744 SAFETY rows only and as free text with no country code scheme.

properties.name: trialDescription
properties.description: The registry's brief summary of the study, as free text.

properties.name: trialOfficialTitle
properties.description: The registered title as the sponsor wrote it.

properties.name: title
properties.description: The report heading: the registered title when one exists, otherwise a sentence the build generated from the stage, first drug and first disease.

properties.name: trialPrimaryPurpose
properties.description: The registry's declared primary purpose (TREATMENT, PREVENTION, BASIC_SCIENCE, DIAGNOSTIC, ...); null is not the OTHER code.

properties.name: trialStudyType
properties.description: The registry's design class, kept to three values: INTERVENTIONAL, OBSERVATIONAL or EXPANDED_ACCESS.

properties.name: trialNumberOfArms
properties.description: The number of arms the registry recorded; a null is not zero arms.

properties.name: trialStartDate
properties.description: The date the study began; 1900-01-31 and 2099-01-01 are registry placeholders, not measured starts.

properties.name: year
properties.description: The year a drug warning was issued; filled on warning rows only and not the year of a trial or an approval.

properties.name: url
properties.description: The source record's address; not a key, because one source document can back several reports.

properties.name: qualityControls
properties.description: Flags naming a reason a consumer may drop the report (NO_DISEASE, UNVALIDATED_INDICATION, INDIRECT_PRIMARY_PURPOSE, PHASE_IV_NOT_APPROVED, SAFETY_REPORT); flagged rows stay published.

document.description: A knowledge graph of the Open Targets Platform 26.09 release. Nodes are entities the release identifies; edges are relations the release reports, derives or lets a consumer read from its records. The graph is a semantic index over the release, not a replacement for the release's own data.

purpose.text: Target-disease evidence review and prioritisation over the Open Targets 26.09 release. For one target, disease or other entity, a consumer asks which relations the release reports, what each relation means, where it came from, and what it does not imply. The graph supports triage and prioritisation; it does not validate a target or establish causation.

frames.text: in this release

limitations.text: Do not read this as what an upstream authority permits or what an earlier release contained.

frames.text: association

limitations.text: Do not read this as a statistical association in a study, or a causal relation.

frames.text: evidence

limitations.text: Do not read this as one harmonised quantity comparable across evidence sources.

frames.text: identifier form

limitations.text: Do not read this as the Platform resolver, which normalises the separator on lookup.

frames.text: score

limitations.text: Do not read this as a probability, a p-value, or one universal confidence measure.

claims.text: A knowledge graph of the Open Targets Platform 26.09 release. Nodes are entities the release identifies; edges are relations the release reports, derives or lets a consumer read from its records. The graph is a semantic index over the release, not a replacement for the release's own data.
What the 26.09 files were measured to contain, never what an upstream authority permits or what an earlier release contained.
A target-disease relation reported by the release from one or more evidence sources, with a score and evidence count. It is not a causal claim and it is not a prediction made by this graph.

A source-specific observation that a target is linked to a disease or phenotype. The observation carries the source's own method and score; the graph does not harmonise those meanings into one quantity.
The spelling of an ontology accession in the release: PREFIX_accession and PREFIX:accession are different strings. A join, filter or resolver must use the form the column actually carries.
A source-specific numeric judgement. Different datasets call different statistics score; a score is not comparable across datasets unless the graph states the comparison.
Ensembl gene identifiers (ENSG) are stable human gene accessions.
Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO), MONDO, HPO, GO, SO and Reactome accessions denote ontology terms in their respective namespaces.
A target-disease association score is a weighted aggregate over evidence sources; its scale and weighting are release-specific.

components.name: credible_set_colocalises_with
components.label: COLOCALISES_WITH
components.description: A colocalisation between two credible sets.

claims.text: A colocalisation the release reports between a left and a right credible set: evidence that the two loci share a causal variant under the release's colocalisation method.

(leftStudyLocusId, rightStudyLocusId, colocalisationMethod). The release ships one method (COLOC_PIP_ECAVIAR) and 0 duplicate pair+method rows over 283,303,467 rows. The pair is also unique and no row exists in the reverse orientation, so left and right are the release's roles, not an arbitrary ordering.

frames.text: clpp is the colocalisation posterior probability. h3 is the posterior probability of two distinct causal variants and h4 of one shared variant. betaRatioSignAverage is the average sign of the beta ratio and is null on 119,431,152 rows. rightStudyType names the right set's study type; the release supplies no left study type. numberColocalisingVariants counts variants in the shared signal.

limitations.text: No edge means the release reports no colocalisation for the pair under the method it ships. Both endpoints resolve to credible sets in 26.09.

283,303,467 edges, the largest relation in this graph; carrying it in full is a deliberate scale decision and dominates the build. A single method means the method property cannot discriminate. Colocalisation is not proof of a shared causal variant: h3 can exceed h4, and clpp is model output. The relation is stored left->right and has no reciprocal rows, so undirected queries must traverse both directions.

claims.text: The colocalisation method that produced the row.

frames.text: Only COLOC_PIP_ECAVIAR occurs in 26.09, so the property does not partition the edges.

limitations.text: Do not read the value as a comparison of methods; a future release may ship several.

claims.text: The colocalisation posterior probability for the pair.

frames.text: Values run from 3.7e-10 to 1.0; higher means stronger evidence of a shared signal.

limitations.text: It is model output under the release's priors, not a direct measurement or a replication.

claims.text: The posterior probability that the two sets have two distinct causal variants.

frames.text: Read h3 against h4: h3 high with h4 low argues against a shared variant.

limitations.text: The hypotheses are model-defined and their priors are not on the edge.

claims.text: The posterior probability that the two sets share one causal variant.

frames.text: h4 is the hypothesis behind the colocalisation claim; it is not a probability that a specific variant is causal.

limitations.text: A high h4 does not identify the shared variant; the membership edges do not carry that identity.

claims.text: The average sign of the beta ratio across the colocalising variants.

frames.text: Its sign indicates whether the two studies' effects point the same way.

limitations.text: An average sign is not an effect size and does not test for a shared direction.

claims.text: The number of variants in the shared signal.

frames.text: Measured 1-3,077; larger values mean a wider shared signal.

limitations.text: A count of variants is not a count of independent causal variants.

claims.text: The chromosome of the colocalising locus.

frames.text: Measured equal to both endpoint credible sets' chromosome on every row.

limitations.text: It is a locus-level fact, not a claim about a specific variant.

claims.text: The study type of the right credible set.

frames.text: 26.09 values are gwas, eqtl, sqtl, tuqtl, pqtl and sceqtl; measured equal to the right credible set's studyType on every row. The left set's study type is not supplied on the row.

limitations.text: It describes the right endpoint only; do not read it as the type of the pair.

claims.text: One edge per colocalisation row: a left credible set colocalises with a right credible set.
(leftStudyLocusId, rightStudyLocusId, colocalisationMethod). 0 duplicate rows over 283,303,467. The pair alone is also unique and no reverse-direction row exists.

frames.text: 283,303,467 edges, all under COLOC_PIP_ECAVIAR. Both endpoints resolve to credible_set.studyLocusId (0 dangling on either side). The edge runs from the release's left set to its right set.

limitations.text: No edge means the release reports no colocalisation for the pair; it does not mean the loci are independent.

The full 283M rows are carried deliberately; this relation dominates the graph's edge volume and build cost. There are no reciprocal rows, so consumers must traverse both directions for an undirected view. betaRatioSignAverage is null on 119,431,152 rows.

components.name: credible_set_contains_variant
components.label: CONTAINS_VARIANT
components.description: A variant's membership in a credible set.

claims.text: One variant's membership in a fine-mapped credible set, carrying the variant-level statistics the release reports for that membership.

(studyLocusId, variantId). The pair is unique for every membership whose variant exists in the release (0 duplicates over 110,939,251 resolvable rows). 21 pairs occur more than once (27 rows), all for three symbolic <DEL> variant ids that have no VARIANT node.

frames.text: posteriorProbability is the variant's membership probability inside the set, not a causal probability outside it. beta and standardError are the study's effect estimate, and pValueMantissa/pValueExponent encode the p-value. r2Overall is LD r² to the set's lead variant and is absent for most rows.

limitations.text: No edge means the variant is not in that credible set. 1,494 membership rows name 651 variant ids with no VARIANT node (630 symbolic structural-variant alleles and 21 alt-contig coordinates), so those edges dangle.

110,940,745 edges; membership is a statistical set, not a causal claim. A variant can be in several sets, and the same set's lead variant is a separate edge. Null statistics are release gaps: logBF is null on 24,500,428 rows, beta on 23,813,059, standardError on 15,809,462, the p-value on 32,391,750 and r2Overall on 86,440,317.

claims.text: The probability the variant belongs to the credible set under the release's fine-mapping.

frames.text: Values run from 5.4e-06 to 1.0; a value is per variant and per set.

limitations.text: It is a membership probability, not the probability that the variant is causal.

claims.text: The variant's log Bayes factor for belonging to the credible set.

frames.text: Larger supports inclusion more strongly.

limitations.text: Null on 24,500,428 of 110,940,745 elements.
Log Bayes factors are not comparable across studies with different priors and models.

claims.text: The study's effect-size estimate for the variant.

frames.text: The scale and effect allele are study-specific; read it with the study and credible set.

limitations.text: Null on 23,813,059 elements.
A beta from one study is not an effect on a target or a disease in general.

claims.text: The standard error of the variant's beta.

frames.text: Use it with beta; it is not a confidence interval.

limitations.text: Null on 15,809,462 elements.
It inherits the study's model and sample size; it is not comparable across studies.

claims.text: The mantissa of the variant's association p-value, p = mantissa x 10^exponent.

frames.text: Read it with pValueExponent; neither part is meaningful alone.

limitations.text: Null on 32,391,750 elements.
A p-value is not an effect size and does not establish causality.

claims.text: The base-10 exponent of the variant's association p-value.

frames.text: Negative values are the usual case; use it only with pValueMantissa.

limitations.text: Null on 32,391,750 elements, always together with pValueMantissa.
Do not compare exponents across studies as a strength ranking without the mantissa.

claims.text: The variant's overall LD r² to the credible set's lead variant.

frames.text: Measured 0.50-1.0 where present, so these are variants in LD with the lead.

limitations.text: Null on 86,440,317 of 110,940,745 elements; a null r² is not zero LD.
r² depends on the study's LD reference population; it is not a functional similarity.

claims.text: One edge per credible_set.locus element, carrying the variant-level membership statistics.

(studyLocusId, variantId). 110,940,745 edges and 110,940,724 distinct pairs; 21 duplicated pairs (27 rows) all name three symbolic <DEL> variants that are absent from variant. Among resolvable variants the key is unique (0 duplicates over 110,939,251 rows).

frames.text: Every locus element becomes an edge; posteriorProbability is membership probability, not causality. 1,494 rows name 651 variant ids with no VARIANT node, so those edges dangle.

limitations.text: No edge means the variant is not in the set. A credible set node always has a lead-variant edge separately; membership is not implied by it.

110.9M edges; this is the second-largest relation in the graph. The 21 key collisions and the 1,494 dangling rows come from structural and alt-contig variant spellings the release did not put in the variant table. Null statistics stay null rather than becoming zero.

components.name: credible_set_lead_variant
components.label: HAS_LEAD_VARIANT
components.description: The lead variant of a credible set.

claims.text: The credible set's lead variant, the variant with the highest posterior probability.
studyLocusId -> variantId.

components.name: disease_has_cross_reference
components.label: HAS_CROSS_REFERENCE
components.description: An external identifier listed in a disease term's cross-references.

claims.text: The disease term's record lists the external identifier.
disease -> source:identifier, keyed disease::HAS_CROSS_REFERENCE::source:identifier. The 127,496 elements are 127,496 distinct pairs within a term.

frames.text: source is the part before the first colon (PMID, UMLS, MEDGEN, GARD, DOID, Orphanet, SCTID, OMIM, MESH, NCIT, ICD9, icd11.foundation, uniprot, EFO, NANDO and others); identifier is the remainder, which may itself contain separators.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no such identifier for the term. A value without a colon cannot name a namespace: one element (EFO_0020991, the sentence 'Quantification of ethanolamine in a sample.') is kept with that sentence as source and an empty identifier rather than dropped.

The edge asserts a listed identifier, not that the external record was verified or describes the same concept. Namespace spelling differs across datasets (NCIT beside NCIt, Orphanet beside ORPHA), so the same authority can yield several nodes.

claims.text: One HAS_CROSS_REFERENCE edge per element of disease.dbXRefs.
disease::HAS_CROSS_REFERENCE::source:identifier; 127,496 distinct keys over 127,496 elements.

frames.text: Read term -> identifier; the edge carries no qualifier.

limitations.text: No element means the release lists no such identifier for the term.
A listed identifier is not identity with the external record or with another entity citing it.

components.name: disease_has_obsolete_cross_reference
components.label: HAS_OBSOLETE_CROSS_REFERENCE
components.description: A retired external identifier listed in a disease term's cross-references.

claims.text: The disease term's record lists the external identifier as one it no longer uses.
disease -> source:identifier, keyed disease::HAS_OBSOLETE_CROSS_REFERENCE::source:identifier. The 24,527 elements are 24,207 distinct pairs; 320 pairs repeat within a term.

frames.text: A separate edge type keeps the retirement assertion: 12,183 pairs are listed both here and in dbXRefs for the same term, so one combined edge type could not carry both states without a qualifier that the shared cross-reference identity does not have.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no retired identifier. A retired identifier can still be the term's current identifier in the external namespace or in another term's dbXRefs.
Retirement is the release's assertion about its own mapping, not proof that the external record was withdrawn. The release names no replacement identifier.

claims.text: One HAS_OBSOLETE_CROSS_REFERENCE edge per element of disease.obsoleteXRefs.
disease::HAS_OBSOLETE_CROSS_REFERENCE::source:identifier; 24,207 distinct keys over 24,527 elements, so 320 duplicate elements collapse.

frames.text: Read term -> retired identifier. A separate edge type preserves the retirement that the shared identifier would otherwise lose.

limitations.text: No element means the release lists no retired identifier for the term.
Retirement is the release's mapping statement; it does not prove the external record was withdrawn.

components.name: disease_has_obsolete_term
components.label: HAS_OBSOLETE_TERM
components.description: A retired ontology accession listed by a disease term.

claims.text: The disease term lists the accession as one it has retired.
disease -> accession, keyed disease::HAS_OBSOLETE_TERM::accession. The 9,852 elements are 9,838 distinct pairs; 14 accessions repeat within a term.

frames.text: Verified resolution: none of the 9,852 elements is a disease.id or a disease_hpo.id, so the target is an ObsoleteTermNode rather than a DISEASE node; a DISEASE target would dangle on every element.

limitations.text: No edge means the term lists no retired accession.
The edge preserves a historical accession. It does not state that the retired term was merged, split or replaced by this term, and it cannot be traversed backwards to a current term.

claims.text: One HAS_OBSOLETE_TERM edge per element of disease.obsoleteTerms.
disease::HAS_OBSOLETE_TERM::accession; 9,838 distinct keys.

frames.text: Read current term -> retired accession. All 9,852 targets resolve to the ObsoleteTermNode set, which is populated from the same arrays.

limitations.text: No element means the release lists no retired accession for the term.
The edge does not state a merge, split or replacement, and it cannot be traversed backwards to a current term.

components.name: disease_has_phenotype
components.label: HAS_PHENOTYPE
components.description: One disease-to-phenotype evidence record.

claims.text: The disease term has the phenotype, as asserted by one evidence record of disease_phenotype. The edge is the record; the endpoint nodes are the disease and the phenotype.

disease -> phenotype, discriminated by the curating record and the assertion's own fields: disease::HAS_PHENOTYPE::phenotype::diseaseFromSourceId::bioCuration::frequency::onset::references, arrays joined with | and a null frequency written as the empty string. The tuple yields 178,888 distinct keys over 220,970 evidence elements, equal to the number of distinct full evidence tuples, so it separates every pair of non-identical records. 42,082 elements (19.0%) repeat an identical record for the same pair and collapse onto one key.

frames.text: One edge per evidence element, so the 163,973 disease-phenotype pairs expand to 220,970 edges; one pair (MONDO_0019588 - HP_0000007) carries 83, distinguished by source record. bioCuration names the curator and date (HPO:probinson[2012-05-01] or ORCID:...), diseaseFromSource(Id) the source disease record (OMIM or DECIPHER), frequency a ratio such as 1/14 or an HPO frequency term such as HP_0040283, and references the cited records.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no phenotype annotation for the pair. A null disease or phenotype cannot key an endpoint and drops the row; the release carries none. A null frequency stays null on the edge and is written as the empty string in the key.

22,759 of the 220,970 evidence elements (10.3%), which collapse to 18,325 of the 178,888 edges (10.2%), name one of 285 phenotype accessions absent from disease_hpo; every one is a MONDO or EFO disease term, so those edges point at no PHENOTYPE node and the disease-side term is reachable only through the DISEASE node of the same accession. An annotation is not a diagnosis, prevalence or causal claim, and frequency text is not a normalized proportion. diseaseName is not carried: it is a display variant of diseaseFromSource, differing on 189,979 records.

claims.text: The single-letter aspect code the release assigns to the evidentiary record.
A qualifier of the record, not part of the edge key.

frames.text: Observed values are P (199,385 records), I (10,728), C (10,684), M (112) and H (61).

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
The dataset ships no legend for the letters, so a category must not be inferred from the letter. The code describes the record, not the phenotype term.

claims.text: Curator identity and curation date of the source annotation.
One component of the edge key.

frames.text: Values pair a curator and a date in brackets, for example HPO:probinson[2012-05-01], HPO:iea[2009-02-17] or ORCID:0000-0002-0736-9199[2025-03-05]. 57,569 records list several curations in one semicolon-separated string, up to six; 23,799 records mention an ORCID.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
An ORCID names an annotator and an HPO:iea value marks an inferred electronic annotation; neither is a publication. The date is the curation date, not the observation date.

claims.text: Accession of the source disease record the annotation was curated from.
One component of the edge key.

frames.text: 220,685 records cite an OMIM accession and 285 a DECIPHER accession; one source record can support many phenotypes of one disease.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Not a disease.id join key: the values use OMIM and DECIPHER namespaces, and one release disease term can aggregate several source records. Use the edge's disease endpoint to reach the DISEASE node.

claims.text: Disease label as the source record spells it.
A qualifier of the record, not part of the edge key.

frames.text: Free text in the source's naming style, for example 'Megabladder, congenital' or 'Spermatogenic failure 93'.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
It is the source's name for the source record, not the preferred label of the edge's disease endpoint and not proof that the source concept is identical to the release term.

claims.text: HPO evidence code stating how the annotation was made.
A qualifier of the record, not part of the edge key.

frames.text: Three values occur: PCS (148,236 records), IEA (43,528) and TAS (29,206).

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
IEA marks an inferred electronic annotation and is not equivalent to a curated PCS assertion. The code is not a confidence score and the dataset does not define the abbreviations.

claims.text: Frequency of the phenotype in the disease as the source states it.
One component of the edge key; a null value is written as the empty string there and stays null on the edge.

frames.text: Two shapes occur: a ratio such as 1/14 or 3/3, and an HPO frequency term such as HP_0040283 (3,658 records). 88,055 records carry no frequency.

limitations.text: Null means the source stated no frequency, not a frequency of zero.
Ratios, HPO terms and free text are not comparable without a conversion the release does not carry. Frequency is the source's claim about the disease, not a measured cohort prevalence.

claims.text: HPO clinical-modifier accessions the source attaches to the annotation.
A qualifier of the record; the array is not part of the edge key.

frames.text: Values are colon-form HPO accessions such as HP:0012825. 1,360 records carry a modifier and 219,610 carry an empty array.

limitations.text: An empty array means no modifier was stated; it is the norm.
The colon form is not the underscore form used by disease_hpo ids, so these values do not key a PHENOTYPE node.

claims.text: HPO onset accessions the source attaches to the annotation.
One component of the edge key, joined with |; an empty array is an empty string there.

frames.text: Values are colon-form HPO accessions such as HP:0003577. 4,019 records carry an onset and 216,951 carry an empty array.

limitations.text: An empty array means no onset was stated, not an onset at birth.
The colon form is not the underscore form used by disease_hpo ids. One record can state several onsets, and their order is not meaningful.

claims.text: Free-text qualifier the source attaches to the annotation.
A qualifier of the record, not part of the edge key.

frames.text: Null on all 220,970 records in 26.09.

limitations.text: Null on every record, so the property carries no information in this release.
Do not read a null as 'no qualifier stated' as opposed to 'not populated': the release never populates the field, so both readings are indistinguishable.

claims.text: Whether the annotation asserts the negation of the phenotype.
A qualifier of the record, not part of the edge key.

frames.text: False on all 220,970 records in 26.09.

limitations.text: Never null; false is the only observed value.
A constant false says the release recorded no negated annotation, not that the phenotype was excluded by study design.

claims.text: Records cited for the annotation, one accession per element.
One component of the edge key, joined with |; the array is never empty.

frames.text: Resolved choice: all 71,009 targets are disease-table rows, and every target is one of the 26 terms whose ontology.isTherapeuticArea is true, so the target is a DISEASE node and no separate therapeutic-area node type exists. components.name: disease_is_a

claims.text: The child disease term is a direct subtype of the parent term, as the release asserts in disease.parents.
child -> parent, keyed child::IS_A::parent. The 64,021 array elements over the 45,896 terms are 64,021 distinct pairs; 25 terms list no parent.

frames.text: One edge per listed parent, so a term with several parents carries several edges. Both ends are DISEASE nodes: the term set mixes EFO, MONDO, GO, HP, Orphanet and other accessions, so an edge can cross vocabularies.

limitations.text: No edge means the term lists no parent (25 terms) or is not in the release. The release does not distinguish a root from a term whose parents were left empty.

A parent link is a classification, not causal, anatomical or temporal containment.

frames.text: In the row's unit; exactly 0.0 on 62,600,925 rows because some pooled samples had no count.

claims.text: Third quartile of the measurement distribution.

frames.text: In the row's unit.

limitations.text: Null on the same 164,481 rows as min.

frames.text: In the row's unit; the release maximum is 290,572,862.

limitations.text: Null on 26,506,752 rows: every PRIDE row and parts of DICE, gtex and tabula_sapiens. Absence means the source did not compute it, not that specificity is zero.

frames.text: An empty array on all 83,290,030 rows in 26.09, so the property never qualifies an edge.

targetId|EXPRESSED_IN|datasourceId|tissueBiosampleId|celltypeBiosampleId|tissueBiosampleFromSource|celltypeBiosampleFromSource, with the empty string for a null id or label: 83,290,030 rows and 83,289,724 distinct keys.

components.name: target_has_constraint
components.label: HAS_CONSTRAINT

target.id -> constraintType: key = target::HAS_CONSTRAINT::constraint_type::constraintType. A target has at most one row per family in the release.

A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.

A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.

limitations.text: Null when the release did not compute an expectation.

A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.

A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.

The ratio is not a significance test; use the release's score for its ranking.

claims.text: The lower bound of the confidence interval on oe.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.

frames.text: Read together with oe and oeUpper.

limitations.text: Null when the release did not compute an interval.
The interval's method and level stay in the source dataset.

claims.text: The upper bound of the confidence interval on oe.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.

frames.text: Read together with oe and oeLower.

limitations.text: Null when the release did not compute an interval.
The interval's method and level stay in the source dataset.

claims.text: The gene's rank in the release's constraint distribution.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.

limitations.text: Null when the release did not rank the gene.
Do not compare ranks across constraint families.

claims.text: The gene's bin index in the release's constraint distribution.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.

frames.text: A coarse position derived from the rank.

A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.

target::HAS_CONSTRAINT::constraint_type::constraintType; the release holds at most one row per target and family.

claims.text: The DepMap gene-effect score for the target in the cell line.

claims.text: The target's expression level in the cell line.

One component of the edge key.

target::HAS_GO_ANNOTATION::go.id::source::evidence::aspect::geneProduct::ecoId, with the empty string for a null ecoId. The tuple is unique per target and term in the release.

components.name: target_has_homologue
components.label: HAS_HOMOLOGUE
components.description: The release records a homologue of the target in a species.

claims.text: One Ensembl compara homology pair: the target has the named homologue gene, with the pair class, the source's confidence flag and the two directional percentage identities.
targetId|HAS_HOMOLOGUE|speciesId|targetGeneId: 3,817,240 edges, one per source row, unique; 25,537 of the 78,733 targets have at least one edge (1-1,335 each, median 19).

frames.text: homologyType is the pair class: other_paralog 3,484,279, ortholog_one2one 168,810, within_species_paralog 67,968, ortholog_many2many 57,952, ortholog_one2many 38,222, gene_split 9. queryPercentageIdentity measures targetId against targetGeneId; targetPercentageIdentity is the same pair measured from the homologue's side. The two differ on 3,323,472 rows and agree on 493,768. isHighConfidence is the source's text flag, not a boolean.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no compara pair between the target and that gene; 53,196 targets have no homology row at all. That is a source gap, not evidence that the target has no homologue.

Human pairs are stored twice, once per direction: 3,544,066 of the 3,552,256 human rows have a reverse row with the two identity values swapped, the same homologyType and the same flag. Both directions are kept because each row is the release's own query measurement and the identity values are not symmetric; the cost is that the 1,772,033 undirected human pairs account for 3,544,066 edges, so counting edges double-counts pairs. 8,190 human rows have no reverse: 8,181 name one of the 46 human gene ids that are absent from target.id and 9 are gene_split. Only 20,864 of the 20,910 human gene ids are targets.
Each human paralogue pair is stored in both directions.
The number of HAS_HOMOLOGUE edges is the number of homologue genes, or the number of undirected pairs.
A non-human homologue is a gene record only.
A mouse or zebrafish homologue is a target of this release.

claims.text: The Ensembl compara classification of the pair.

frames.text: Six values: other_paralog (human-only, 3,484,279), ortholog_one2one (168,810, the 12 non-human species), within_species_paralog (human-only, 67,968), ortholog_many2many, ortholog_one2many and gene_split (9). Every non-human edge is an ortholog class; every human-query edge is a paralog or gene_split class.

limitations.text: The classes answer different questions: paralogues sit in one genome, orthologues across genomes, and many-to-many records a family-level correspondence with no one-to-one gene. Do not rank or pool the classes.

claims.text: The source's confidence flag for the pair, carried as the text the release writes: '1', '0' or null.

frames.text: '1' on 168,998 edges, '0' on 95,986 and null on 3,552,256. Null is exactly the human rows: the flag is only populated for cross-species orthologue pairs, so every human paralogue edge and all 9 gene_split edges carry null.

limitations.text: Null means the source states no confidence for this pair class, not low confidence; casting the column to boolean without keeping null makes 93.1% of the rows indistinguishable from '0'.
It is a source flag on a pair, not a probability, a score or a comparison between pairs of different classes.

claims.text: Percentage identity of the query gene (this target) to the homologue, on the source's 0-100 scale.

claims.text: Percentage identity of the homologue to the query gene, on the source's 0-100 scale.

frames.text: 0-100 with no nulls. It is the same pair as queryPercentageIdentity measured from the other sequence, so the two values differ on 3,323,472 rows and are equal on 493,768.

claims.text: One HAS_HOMOLOGUE edge per row of homology.
targetId|HAS_HOMOLOGUE|speciesId|targetGeneId: 3,817,240 edges, one per source row; the row set is unique on (targetId, targetGeneId) and the species is determined by the gene.

limitations.text: No edge means no compara pair for that target and gene. 53,196 targets have no row and therefore no edge.

The 3,817,240 edges are 3,817,240 source measurements, not 3,817,240 undirected pairs: human pairs are stored in both directions, so 1,772,033 human pairs account for 3,544,066 edges. The edge keeps both directions rather than choosing one, because the identity values differ by direction and 8,190 human rows have no reverse.

components.name: target_has_mouse_model

limitations.text: A null property is an unrecorded fact, not a zero. Null trial columns on the 58,965 non-registry rows are structural: those rows are labels, approvals and warnings.
The node is called a trial but is a report; counts of this label are not trial counts. No outcome, target or effect size is carried.

components.name: constraint_type
components.label: CONSTRAINT_TYPE
components.description: One constraint metric family reported for targets.

claims.text: A constraint metric family: missense (mis), loss of function (lof) or synonymous (syn). The node names the family; each target's values are on the HAS_CONSTRAINT edge.
constraint_type::constraintType, one of mis, lof and syn.

frames.text: The same gene has up to three constraint edges, one per family. Compare values only within one family.

limitations.text: A gene with no constraint edge has no metric in the release, which is not a value of zero.
Constraint is a population-variation depletion signal, not a measured essentiality or a statement that loss of function is pathogenic.

claims.text: The constraint metric family reported on this node.
The node key.

frames.text: mis is missense, lof is loss of function, syn is synonymous.

limitations.text: The release's constraint array never carries a null constraintType.
The three families are separate metrics; their scores are not comparable.

claims.text: One ConstraintTypeNode per constraint family in target.constraint.
constraint_type::constraintType, one of mis, lof and syn.

frames.text: The same three nodes are rebuilt from every target row; the metric values stay on the per-target edge.

limitations.text: No element means the target has no constraint metric in the release.
The node names a metric family, not a threshold or a verdict.

components.name: credible_set
components.label: CREDIBLE_SET
components.description: A fine-mapped credible set for one study locus.

claims.text: A 95% credible set from a GWAS or molecular QTL study, with the lead variant, fine-mapping method and summary statistics.
credible_set.studyLocusId. It is unique in the release and names one study-locus credible set, not one variant.

frames.text: credibleSetIndex orders sets within a study locus. The lead variant is the variant with the highest posterior probability, not the causal variant.

limitations.text: No credible set means the study has no fine-mapped locus in the release, not that no association exists.
A credible set is a statistical set, not a biological mechanism. Membership does not establish causality; the L2G edge is a prediction.

claims.text: GRCh38 chromosome of the set's lead variant, stored without a chr prefix.

frames.text: Categorical string from 1-22, X and Y; read it with position.

limitations.text: Never null; unusable chromosomes reject the row rather than nulling it.
Its value set differs from the variant and colocalisation chromosome columns; it is not the locus span.

claims.text: One-based GRCh38 position of the set's lead variant.

frames.text: Base pairs; always paired with chromosome.

limitations.text: Never null.
The lead's position, not the fine-mapped interval and not a causal coordinate.

claims.text: Text start and end of the fine-mapped region, in one of two incompatible formats.

frames.text: Either chr-prefixed or bare and zero-based text; parse tolerantly.

limitations.text: Null on every PICS row, whose method publishes no window here.
Null does not mean the set has no region; prefer the integer locus bounds where populated.

claims.text: Effect size of the lead variant with respect to its alternate allele.

frames.text: Sign gives ALT-allele direction; scale comes from the producing pipeline and is comparable only within a study.

limitations.text: Null when the source published no estimate, not a measured zero.
Never pool across finemappingMethod; a SuSiE beta is a shrunk posterior mean.

claims.text: Signed association statistic for the lead variant, beta divided by its standard error.

frames.text: Standard-error units, sharing beta's polarity.

limitations.text: Null on every non-SuSiE-inf row, so a null is a method boundary rather than an absence of association.
It describes only the SuSiE-inf subset and cannot characterise the whole file's signal strength.

claims.text: Mantissa half of the lead variant's study p-value, with p equal to mantissa times ten to the exponent.

frames.text: Range 1.0 to 10.0; read it only with pValueExponent.

limitations.text: Never null at lead level in 26.09.
An unconditioned study p-value, not a posterior probability; sorting on it alone gives the wrong order.

claims.text: Base-10 exponent half of the lead variant's study p-value.

frames.text: Negative integer; smaller means stronger and it is read with the mantissa.

limitations.text: Never null at lead level in 26.09.
Not the set's posterior evidence; a null here would mean the member-level field was read instead.

claims.text: Frequency of the lead variant's effect allele as the source study reported it.

frames.text: Proportion from 0 to 1, specific to the study's ancestry and allele coding.

limitations.text: Null when the source published no frequency, overwhelmingly molecular-QTL and curated-top-hit rows; not frequency zero.
Not a reference-panel frequency; filtering non-null restricts analysis to studies that reported it.

claims.text: Standard error of the lead variant's beta.

frames.text: Effect-size units; beta divided by it approximates the z-score, and zero is suspect.

limitations.text: Null when the source published no standard error, not a precision of zero.
Some pipelines publish placeholder or member-level values, so it is not always the study's estimate.

claims.text: Fine-mapping algorithm that produced the set's posteriors.

frames.text: Categorical values SuSie, SuSiE-inf and PICS; case-sensitive, and the method predicts which columns are populated.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
A pipeline label, not a model specification or a quality rank.

claims.text: One-based ordinal of this set among the sets returned for its study region, up to ten.

frames.text: Ordinal position, not an importance ranking; most populated rows are index 1.

limitations.text: Null on every PICS row, whose method does not enumerate signals.
The first index is not the causal set, and a non-null filter is a method filter in disguise.

claims.text: Base-10 log Bayes factor that the credible set contains a causal variant.

frames.text: Unbounded model evidence; higher is stronger and values span many orders of magnitude.

limitations.text: Null on every PICS row, which returns no model evidence; null is not weak evidence.
Orthogonal to resolution; read it with set size and never as a probability.

claims.text: Mean pairwise linkage-disequilibrium R-squared among the set's member variants.

frames.text: Zero to one; near one means little internal resolution, while a low value means the set spans weakly linked variants.

limitations.text: Null where the pipeline computed no within-set LD; not a purity of zero.
Read it with set size; high purity is not good resolution.

claims.text: Minimum pairwise linkage-disequilibrium R-squared within the credible set.

frames.text: Zero to one; a single-member set reads 1 trivially.

limitations.text: Null where no within-set LD was computed, not zero LD.
Method-specific floors are not global; do not threshold the whole column.

claims.text: Study-level sample size copied onto the credible set.

frames.text: Rough study attribute; many rows share a few values.

limitations.text: Null where the study index surfaced no usable total, not a small study.
Not for power calculations and not always a real cohort size.

claims.text: Fine-mapping framework and linkage-disequilibrium source behind the set, as a four-value label.

frames.text: Ordinal provenance, best first; 26.09 stores long labels such as 'SuSiE fine-mapped credible set with in-sample LD'.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09; the documented unknown class does not occur.
Not association strength or effect size; never sort the labels alphabetically.

claims.text: Study design behind the credible set: gwas or one of five molecular QTL classes.

frames.text: Lower-case categorical code copied from the study; read it with isTransQtl.

limitations.text: Never null; unknown designs are excluded upstream.
Says nothing about tissue or condition; read the joined study for those.

claims.text: Whether the molecular-QTL lead variant lies more than five megabases from the gene whose molecular trait is measured.

frames.text: Boolean cis/trans flag from a fixed five-megabase window.

limitations.text: Null on exactly the GWAS rows, where cis and trans are undefined; false is measured cis.
Populated on all molecular-QTL classes despite the name, and the deciding distance is not published.

claims.text: One CredibleSetNode per row of credible_set.
credible_set.studyLocusId.

frames.text: The lead variant and membership edges carry the set's interpretation; the node carries the set-level statistics.

limitations.text: A missing statistic is not a zero. A study without a credible set is not fine-mapped in this release.
A credible set is a statistical object. Its membership does not establish causality, and its lead variant is not necessarily causal.

components.name: crispr_cell_line
components.label: CRISPR_CELL_LINE
components.description: A cell line named by a CRISPR screen, keyed by the release's SIDM id.

claims.text: A cell line used by a CRISPR screen, identified by the release's SIDM cell-line id in evidence_crispr.diseaseCellLines.
diseaseCellLines.id (SIDM). The release supplies no crosswalk to the DepMap ACH ids used by target_essentiality, so these are a separate node space from CELL_LINE.

frames.text: The name/tissue fields are source labels, not ontology keys.

limitations.text: A screen without a cell-line id emits no TESTED_IN edge.
A SIDM line is not a DepMap line; do not join the two id spaces. The screen result is an in-vitro observation.

claims.text: The cell-line name supplied by the CRISPR screen.

frames.text: A source label for display; the SIDM id is the key.

limitations.text: Null when the screen supplies no name.
Do not use the label as identity; names are not unique.

claims.text: The tissue label supplied by the CRISPR screen.

frames.text: A source label, not a biosample ontology key.

limitations.text: Null when the screen supplies no tissue label.
Tissue labels are not normalised and do not replace a biosample id.

claims.text: The tissue identifier supplied by the CRISPR screen.

frames.text: An ontology-style id where supplied; it is not a biosample id.

limitations.text: Null when the screen supplies no tissue id.
No crosswalk to BiosampleNode is supplied by the release.

claims.text: One CRISPR cell-line node per SIDM id in evidence_crispr.diseaseCellLines.
diseaseCellLines.id (SIDM).

frames.text: SIDM ids are separate from the DepMap ACH ids in CELL_LINE.

limitations.text: NULL ids are dropped; the release supplies none.
No SIDM-to-ACH crosswalk exists in 26.09; do not merge the node spaces.

components.name: cross_reference
components.label: CROSS_REFERENCE
components.description: An identifier in an external namespace, independent of the entity using it.

claims.text: An external identifier, stored once per (source, identifier) pair. It is the join surface between the release's entities and external namespaces.
(source, identifier), written source:identifier in edges.

frames.text: The source names the authority (Ensembl, UniProt, Reactome, DrugBank, ClinVar, ...), not the entity type.

limitations.text: An absent cross-reference means the release did not list it.
Two entities sharing a cross-reference are not thereby the same entity; the edge means 'has this identifier', not identity.

claims.text: Authority or namespace that issued the cross-reference identifier.

frames.text: Names the authority, such as Ensembl, UniProt, Reactome, DrugBank or ClinVar, not the entity type.

limitations.text: An absent value means the release listed no authority for the identifier.
Casing and vocabulary differ by dataset, so the source alone does not prove the external record exists.

claims.text: Accession or identifier string within the namespace named by source.

frames.text: Meaningful only together with source; identifier formats are namespace-specific.

limitations.text: An absent identifier means the release listed no accession for that authority.
Not necessarily a resolvable or unique accession, and two entities sharing it are not thereby identical.

claims.text: One CrossReferenceNode per element of disease.dbXRefs.
source:identifier, the shared cross-reference key. The 127,496 elements are 127,496 distinct pairs within a term.

frames.text: source is the text before the first colon, identifier the remainder. The same pair listed by another entity is the same node.

limitations.text: No element means the term lists no identifier. One element without a colon (EFO_0020991) is keyed with the whole sentence as source and an empty identifier.
The node records a listed identifier; it does not resolve or verify the external record. Namespace spellings are not normalized across datasets.

claims.text: One CrossReferenceNode per element of disease.obsoleteXRefs.
source:identifier, the shared cross-reference key. The 24,527 elements are 24,207 distinct pairs; 320 pairs repeat within a term.

frames.text: The same node type and key as the current cross-references, because an identifier is the same external identifier whether or not the term still uses it.

limitations.text: No element means the term lists no retired identifier.
The node does not record retirement; the edge type does. 12,183 pairs are both current and retired for the same term.

claims.text: One CrossReferenceNode per (source, identifier) listed by a molecule.
source:identifier, the shared cross-reference key stated on CrossReferenceNode. A molecule's listing contributes one node; molecules sharing the pair share the node.

frames.text: The node is the external identifier, not the molecule. The HAS_CROSS_REFERENCE edge attaches the molecule.

limitations.text: A null source or identifier cannot be keyed and is dropped; the release lists neither.

The node records a listed identifier. It does not verify the external record or assert identity between molecules that cite it. The shared key is case-sensitive and source spellings differ across datasets, so the same authority can yield two nodes (drugbank here, DrugBank on a target).

claims.text: One CrossReferenceNode per element of disease_hpo.dbXRefs.
source:identifier, the shared cross-reference key. The 43,966 elements are 43,966 distinct pairs within a term.

frames.text: source is the text before the first colon (FMA, CALOHA, MESH, GO, BTO, EMAPA, UBERON and others); identifier is the remainder. Every value carries a colon.

limitations.text: No element means the phenotype term lists no external identifier.
The shared node type means an identifier listed by a target, disease or phenotype is one node with several inbound edges. A listed identifier is not a verified external record.

claims.text: One CrossReferenceNode per element of target.dbXrefs.
source:identifier.

frames.text: Other domains may bind the same node type; the shared key space means an identifier listed by two entities is one node.

limitations.text: A null source or identifier cannot key the node and drops the row; the release carries none.
The binding only lists identifiers; it does not resolve them to external records or assert equivalence.

components.name: disease
components.label: DISEASE
components.description: A disease, phenotype, biological process or measurement in the release.

claims.text: A disease or phenotype term used by the release. The node includes EFO, MONDO, Orphanet, HPO and other ontology accessions; it is one term, not a rolled-up therapeutic area.
disease.id, the ontology accession as written in the release.

frames.text: The id space is mixed-prefix. Read ontology.isTherapeuticArea and ontology.leaf to distinguish a therapeutic area, a leaf term and an internal ontology term.

limitations.text: A term absent here is not in the release's disease vocabulary; it is not evidence that the disease does not exist.
disease.id is not a MONDO-only identifier and the same biological concept can appear under more than one accession. Do not assume a single hierarchy or a single namespace.

claims.text: Full ontology IRI of the disease term, copied from the source.

frames.text: Use for external links; the base address varies within one prefix family.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Not the join key and a weaker identity test than disease.id.

claims.text: Preferred label of the ontology term.

frames.text: Display text spanning diseases, phenotypes, measurements and non-Latin scripts.

limitations.text: Never null or empty in 26.09.
Not a join key; whitespace padding and re-labelling break exact matching.

claims.text: Free-text definition asserted by the term's owning ontology.

frames.text: Unstructured context whose voice and length vary by ontology.

limitations.text: Null when the ontology supplies no definition, not evidence that the concept is undefined.
Do not parse prose thresholds or treat it as a curated disease summary.

claims.text: Whether the term is one of the release's therapeutic-area grouping roots.

frames.text: Boolean from the ontology subset tag; true marks a grouping root, not a graph root.

limitations.text: Never null; false is a definite non-membership.
Some flagged terms are not diseases, so the flag is not a clinical-content filter.

claims.text: Leaf flag on the disease ontology record.

frames.text: Reads false on every 26.09 row because the build evaluated it before children were populated.

limitations.text: Never null; false therefore carries no information.
Do not infer a leaf from this flag; test the children or descendants edge instead.

claims.text: Source URL of the ontology term, taken from disease.ontology.sources.url.

frames.text: External address; it often equals code but may use a different base.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
It corroborates nothing beyond the source pointer and is not an independent identifier.

claims.text: Short source identifier stored in disease.ontology.sources.name.

frames.text: Despite the property name it is the term's accession, not its label.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Do not render it as a name or join on it; use disease.id for identity.

claims.text: One DiseaseNode per ontology term row in disease.
disease.id, the ontology accession as written.

frames.text: The ontology flags separate therapeutic areas, leaf terms and internal terms. The node is a term, not a union of its synonyms.

limitations.text: A term absent from disease is outside the release's vocabulary. A null name or description is a release gap, not a missing term.
The id is not guaranteed to be EFO or MONDO, and two accessions can denote the same biological concept. Resolve with the explicit ontology and cross-reference edges.

components.name: disease_synonym
components.label: DISEASE_SYNONYM
components.description: One name listed for a disease term, in one synonym class.

claims.text: A name the release lists for a disease term, qualified by the synonym class it was recorded under.
(kind, label), keyed disease_synonym::kind::label. The same string under two classes is two nodes, because the release records the classes separately.

frames.text: kind is the release's synonym class: exact, related, narrow or broad. disease.synonyms repeats the four flat arrays field for field (93,524 exact, 14,670 related, 1,909 narrow and 1,523 broad elements, with no row differing), so the struct supplies no additional nodes.

limitations.text: No node means the release lists no such name for any disease term. The synonym arrays carry no source, curator or date, so a name node cannot say who asserted the name.

A synonym is a naming fact, not an equivalence claim: an exact synonym does not merge two DISEASE nodes, a broad synonym is wider than the term and a narrow synonym is narrower. The release supplies no synonym source field, so source is unresolved for this domain.

claims.text: The synonym string as the release spells it.
Part of the node key, with kind.

frames.text: Case, punctuation and whitespace are as supplied; there is no normalization.

limitations.text: The release's four synonym arrays never carry a null element.
Two disease terms can share a label, and the same label can appear under two classes; the node is a vocabulary entry, not a disease.

claims.text: The synonym class the string was recorded under.
Part of the node key, with label.

frames.text: exact comes from exactSynonyms, related from relatedSynonyms, narrow from narrowSynonyms and broad from broadSynonyms.

limitations.text: Every synonym node names exactly one class.
The four classes are release fields, not an ontology of synonym scopes; their definitions are not restated in the dataset.

claims.text: One DiseaseSynonymNode per element of disease.broadSynonyms.
disease_synonym::broad::label, the shared (kind, label) key.

frames.text: kind is the literal 'broad' because the string came from disease.broadSynonyms. The unified disease.synonyms struct repeats this array field for field and is not bound separately, so the same string does not produce a second node.

limitations.text: No element means the release lists no broad synonym. A shared label yields one node with several inbound edges.
The node is vocabulary-level and records no source, because the release supplies no synonym source field.

claims.text: One DiseaseSynonymNode per element of disease.exactSynonyms.
disease_synonym::exact::label, the shared (kind, label) key.

frames.text: kind is the literal 'exact' because the string came from disease.exactSynonyms. The unified disease.synonyms struct repeats this array field for field and is not bound separately, so the same string does not produce a second node.

limitations.text: No element means the release lists no exact synonym. A shared label yields one node with several inbound edges.
The node is vocabulary-level and records no source, because the release supplies no synonym source field.

claims.text: One DiseaseSynonymNode per element of disease.narrowSynonyms.
disease_synonym::narrow::label, the shared (kind, label) key.

frames.text: kind is the literal 'narrow' because the string came from disease.narrowSynonyms. The unified disease.synonyms struct repeats this array field for field and is not bound separately, so the same string does not produce a second node.

limitations.text: No element means the release lists no narrow synonym. A shared label yields one node with several inbound edges.
The node is vocabulary-level and records no source, because the release supplies no synonym source field.

claims.text: One DiseaseSynonymNode per element of disease.relatedSynonyms.
disease_synonym::related::label, the shared (kind, label) key.

frames.text: kind is the literal 'related' because the string came from disease.relatedSynonyms. The unified disease.synonyms struct repeats this array field for field and is not bound separately, so the same string does not produce a second node.

limitations.text: No element means the release lists no related synonym. A shared label yields one node with several inbound edges.
The node is vocabulary-level and records no source, because the release supplies no synonym source field.

components.name: drug_warning
components.label: DRUG_WARNING
components.description: A regulatory drug warning recorded by ChEMBL.

claims.text: A drug warning row from ChEMBL: a labelled safety concern of a molecule, with its regulatory jurisdiction, warning type, year and disease context where the release supplies one.
drug_warning.id cast to text and prefixed drug_warning::. The release's id is unique across its 2,009 warning rows.

frames.text: warningType separates a black box warning from a withdrawal. efoTerm/efoId name the warning's disease context where present; a null EFO field is a release gap, not an assertion that the warning has no disease context.

limitations.text: A warning absent here is not in the release's warning set. A null country, year, toxicity class or description is a gap in the source row, not a property of the warning.

A warning is regulatory label text, not an observed adverse event, an incidence rate or a causal finding. Warnings are not deduplicated across countries or years, so the same concern can appear in several nodes.

claims.text: The release's toxicity category for the warning, for example hepatotoxicity or cardiotoxicity.

frames.text: The release's toxicity category for the warning, for example hepatotoxicity or cardiotoxicity.

limitations.text: Null for 246 rows; that is a release gap, not 'no toxicity'.
The category is a label given by the source, not a severity grade.

claims.text: The regulatory jurisdiction or jurisdictions named by the warning, sometimes a semicolon-separated list.

frames.text: Read the string as a list when it contains semicolons; it is not an ISO code.

limitations.text: A jurisdiction is not a marketing authorisation for the molecule.

claims.text: Free-text description of the warning as published.

frames.text: Free-text description of the warning as published.

limitations.text: Null for 1,024 rows; the warning still exists as a node.
The text is quoted source prose, not a normalised statement of effect.

claims.text: The warning class used by the release: 'Black Box Warning' or 'Withdrawn' in 26.09.

frames.text: The two classes are different regulatory actions; do not pool them as 'safety'.

limitations.text: A withdrawal is not the same statement as a boxed warning, and neither is an adverse event report.

claims.text: The year recorded for the warning.

frames.text: The year recorded for the warning.

limitations.text: Null for 1,028 rows; a null year is a release gap, not an undated event.
The year is the source's warning year, not the first approval or the first report.

claims.text: The disease or phenotype label the release associates with the warning.

frames.text: The disease or phenotype label the release associates with the warning.

limitations.text: Null for 1,057 rows; those warnings carry no disease context in this release.
The label is source vocabulary, not a DiseaseNode name unless efoId resolves in the release.

claims.text: The EFO accession paired with efoTerm where the release supplies one.

frames.text: It is the warning's disease context; the release does not materialise a warning-to-disease edge from it in this layer.

limitations.text: Null for 1,057 rows; a null id does not mean the warning lacks a disease context.
The accession is not guaranteed to be a DiseaseNode in 26.09; resolve it before joining.

claims.text: The EFO accession the release uses for the warning's toxicity class.

frames.text: The EFO accession the release uses for the warning's toxicity class.

limitations.text: Null for 246 rows, which are the rows with no toxicityClass.
The class accession is not the same fact as efoId, which describes the warning's disease context.

claims.text: One DrugWarningNode per row of drug_warning.
drug_warning.id cast to text and prefixed drug_warning::; the id is unique across the release's warning rows.

frames.text: The node carries the warning's own facts; the molecule relation is a separate HAS_DRUG_WARNING edge.

limitations.text: A null id cannot be keyed and the row would be dropped; no warning id is null in 26.09. Null optional fields stay null on the node.
A warning node is label text, not an observed event or a causal claim. The same concern can appear in several rows across countries and years.

components.name: drug_warning_reference
components.label: DRUG_WARNING_REFERENCE
components.description: A document cited by a drug warning, keyed by source namespace and id.

claims.text: A document or record cited by a drug warning, identified by its source namespace and the source's own identifier.
The (source, id) pair, keyed source::id. A pair always carries the same url in 26.09.

frames.text: Read warning -> reference. id is the source's identifier (PMID, DOI, document number); source is its namespace or publisher.

limitations.text: A warning whose references array is empty has no reference node or edge.
A citation is not evidence that the document supports every statement in the warning, and different sources can reuse the same identifier string.

claims.text: The identifier assigned by the citing source, for example a PMID or DOI.

frames.text: Read it together with source; the string alone has no namespace.

limitations.text: The same string can denote different records under different sources.

claims.text: The namespace or publisher of the reference, for example PubMed, WHO or DOI.

frames.text: The source qualifies referenceId; it is not the warning's country.

claims.text: The URL recorded for the reference.

frames.text: The URL recorded for the reference.

limitations.text: A locator is not a guarantee that the resource is reachable or supports the warning.

claims.text: One DrugWarningReferenceNode per (source, id) cited by a warning.
references.source::references.id. A reference cited by several warnings is emitted once per citation and collapses on this key.

frames.text: The url is the same for a given (source, id) pair in 26.09, so it is a node property rather than a qualifier of each citation.

limitations.text: A warning with no references produces no reference row. A null id, source or url cannot be keyed and is dropped; the release has none.
The node is a citation target, not proof that the document supports the warning.

components.name: entity
components.label: entity
components.description: A thing the release identifies and a consumer can ask about.

claims.text: An entity with its own identity in the release: a target, disease, molecule, variant, study, credible set or another identified record.
The concrete node's own release identifier.

frames.text: Read the concrete node for its properties and limits.

limitations.text: No node means the release does not identify the entity in this build.
An edge between two entities records the relation the concrete edge declares; it does not make the entities interchangeable.

components.name: evidence
components.label: evidence
components.description:
One source row asserting a target-disease relationship.

The common properties are the release's uniform evidence envelope.  They are
declared once here so every source node carries the same provenance fields;
a source that lacks a field carries null on that node, not a missing property.

claims.text: One row of a target-disease evidence dataset, kept as a node so its target, disease and provenance can be traversed. The node is the source's assertion, not an aggregate target-disease score.
The dataset's own id field. Every evidence id in 26.09 is a build-assigned hash, unique within the released table but not a provider accession and not stable across releases.

frames.text: Every source node has one HAS_TARGET and one HAS_DISEASE edge. Source-specific provenance edges are HAS_VARIANT, FROM_STUDY, SUPPORTED_BY, TESTED_IN, FROM_MODEL, HAS_MODEL_PHENOTYPE, HAS_HUMAN_PHENOTYPE, HAS_MOLECULE and IN_PATHWAY.

limitations.text: A missing source row is absent evidence, not a tested negative. A null provenance field means the source did not supply it.
An evidence node is not the aggregate association between its target and disease; the aggregate layer is separate and is not linked back to individual rows by the release.

properties.name: id
properties.description: The source row's id.

claims.text: The source row's id.

frames.text: The value is a build-assigned SHA-1 content hash in all twenty sources, not a ClinVar, ClinGen, COSMIC or UniProt accession. It is unique within the released table, so it is the node key.

limitations.text: Do not carry the id across releases: a changed input mints a new hash. The hash covers the row's identity fields, not its free text or score, unless the source's own definition says otherwise.

properties.name: datasourceId
properties.description: The release's datasource code for the evidence row.

claims.text: The release's datasource code for the evidence row.

frames.text: The value is constant within each source table and names the source, not the assay.

limitations.text: The code is a reporting label; it does not encode the evidence method.

properties.name: datatypeId

components.label: EVIDENCE_CLINGEN
components.description: A ClinGen gene-disease validity curation.

claims.text: One ClinGen Gene-Disease Validity curation of a gene-disease pair, with the expert panel's classification.
evidence_clingen.id; 4,031 rows and 4,031 distinct ids, none null. SHA-1 over gene id, symbol, disease id, datasource, curated label, panel and mode.

evidence_orphanet.id; 6,771 rows and 6,771 distinct ids, none null. SHA-1 over the two gene ids, the two disease ids and datasourceId; no internal structure.

frames.text: confidence is Assessed (6,760) or Not yet assessed (11). directionOnTrait is risk on every row; directionOnTarget is LoF (1,229), GoF (204) or null (5,338).

limitations.text: publicationDate is null on 554 rows. There is no variantId column, so this source contributes no HAS_VARIANT edge.
alleleOrigins is free text and variantFunctionalConsequenceId is a property. The row is a curated gene-disease assertion, not a patient observation.

frames.text: The value is constant within a source table and groups sources into broad buckets such as genetic_association, affected_pathway or literature. It is not a measurement type or a controlled assay vocabulary.

properties.name: score

properties.name: resourceScore

claims.text: A Gene Ontology term: a biological process, molecular function or cellular component. The term is the ontology unit, not an annotation of one gene. Retired classes keep a row.

frames.text: namespace separates the three branches. altIds are retired accessions recorded on the current term, not separate terms. isObsolete marks the 10,248 rows GO retired, which the release keeps for historical annotations.

A GO annotation is an edge from a target with its own evidence, aspect and qualifier; the term alone does not say a gene is annotated with it. A retired term is a class GO no longer curates, not a synonym of its replacement.

claims.text: The term name as GO publishes it, including the 'obsolete ' prefix.

frames.text: Display, not identity: 48,318 distinct labels cover 48,340 rows, and each of the 22 repeated labels belongs to two retired terms.

claims.text: The GO branch the term belongs to.

frames.text: Exactly three lowercase values: biological_process (30,885 terms), molecular_function (12,855) and cellular_component (4,600), with no nulls and no fourth value.

limitations.text: The branch is an ontology branch, not an identifier prefix or a resolver namespace. It is not preserved across all relations: 786 of 7,058 part-of edges join terms from different branches, so filtering a walk by namespace cuts real part-of links.

claims.text: True when GO retired the class; the release keeps the row.

frames.text: True on 10,248 of 48,340 rows: 6,911 biological_process, 2,814 molecular_function and 523 cellular_component terms. Every retired row has empty isA, partOf, regulation, ancestor and descendant arrays.

claims.text: One hallmark annotation of a target. The release stores two kinds: attribute records, a categorised free-text observation with a PubMed reference, and cancerHallmark records, an assignment to one of the release's cancer-hallmark labels with an impact word.

The node key: hallmark::kind::category::pmid::description for an attribute record, with ::impact inserted before the description for a cancerHallmark record. One target can carry several statements for the same hallmark category under different publications.

frames.text: kind separates the two record shapes. category is the attribute name (for example function summary) or the cancer-hallmark label. impact is set only for cancerHallmark records.

limitations.text: A target with no hallmark edge has no hallmark annotation in the release. An empty hallmark struct and a missing one are equivalent here.
Attribute text is free prose and is not normalized or scored. A cancer-hallmark label is a curator's interpretation; impact is a direction word, not a measured effect size.

components.name: interaction
components.label: INTERACTION
components.description: One aggregated molecular interaction between two participants.

claims.text: An aggregated molecular interaction as the release's interaction dataset reports it: two participants, the species each was observed in, the contributing database and the evidence count. It is a pair-level record, not a single experiment.

interaction.interactionId, an opaque signed 64-bit hash rendered as text; 14,612,199 rows and 14,612,199 distinct ids, so the release key is unique. It is not derived from the participants: 13,578,595 distinct (targetA, targetB) pairs cover the 14.6M rows, and 340,613 rows share even (targetA, targetB, sourceDatabase) with another row.

frames.text: count is the number of interaction_evidence rows behind the pair: it agrees with the evidence count on all 14,612,199 interactions. scoring is the maximum evidence interactionScore on 14,516,323 rows and null on 95,875, which are the reactome and signor rows that carry no score. sourceDatabase names the contributing database; speciesA and speciesB are the participants' species, and the participants themselves are the HAS_PARTICIPANT_A and HAS_PARTICIPANT_B edges.

limitations.text: No node means the release has no aggregated interaction for that pair. A null scoring means the source database does not score interactions, not a score of zero.

A node per interaction is 14.6M nodes plus about 29M participant edges: the interaction cannot be a bare target-target edge because one pair can carry several ids and because a two-sided record needs a place for both roles and both species. 'string' is the literal sourceDatabase on 13,205,373 rows, an upstream placeholder rather than a database name. interaction_evidence is materialised only where the release identifies a row: INTERACTION_EVIDENCE nodes and HAS_EVIDENCE edges cover the 2,447,776 rows that carry an interactionIdentifier, while 24,948,510 rows (91%) carry none and stay in the source. This node already states the full evidence count and a near-maximum evidence score (the max matches on 14,516,323 of 14,612,199 interactions), so the evidence layer adds detection method, host organism and citation for the identified subset only. Physical interaction is not functional modulation, pathway membership or a target-disease assertion.
An INTERACTION node aggregates evidence rows for one participant pair from one database.
