components.name: pgx_annotation
components.label: PGX_ANNOTATION
components.description: One ClinPGx clinical annotation as the release publishes it.

claims.text: One pharmacogenomic clinical annotation: a statement that a genotype or haplotype changes a drug's behaviour for one gene, curated under one phenotype category and graded by ClinPGx. It is the release's pharmacogenomics row, not a study, a variant or a drug label.

studyId|genotype|variantId|variantFunctionalConsequenceId|targetFromSourceId|pgxCategory|phenotypeText|phenotypeFromSourceId|drug set: 33,479 nodes for 33,479 rows. studyId alone is not the key: it is the ClinPGx clinical-annotation accession with 5,190 distinct values and up to 270 rows each, because one annotation fans out over genotypes, phenotypes and drugs. All nine parts are needed: dropping studyId leaves 32,551 distinct keys, phenotypeText 29,503, the drug set 26,558, targetFromSourceId 24,997, genotype 23,929, pgxCategory 32,495, variantId 33,366, variantFunctionalConsequenceId 33,473 and phenotypeFromSourceId 33,471. The drug set is the sorted drugId|drugFromSource pairs of the row. genotypeId, variantRsId and haplotypeId do not discriminate further and stay properties.
The node is keyed by the annotation's subject plus its fan-out axes.

frames.text: pgxCategory is the curated role of the phenotype (toxicity, efficacy, metabolism/pk, dosage, other, pd). directionality is the allele-function label of the genotype, not the direction of the drug response. evidenceLevel grades the whole annotation on ClinPGx's scale, 1A highest and 4 meaning the evidence does not support the association. phenotypeText is the drug-response phrase, and phenotypeFromSourceId is the disease accession the release mapped it to. isDirectTarget is build-computed: true when the gene is a mechanism-of-action target of a drug in the row. variantId is derived by the build from genotypeId, not supplied by ClinPGx.

limitations.text: Nulls are source gaps with different causes: phenotypeFromSourceId is null on 32,755 rows (the label lookup matched nothing, although phenotypeText is still present on 31,625 of them), variantId on 17,310 (the 9,548 haplotype-anchored rows plus 7,762 rsID-anchored genotypes that reduce to the reference), variantRsId on 9,548, variantFunctionalConsequenceId on 11,117, directionality on 26,453, targetFromSourceId on 1,569, haplotypeId on 23,931 and phenotypeText on 1,130.

studyId is ClinPGx's annotation accession and joins to no row of the release's study dataset (0 of the 5,190 values occur there): the shared name is a collision. genotypeId is a genotype spelling (chr_pos_ref_allele1,allele2), not a variant id, and one genotype can name two variants. variantAnnotation (47,749 elements, 1-80 per row, 10,288 distinct ids) stays in the source: it holds the per-publication variant statements and is not a graph relation here. genotypeAnnotationText is ClinPGx's sentence for the genotype; phenotypeText is the release's phrase cut from it on 29,818 of the 32,349 non-null rows and different from it on 2,531, so it is neither always the source sentence nor a ClinPGx term, and never a controlled vocabulary. An annotation grades evidence; it is not a prescription, a dose recommendation or a clinical guideline.
The number of PGX_ANNOTATION nodes is the number of ClinPGx clinical annotations, or of variant annotations.
evidenceLevel is ClinPGx's grade of the annotation.
A level-1A annotation is a clinical guideline recommendation, or a level-3 annotation is an unscored record.
phenotypeFromSourceId is a sparse mapped disease term.
A null phenotypeFromSourceId means the annotation states no drug-response phenotype.

claims.text: ClinPGx's clinical-annotation accession, as a decimal string.

frames.text: 5,190 distinct values over 33,479 rows; the largest annotation (1184757183, CYP2D6 and bufuralol) has 270 rows.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Not the release's study: none of the 5,190 values occurs in study.studyId, and it is not unique per row.

claims.text: The data provider that supplied the annotation.

frames.text: The constant 'clinpgx' on every row.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
One value means the property cannot partition the annotations; the release integrates no other pharmacogenomics source in 26.09.

claims.text: The ClinPGx dump date the annotations were taken from.

frames.text: The constant '2026-07-05' on every row, an ISO date.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
It dates the ClinPGx feed, not the Open Targets release (published 2026-09-18) and not the release's own files.

claims.text: The record-type stamp of the pharmacogenomics file.

frames.text: The constant 'clinical_annotation' on every row.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
It is not a member of the association datasets' datatype vocabulary, so it must not be unioned with their values.

claims.text: The allele-function label ClinPGx gives the annotated genotype or haplotype: how it changes the gene product.

frames.text: Ten values in three schemes: function terms (No function 3,111, Decreased function 1,420, Normal function 1,226, Uncertain function 773, Increased function 343, Unknown function 6), a copy-state 'Presence' (112) and class pairs (IV/Normal 20, III/Deficient 10, II/Deficient 5). Null on 26,453 rows.

limitations.text: Null means ClinPGx left the cell blank, not that function is unchanged: 'No function' and 'Normal function' are separate populated values.
It describes the allele, not the drug response; the three schemes are not ordered, so the values must not be sorted by severity.

claims.text: ClinPGx's evidence grade for the annotation as a whole.

frames.text: Six codes: 1A (4,992 rows), 1B (353), 2A (510), 2B (131), 3 (25,871) and 4 (1,622). The order 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B, 3, 4 is ClinPGx's, not alphabetic.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.

3 is the modal low-evidence bucket and 4 means the evidence does not support the association, so a high code is not a missing score. The grade is not a strength estimate and does not transfer between drugs.

claims.text: The genotype or allele as ClinPGx writes it.

frames.text: 418 distinct labels over 33,479 rows: star-allele diplotypes such as *1/*1, single alleles such as *48, repeat counts, and the literal 'null/null' for deletion alleles on 38 rows.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
A label, not a key: '*1/*1' occurs for many genes. It is part of the annotation's identity because it separates rows that share every other field.

claims.text: The VCF-style genotype spelling chr_pos_reference_allele1,allele2 that the release records for the row.

frames.text: 8,568 distinct values, null on 9,634 rows: all 9,548 haplotype-anchored rows plus 86 rsID-anchored rows without coordinates. Example: 10_119371801_A_A,G.

limitations.text: Null is a row with no coordinates to write down (the haplotype-anchored branch), not a genotype whose annotation failed to resolve.
A genotype is not a variant: it holds both alleles, and variantId is the build's reduction of it. Never join genotypeId to variant.variantId.

claims.text: ClinPGx's full sentence explaining the genotype's clinical significance.

frames.text: Repeats across every row one annotation fans out to, so it is not unique. 29,818 of the 32,349 non-null phenotypeText values are substrings of it.

limitations.text: Null on 1,130 rows.
Prose, not a term: do not group by it and do not parse dosages from it. It is the source sentence behind phenotypeText, not a second phenotype.

claims.text: The allele or diplotype name ClinPGx uses for the row's subject.

frames.text: 593 distinct values such as CYP2C19*17 and CYP1A1*1/*1; null on 23,931 rows, exactly the rows that name a variant by rsID instead.

limitations.text: Null marks the rsID-anchored branch, not an annotation without a subject.
A name, not an accession, and it can be a pair of alleles; there is no haplotype table in the release to resolve it against.

claims.text: ClinPGx's own haplotype accession, PA followed by 8 or 9 digits.

frames.text: 422 distinct PA accessions on 8,248 rows; null on 25,231 rows, which include the rsID-anchored rows and haplotypes ClinPGx left without an accession.

limitations.text: Null is a missing ClinPGx accession, not a missing haplotype name.
It is not a release identifier and joins to no table in this release; the node keeps it as the source's accession only.

claims.text: ClinPGx's curated role of the annotated phenotype in drug response.

frames.text: Six lower-case codes: toxicity (11,846 rows), efficacy (10,948), metabolism/pk (7,401), other (1,823), dosage (1,442) and pd (19).

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
An annotation with several categories contributes one row per category, so rows count categories, not annotations. 'pd' (pharmacodynamic) holds 19 rows, too few to stratify on.

claims.text: The drug-response phrase the release publishes for the annotation.

frames.text: 5,037 distinct strings over 32,349 non-null rows, for example 'decreased clearance of bufuralol'. 29,818 are literal substrings of the row's genotypeAnnotationText; the other 2,531 are not, so the wording is not always a verbatim excerpt.

limitations.text: Null on 1,130 rows means the extraction returned nothing, not a genotype with no response.
Extracted prose, not a controlled term: different strings state one phenotype, so do not group on it. It is not ClinPGx's own phenotype wording and no ontology term is attached to it directly.

claims.text: The release's disease accession for the row's phenotype phrase.

frames.text: 30 accessions over 724 rows, mixing MONDO, EFO, GO, HP and NCIT; MONDO_0018493 alone covers 581 rows. All 30 resolve to disease.id.

limitations.text: Null on 32,755 rows (97.8%) means the phrase matched no disease label; the phenotype text is still present on 31,625 of those rows.
The mapping is sparse and many-to-one, so it is not a substitute for phenotypeText and does not make the annotation a disease association.

claims.text: The dbSNP rsID ClinPGx names for the variant.

frames.text: 2,843 distinct rs-prefixed values, null on 9,548 rows; 2,829 of the distinct values occur in variant.rsIds and 14 do not.

limitations.text: Null marks the haplotype-anchored branch, not a variant without an rsID.
It is not a key: nothing in the release is keyed by rsID and 14 values resolve to no variant row. The variant edge uses variantId, not this.

claims.text: The release's variant key for the row, derived by the build from genotypeId by splitting the two alleles and dropping any equal to the reference.

frames.text: 16,169 non-null rows over 2,882 distinct chromosome_position_ref_alt values; all 2,882 resolve to variant.variantId. Example: 10_119371801_A_G from genotypeId 10_119371801_A_A,G.

limitations.text: Null on 17,310 rows for two reasons: the 9,548 haplotype-anchored rows have no genotypeId coordinates (genotypeId is null on all of them), and 7,762 rsID-anchored genotypes reduce to the reference and leave no alternate allele.
Derived, not supplied: a row holds one allele and one genotype can yield two variants, so the row's variant is not necessarily the subject the annotation was curated about.

claims.text: The Ensembl gene id of the pharmacogene the annotation is about.

frames.text: 1,152 distinct ENSG values on 31,910 rows; 1,101 resolve to target.id and 51 do not (6,615 rows). The column is already an Ensembl id, not a symbol or UniProt accession.

limitations.text: Null on 1,569 rows means upstream gene resolution returned nothing.
The 51 unresolved genes are the release's own resolution gap, so the target edge dangles for those rows rather than inventing a target.

claims.text: The Sequence Ontology accession of the variant's consequence in the row's gene context, in the release's underscore spelling SO_0001583.

frames.text: 21 distinct accessions on 22,362 rows; SO_0002073 (no sequence alteration) is the commonest with 7,191, ahead of intron (5,374) and missense (5,046).

limitations.text: Null on 11,117 rows: every haplotype-anchored row plus rsID-anchored rows with no consequence term.
The term describes the variant read in the row's gene, not the variant alone, and it is not joined to a SO term node by this layer.

claims.text: Whether the row's gene is a mechanism-of-action target of a drug in the row; computed by the build, not curated by ClinPGx.

frames.text: True on 1,612 rows and false on 31,867; no nulls.

limitations.text: Never null. False is not evidence of absence: an unmapped drug id, a null gene id or a drug with no mechanism row also give false.

The test runs per drug inside the row's array, so a multi-drug row where only one drug matches splits into two rows. It says nothing about whether the drug acts through the gene in the annotated phenotype.

claims.text: One PgxAnnotationNode per row of pharmacogenomics.

studyId|genotype|variantId|variantFunctionalConsequenceId|targetFromSourceId|pgxCategory|phenotypeText|phenotypeFromSourceId|drug set: 33,479 keys for 33,479 rows. The drug set is the sorted drugId|drugFromSource pairs, with the empty string for a null component. Every part is needed: dropping studyId leaves 32,551 distinct keys, phenotypeText 29,503, the drug set 26,558, targetFromSourceId 24,997, genotype 23,929, pgxCategory 32,495, variantId 33,366, variantFunctionalConsequenceId 33,473 and phenotypeFromSourceId 33,471.

frames.text: The node carries the annotation's scalars. The variant, gene, drugs, mapped phenotype and citations are edges; studyId is ClinPGx's annotation accession, not a study.

limitations.text: A row with a null studyId, genotype, pgxCategory or drugs array cannot be keyed and is dropped; the release carries none. Null nullable parts key as the empty string and stay null properties.

The key mixes text (genotype, phenotypeText) and a derived drug set, so a re-wording in a later release is a new node. genotypeId, variantRsId and haplotypeId do not discriminate and are properties only.

components.name: phenotype
components.label: PHENOTYPE
components.description: A phenotype term (HPO or MP).

claims.text: A phenotype or ontology term used by the release's disease-phenotype and mouse-phenotype records. The vocabulary is mixed: disease_hpo contains HP, UBERON, GO, CHEBI, CL, PATO, PR, MPATH and other accessions, and mouse records use MP terms.
The ontology accession, prefixed phenotype:: in keys. Different vocabularies must not be merged even when accessions collide.

frames.text: The label is the term's preferred name; the accession is the key. A disease-phenotype relation and a mouse-phenotype relation are different edges.

limitations.text: A term absent here is outside the release's phenotype subset.
A phenotype annotation is an association, not a diagnosis. A mouse phenotype mapped to a human term is a model inference.

claims.text: Preferred label of the phenotype term in its source ontology.

frames.text: HPO or MP label; casing follows the source vocabulary.

limitations.text: Never null or empty in both source datasets.
The same label need not denote the same term across HP and MP; join on the accession.

claims.text: One PhenotypeNode per distinct modelPhenotypeClasses element, so the 28 MP class terms exist as terms.
modelPhenotypeClasses.id: 28 distinct MP accessions. 21 are also bound from modelPhenotypeId with the same label and collapse; 7 occur only here.

frames.text: The class ids are MP accessions in colon form (MP:0001186 pigmentation phenotype, MP:0005367 renal/urinary system phenotype) and the labels agree with the observation labels where both occur.

limitations.text: A null class id cannot key the node; none occur.
The class terms are broader than the observed phenotypes and have no published MP parent edges in this release, so their only relation is HAS_PHENOTYPE_CLASS from the model.

claims.text: One PhenotypeNode per MP term named by mouse_phenotype.
phenotype::MP:<accession>; 203,583 rows and 10,584 distinct MP accessions. The prefix matches the disease_hpo phenotype key convention and keeps the key disjoint from DISEASE.

frames.text: The MP accession is used as written (colon form). 10,368 of the 10,373 MP accessions cited by evidence_impc are present here.

limitations.text: A term absent here is outside the mouse_phenotype file; five evidence_impc MP accessions have no node.
An MP term is a mouse phenotype vocabulary term, not an HPO term. The two vocabularies are not merged.

claims.text: One PhenotypeNode per row of disease_hpo.

phenotype::accession. The prefix keeps the key disjoint from DISEASE: 2,399 of these accessions (2,183 HP, 213 GO, 2 PATO, 1 UBERON) are also disease.id values, and a raw accession would silently resolve an edge to the DISEASE node of the same string.

frames.text: 32,082 rows carry 32,082 distinct ids, of which 19,836 are HP terms; the rest are the imported terms the phenotype hierarchy relies on (UBERON 5,641, GO 2,443, CHEBI 1,927, CL 1,187, PATO 571, PR 321, MPATH 75, NBO 64, HsapDv 16, RO 1).

limitations.text: A term absent here is outside the release's phenotype hierarchy. A null description (3,451 rows) is a vocabulary gap, not a missing term; disease_hpo.description is not carried because PhenotypeNode declares no description property in this build.

The node set is a phenotype hierarchy, not an HPO-only list: a non-HP accession is a term the hierarchy imports, not a phenotype annotation. The node key prefix is a build convention; the identity is the accession.

components.name: prioritisation_profile
components.label: PRIORITISATION_PROFILE
components.description: The Target Engine's per-target prioritisation feature vector.

claims.text: One target's prioritisation profile: the Target Engine's computed feature vector over tractability, safety, constraint, homology, clinical stage, chemical probes and expression specificity. It is a derived summary of the target, not an independent entity.
target_prioritisation.targetId: 78,733 rows and 78,733 distinct ids, exactly one profile per target in the release, all resolving to a TargetNode.

frames.text: The attributes sit on a node rather than on the edge because the row identifies only the target: an edge carrying them would need a second endpoint and would degenerate to a target self-loop the release does not state. The node gives the attribute bag an address, is total over the 78,733 targets, and keeps 17 computed columns out of TARGET; it carries no fact that is independent of its target.

limitations.text: No node means the release computed no profile for that target; none occur in 26.09, where the profile covers all 78,733 targets. A null attribute is the feature not being computed, not a negative value.

There is no evidence trail: the profile is the release's computed roll-up, and its inputs are the tractability, safety, essentiality, probe and baseline-expression datasets, which are separate graph layers. Values must not be treated as independent facts about the target, and the negative sentinels (-1) are not measurements; see each property. 59,710 targets have no isInMembrane or isSecreted value and 77,779 have no hasSafetyEvent value.
A prioritisation profile is the Target Engine's derived vector for one target.
The profile is an independent assessment, evidence, or a ranking produced by this graph.

claims.text: The release's membrane-localisation flag for the target.

frames.text: 1 on 4,195 profiles, 0 on 14,828 and null on 59,710.

limitations.text: Null means the release did not assess localisation, not that the target is not membrane-bound.
An integer flag, not a boolean: null is unassessed and must not be coerced to false. It summarises localisation evidence and is not a measured topology.

claims.text: The release's secreted-protein flag for the target.

frames.text: 1 on 1,991 profiles, 0 on 17,032 and null on 59,710.

limitations.text: Null means the release did not assess secretion, not that the target is intracellular.
An integer flag with an unassessed state; not a measured secretion assay.

claims.text: Whether the target has at least one target_safety_event row. The column is encoded as -1 and never as 1 or 0.

frames.text: Exactly 954 profiles carry -1 and 77,779 are null; those 954 are exactly the 954 targets with a target_safety_event row, so -1 is the release's true.

limitations.text: Null means the target has no safety event in the release, not that it was assessed and cleared.
Read -1 as present, not as a missing-value code or a negative assessment. The flag hides event identity, direction, dosing and source, which are on the HAS_SAFETY_EVENT edges.

claims.text: Whether the target has a high-quality small-molecule pocket in the tractability assessment.

frames.text: 1 on 982 profiles, 0 on 17,887 and null on 59,864; it reproduces the tractability bucket SM/High-Quality Pocket exactly.

limitations.text: Null means no tractability assessment, not the absence of a pocket.
A summary of one tractability bucket, not structural evidence; the bucket value stays on the HAS_TRACTABILITY edge.

claims.text: Whether the target has a high-quality small-molecule ligand in the tractability assessment.

frames.text: 1 on 2,352 profiles, 0 on 16,517 and null on 59,864; it reproduces the tractability bucket SM/High-Quality Ligand exactly.

limitations.text: Null means no tractability assessment, not the absence of a ligand.
A roll-up of one bucket, not a measured binding affinity.

claims.text: Whether the target has a small-molecule binder in the tractability assessment.

frames.text: 1 on 3,047 profiles, 0 on 15,822 and null on 59,864; it reproduces the tractability bucket PR/Small Molecule Binder exactly.

limitations.text: Null means no tractability assessment, not the absence of a binder.
A roll-up of one bucket; it does not say the binder is potent, selective or safe.

claims.text: The release's signed genetic-constraint score for the target.

frames.text: Continuous in [-1, 1]; 18,245 distinct values, 9,121 negative, null on 60,488 profiles.

limitations.text: Null means no constraint metric, not an unconstrained gene.

The release does not state which constraint family (mis, lof, syn) or which signed statistic it summarises; the per-family metrics are on the HAS_CONSTRAINT edges. The single -1.0 value cannot be told apart from a real extreme score.

claims.text: The release's maximum identity among the target's paralogues. The field is described as a percentage but is stored as a sign-flipped fraction.

frames.text: Negative fractions in [-1, 0]: -0.997265 means 99.7% identity, 0.0 means no identity and -1.0 occurs on 676 profiles. Null on 57,861.

limitations.text: Null means no homolog data, not the absence of a paralogue.

The sign and scale are release artefacts: the stored values are negative fractions, not the 0-100 percentage the field description names, and they do not reproduce homology.queryPercentageIdentity (median gap 31.5 percentage points over 20,872 targets). The meaning of -1.0 is unresolved.

claims.text: The release's maximum identity between the target and its mouse orthologue, stored as a positive fraction rather than the percentage its description names.

frames.text: Continuous in [0, 1], 0.0 on 7,018 profiles, null on 59,481.

limitations.text: Null means no mouse orthologue was assessed; 0.0 is a measured zero.

The opposite sign convention to paralogMaxIdentityPercentage in the same row, and also not the percentage its description names. It does not reproduce homology identity (mean gap 47 percentage points), so it is a Target Engine input, not a homology value.

claims.text: Whether the target is a cancer driver gene. The column is encoded as -1 and never as 1 or 0.

frames.text: Exactly 336 profiles carry -1 and 78,397 are null. 332 of the 336 are targets in evidence_cancer_gene_census; 4 are not, so the flag also has an input outside that dataset.

limitations.text: Null means the release does not call the target a cancer driver gene; it is not an assessed negative.
Read -1 as present. The flag collapses the census's driver role, direction and tumour types, which are on the evidence layer.

claims.text: The release's mouse knockout score for the target.

frames.text: Continuous in [-0.994, 0], 9,224 negative, null on 66,864 profiles; 0.0 is the maximum.

limitations.text: Null means no knockout data was scored, not a score of zero.
The release does not state the sign convention or the phenotype scale, so a more negative value cannot be read as stronger evidence from this column alone.

claims.text: Whether the target has at least one high-quality chemical probe.

frames.text: 1 on 516 profiles, 0 on 160 and null on 78,057; it reproduces chemical_probe.isHighQuality on exactly 516 targets.

limitations.text: Null means no probe record, not that no high-quality probe exists.
A presence flag; probe identity, scores and origin stay on the HAS_CHEMICAL_PROBE edges.

claims.text: The release's score derived from the highest clinical stage any molecule against the target has reached.

frames.text: Ordinal fractions 0.01, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.5, 0.7 and 1.0 on 1,552 profiles and null on 77,181. 1.0 covers 1,075 profiles.

limitations.text: Null means no clinical assessment for the target, not stage zero.

The release describes it as a score derived from the highest stage reached for any indication, not as a stage: it publishes no labels behind the fractions, and they are not probabilities. It is a target-level roll-up across molecules, not an approval for an indication.

claims.text: The Target Engine's tissue-specificity score for the target.

frames.text: Continuous in [-0.907, 1.0], 15,409 negative, null on 22,970 profiles.

limitations.text: Null means no expression-based score, not that the target is broadly expressed.
A Target Engine roll-up over expression sources; it is not the per-context baseline_expression specificity_score and the two are not on a common scale.

claims.text: The Target Engine's tissue-distribution score for the target.

frames.text: 119 distinct values: fractions in (0, 1] plus -1.0 on 10,010 profiles, null on 22,970.

limitations.text: Null means no expression-based score, not zero distribution.
The release does not state what -1.0 encodes; it is not a fraction and must not be averaged with the positive values.

claims.text: The Target Engine's cell-type-specificity score for the target.

frames.text: Continuous in [-0.920, 1.0], 13,696 negative, null on 35,623 profiles.

limitations.text: Null means no cell-type expression score, not that the target is ubiquitous.
A Target Engine roll-up, not the per-context baseline_expression specificity_score and not comparable with it.

claims.text: The Target Engine's cell-type-distribution score for the target.

frames.text: 171 distinct values: fractions in (0, 1] plus -1.0 on 957 profiles, null on 35,623.

limitations.text: Null means no cell-type expression score, not zero distribution.
The release does not state what -1.0 encodes; it is not a fraction and must not be averaged with the positive values.

claims.text: One PrioritisationProfileNode per row of target_prioritisation, keyed by the target.
target_prioritisation.targetId: 78,733 rows and 78,733 distinct ids, all resolving to a TargetNode, so the node is 1:1 with the target universe.

frames.text: The integer flags are stored as integers, not booleans, because null is an unassessed state and because hasSafetyEvent and isCancerDriverGene encode true as -1 and never as 1. Null is the feature not being computed; -1 is a measured present for those two columns and a sentinel of unknown meaning on the distribution columns.

limitations.text: A null targetId cannot key the node; none occur. A missing profile would mean the target was not prioritised; none occur in 26.09.

The binding copies the release's encodings without converting them, so the reader must apply the per-property rules; no value is rescaled or re-signed. It does not join the profile back to tractability, safety, probe or expression rows.
The profile keys on the target, so it adds no entity the target does not already have.
The profile node can be used as an independent assessment, or that two profiles can be compared across releases.

components.name: protein
components.label: PROTEIN
components.description: A protein identifier that the target gene maps to.

claims.text: A protein-record identifier listed for a target: a current UniProt accession, a retired UniProt accession, or an Ensembl protein id. It names a protein record, not the gene that encodes it.
(source, identifier), written source:identifier. One node per identifier in the namespace named by source.

frames.text: source separates current UniProt entries from retired ones and from Ensembl protein ids. identifier is the accession as the release spells it; the same string under two sources is two identifiers.

limitations.text: A target with no protein edge is a gene for which the release lists no protein identifier; it is not evidence that the gene encodes no protein.
A protein identifier is not a structure, an isoform function or proof of expression. One gene can map to several protein identifiers, and a retired accession does not resolve to a current entry.

claims.text: The namespace that issued the protein identifier.
One component of the node key (source, identifier).

frames.text: Observed values are ensembl_PRO, uniprot_swissprot, uniprot_trembl and uniprot_obsolete.

limitations.text: The release's proteinIds array never carries a null source.
The value is a namespace label, not a database version or release date.

claims.text: The protein accession in the namespace named by source.
One component of the node key (source, identifier).

frames.text: Use together with source; an accession alone does not name a record.

limitations.text: The release's proteinIds array never carries a null identifier.
Retired UniProt accessions are kept under uniprot_obsolete and do not resolve to a current UniProt entry.

claims.text: One ProteinNode per element of target.proteinIds.
source:identifier, the node key.

frames.text: The same accession listed for several targets yields one node with several inbound edges.

limitations.text: A null source or identifier cannot key the node and drops the row; the release carries none.
The binding does not check that the accession is current and does not create an edge to a transcript.

components.name: publication
components.label: PUBLICATION
components.description: A literature entry identified by its PubMed identifier.

claims.text: A literature entry the release cites, identified by the release's literature key. The same entry is one node regardless of how many studies or evidence rows cite it.
The release literature key, normally a PubMed id but also PPR, PMC, IND, CAIN, ADL, FNI and other Europe PMC keys. A PMCID is a cross-reference and can be absent.

frames.text: Most keys are PubMed ids; 899,451 of 21,938,364 are not. The key is the release's spelling, not a promise that a PubMed record exists.

limitations.text: An evidence row with no PMID has no publication node; it is not a publication with an empty title.
A publication node records that the release cites the paper. It does not mean the paper's claims were verified by this graph.

claims.text: PubMed Central identifier of the publication where a PMC deposit exists.

frames.text: PMC-prefixed text used as a cross-reference, not as the node key.

limitations.text: Null when the paper has no PMC deposit, so no full text was mined.
Absence is not a missing publication record; the PMID remains the identity.

claims.text: One PublicationNode per literature entry in literature_entity_lut.

literature_entity_lut.pmid. The table's grain is (pmid, keywordId), so the binding emits one record per grounded mention, 173,137,629 of them, and the build's exact-duplicate collapse leaves one record per identifier: 21,938,364 distinct keys, one record per key. The source's date/year are not node properties because one key carries two dates; publication dates remain on study and evidence records.

frames.text: pmid is the release's literature key, not always a PubMed id: 899,451 of the 21,938,364 keys are not PubMed numbers, 895,626 prefixed PPR, PMC, IND, CAIN, ADL, FNI or c (preprints and Europe PMC records) and 3,825 sixteen-digit numbers above the PubMed range. Numeric keys top out at 42,701,903. 5,740,182 identifiers carry a pmcid and 16,198,182 do not; date and year are null on 16 rows.

limitations.text: pmid is never null in 26.09, so no placeholder identity is minted. A paper absent here is outside the release's text-mined corpus; that is not a claim that the paper does not exist.

The node set is the corpus the release mined for entities, not every publication the release cites: the 174 study PMIDs outside it keep no node although PUBLISHED_AS still names them. Month and day are not carried because the release's day is an upstream placeholder on most rows. literature_vector is a word-embedding table keyed by word and category, with no entity identifier, so it is not a graph relation and no node or edge binds it.

components.name: regulatory_element
components.label: REGULATORY_ELEMENT
components.description: One ENCODE E2G prediction linking a regulatory interval to a gene.

claims.text: A regulatory interval as the release's E2G model reports it for one biosample and one study, with the gene it is predicted to regulate. It is a prediction record, not a validated enhancer or promoter.

enhancer_to_gene.intervalId, a 32-hex-character hash: 48,808,491 rows carry 48,806,245 distinct ids, and the 2,246 repeated ids are exact duplicate rows. The id is not a genomic-interval id: 38,343,584 distinct (chromosome, start, end, biosampleId) intervals exist, and one interval linked to one gene recurs once per study (up to 255 times for one such interval). Read the node as the release's element-gene-study record.

frames.text: chromosome, start and end are GRCh38 coordinates in the release's own spelling (no chr prefix). intervalType is the model's classification of the interval: promoter (24,407,590 rows), genic (13,257,251) or intergenic (11,143,650). score is the E2G link score; distanceToTss is a non-negative distance to the gene's TSS, zero for every promoter row. The gene is the REGULATES edge, the biosample and publication are separate edges.

limitations.text: No node means no E2G prediction for that interval in this release. A gene absent from this node set has no predicted element in the 322 covered biosamples.

The node is biosample- and study-specific: the same genomic interval and gene appear once per ENCODE study with the same coordinates and different scores, so counting nodes counts predictions, not elements. Only 20,088 targets have any prediction and only 322 biosamples are covered. Nothing here is a measured enhancer-gene interaction, a variant effect or a disease mechanism.
An intervalId is one study's element-gene prediction.
The graph contains 48.8M distinct regulatory elements, or that two nodes with the same coordinates are two elements.

The dataset has no other contributor, so the property carries no discrimination today.

components.name: safety_event
components.label: SAFETY_EVENT
components.description: One datasource's safety observation for one target.

claims.text: A safety observation row from target_safety_event: one datasource reporting that a target is associated with an event, with the source's event accession, citation and page where supplied.

targetId|event|datasource|eventId|url, with the empty string where eventId or url is null: 4,387 rows and 4,387 distinct keys. The target is part of the identity because each row is a target-specific observation, but it is not a property; the incoming HAS_SAFETY_EVENT edge carries it. (targetId, event, datasource) has only 4,337 distinct values, and adding eventId still gives 4,337: 31 repeated (target, event, datasource, eventId) groups, 15 of them with a null eventId, are separated only by url. eventId is null on 2,176 rows overall, and rows with both extra fields null still have distinct target, event and datasource triples.

frames.text: event is free text as the datasource writes it, not an ontology label. eventId, where present, is an accession in underscore form from several vocabularies (MONDO_, HP_, EFO_, GO_, NCIT_, CHEBI_, MP_, OBA_). datasource is the contributing source, not a release dataset. literature is a PubMed id as text. url is the source page.

limitations.text: No node means the release records no such observation for that target. A null eventId, literature or url is a source gap, not an empty event, citation or page.

The node is the observation, not a controlled event vocabulary: the same event text from the same datasource for another target is a different node, and two datasources writing the same clinical event are not merged. Two nodes can therefore share every stored property and differ only by their incoming target edge. Effects and biosamples are separate edges. studies is a documented limit: its 5,561 elements form 3,448 distinct description/name/type triples. name is null on 642 elements, carries an HP_, EFO_, MONDO_ or GO_ accession on 1,764, and free text (for example 'cyclophosphamide induced effect') on the rest; description is free text on 5,119; type is biochemical, cell-based, clinical or preclinical, with one null. The triple is not an identified study, so it produces no node or edge and stays in the source. Nothing here asserts causality, incidence, severity or a dose-response.

claims.text: The event text as the contributing datasource writes it.

frames.text: Free text: 1,459 distinct strings over 4,387 rows. The labels mix clinical events, assay readouts and model-organism observations.

limitations.text: Do not group by event text as if it were a MedDRA, HPO or EFO term. Identical strings from different datasources are not the same curated term; eventId is the accession where the source supplies one.

claims.text: The ontology accession the source supplies for the event, in underscore form such as HP_0001649 or MONDO_0005252.

frames.text: Present on 2,211 of 4,387 rows over 435 distinct accessions from eight prefixes: MONDO, HP, EFO, GO, NCIT, CHEBI, MP and OBA. The prefixes mix diseases, phenotypes, biological processes, a chemical and model-organism terms. The build carries the accession as a property and does not resolve it to a DiseaseNode or GO term.

limitations.text: Null on 2,176 rows, mostly ToxCast and ClinPGx, which name an event without an accession. A null id is a source gap, not a claim that the event has no ontology term.
The accessions are not filtered to the release's disease vocabulary, and the event string is not checked against the accession's label.

claims.text: The source that contributed the observation: a program, a study or a paper, for example ClinPGx, ToxCast, AOP-Wiki or Lynch et al. (2017).

frames.text: Nine values cover the 4,387 rows. ClinPGx (1,590) and Lynch et al. (2017) (1,341) supply most rows.

limitations.text: The values are not normalised across programmes or papers and do not name a release dataset. Two spellings of one source would be two datasources here.

claims.text: The PubMed id cited for the observation, as a decimal string.

frames.text: Non-null on 1,941 rows over 5 distinct PMIDs; every value is numeric. It is a citation attached to the observation, not a PublicationNode edge in this layer.

claims.text: The source page recorded for the observation.

frames.text: Non-null on 2,446 rows and null on 1,941. The value is also part of the node key, where null is written as the empty string.

limitations.text: A null url means the source supplied no page, not that no source exists.
A locator is not proof that the page supports the row. ToxCast reuses one page across many events and targets, so the url is not unique to an event.

claims.text: One SafetyEventNode per row of target_safety_event.
targetId|event|datasource|eventId|url, with the empty string where eventId or url is null: 4,387 rows and 4,387 distinct keys.

frames.text: event is source free text; eventId is the source's ontology accession where supplied. The target is not stored on the node; the HAS_SAFETY_EVENT edge carries it.

limitations.text: A row with a null targetId, event or datasource cannot be keyed and is dropped; the release carries none. A null url keys as the empty string and stays a null property.

The node key contains the target even though the target is not a property, so two targets sharing an event row produce two nodes with identical properties. The node does not normalise the event to an ontology term.

components.name: safety_event_effect
components.label: SAFETY_EVENT_EFFECT
components.description: One direction-and-dosing descriptor reported for a safety observation.

claims.text: An effect descriptor: the direction in which modulating the target is reported to change the event, together with the dosing context. It is a shared nine-value vocabulary, not an assay, study or measured effect.
direction|dosing, with the empty string where dosing is null: 9 distinct pairs over 2,349 array elements. direction is never null; dosing is null on 406 elements.
The nine descriptors are a closed vocabulary for this release.

frames.text: direction is one of two statements: Activation/Increase/Upregulation or Inhibition/Decrease/Downregulation. dosing is acute, general, chronic or developmental toxicity, or null.

limitations.text: No effect node means no effects element names the pair. A null dosing is a source gap, not a no-dose context.

The descriptor exists so that direction and dosing are not flattened into variable-length properties of the observation; it has no identity beyond the pair. direction describes the reported effect of modulating the target on the event, not the event's direction in a patient. dosing is a coarse context, not a dose, duration or exposure. The edge, not the node, ties a descriptor to an observation.
A descriptor is a curated ontology term.

claims.text: The signed direction of the reported effect.

frames.text: Two values only: Activation/Increase/Upregulation (1,162 elements) and Inhibition/Decrease/Downregulation (1,187 elements).

limitations.text: The wording combines activation, increase and upregulation into one bucket; it does not distinguish pharmacology from physiology.

claims.text: The dosing context in which the effect was reported.

frames.text: acute (1,286 elements), general (560), chronic (61), developmental toxicity (36) or null (406).

limitations.text: Null means the source states no dosing context, not that dosing was zero.
The values are coarse context labels, not doses, schedules or exposures, and they are not ordered by severity.

claims.text: One SafetyEventEffectNode per distinct effects element.
direction|dosing, with the empty string for a null dosing: 9 nodes from 2,349 array elements. The binding reads every effects element, so the repeated descriptors collapse to nine records.

frames.text: direction is the signed statement; dosing is the context label.

limitations.text: A row with a null or empty effects array emits no effect record.
The node set is a closed nine-value vocabulary, not an entity set; the HAS_EFFECT edge, not the node, ties a descriptor to an observation.

target_class::id::label::level. The numeric id is reused across levels with different labels, so the id alone is not the identity.

frames.text: level is the hierarchy tier (l1 to l6). A gene carries one edge per ancestor class from the most specific tier up to the root.

limitations.text: A target with no class edge is unclassified in the release, not classless in biology.
The classification is a curated descriptor for target assessment. It is not a functional assay, a protein family membership proof or a drug tractability claim.

claims.text: The release's numeric identifier for a target-class node.
One component of the node key, with label and level.

frames.text: The same id appears at several levels with different labels, so it must not be used as a class identifier on its own.

claims.text: The class name at this hierarchy level.
One component of the node key.

components.name: tractability_bucket
components.label: TRACTABILITY_BUCKET
components.description: One modality-by-category tractability assessment axis.

claims.text: A tractability bucket: one (modality, category) axis on which the release reports a yes/no assessment for a target.
modality|category: 28 buckets over 4 modality codes and 19 categories. Every one of the 18,869 assessed targets has exactly one row per bucket, 528,332 rows in total.
The bucket node exists so the modality and category vocabulary is shared instead of repeated on 528,332 edges.

frames.text: modality is the source code as written: AB, SM, PR, OC. category names the evidence axis, for example High-Quality Pocket, Approved Drug or UniProt loc high conf.

limitations.text: A bucket absent here is not an assessment axis in this release.

The release does not expand the modality codes in this dataset; do not read AB, SM, PR or OC as a spelled-out modality without external documentation. Bucket names are source labels, not a hierarchy, and they mix structural, localisation, ligand and clinical evidence.
The bucket is a measured property of a target.

claims.text: The drug-modality code the assessment applies to.

limitations.text: The codes are abbreviations whose expansions the release does not define in this dataset; do not infer them from the letters.

claims.text: The tractability evidence axis the assessment applies to.

frames.text: Nineteen labels such as Approved Drug, Phase 1 Clinical, High-Quality Pocket, High-Quality Ligand and UniProt loc high conf. Each label is reported under a subset of the four modalities.

limitations.text: Labels are free-text source names, not a controlled vocabulary: 'High-Quality Pocket' and 'Med-Quality Pocket' are separate buckets, and a bucket does not imply the others.

claims.text: One TractabilityBucketNode per distinct (modality, category) pair.
modality|category: 28 nodes from 528,332 rows. The binding reads every target row, so the repeated pairs collapse to 28 records.

frames.text: modality is a source code and category is the source's evidence label.

limitations.text: A bucket absent here is not an axis in this release.
The modality codes are not expanded in this dataset. The node collects source labels; it does not grade or order them.

components.name: transcript
components.label: TRANSCRIPT
components.description: A transcript annotated to a target gene.

claims.text: One transcript of a target gene: the release's transcript row, with its biotype, translation and genomic span. A transcript is a product of the gene, not the gene and not the protein.
transcript.transcriptId, the ENST accession. It is unique across the 644,292 transcript rows; the target is not part of the key.

frames.text: biotype is the transcript biotype. proteinId is the ENSP translation and is null for the 273,406 non-coding transcripts. isEnsemblCanonical is the Ensembl canonical choice; exactly one transcript per target is canonical. The transcript's target is the HAS_TRANSCRIPT edge, not a property.

limitations.text: A transcript absent here is outside the release's transcript set; it is not an unannotated isoform. A target with no transcript rows has no transcript annotation in the release.

The release carries flags (appris, gencode_primary, ensembl_canonical, mane) and 5,078,384 per-exon intervals as arrays on the transcript row. Only the canonical flag is published; the per-flag values and exon intervals stay in the source. A canonical transcript is the Ensembl choice, not a claim about the dominant isoform in a tissue.

claims.text: The transcript biotype from the release's annotation.

frames.text: protein_coding (278,455 rows) separates coding transcripts from lncRNA, nonsense_mediated_decay and other non-coding biotypes.

limitations.text: The label is the release's biotype vocabulary, not a functional assay.

claims.text: The ENSP translation identifier of the transcript.

frames.text: Read it together with biotype; a non-coding transcript has no translation.

limitations.text: Null for 273,406 of 644,292 transcripts; that is the release's annotation, not a zero-length protein.
The identifier names a translation, not a UniProt entry or a folded structure.

claims.text: Whether the release marks the transcript as the Ensembl canonical transcript of its gene.

frames.text: True on 78,733 transcripts, exactly one per target gene.

limitations.text: Canonical is an annotation choice; it does not establish expression, dominance or clinical relevance.

claims.text: The chromosome of the transcript's genomic span.

frames.text: Compare with the target's chromosome; a transcript lies on the gene's chromosome in this release.

claims.text: The transcript span's start coordinate on the chromosome.

frames.text: Coordinates are the release's chromosome coordinates; strand tells the direction. Do not compare them with another assembly without a liftover.

claims.text: The transcript span's end coordinate on the chromosome.

frames.text: start/end describe the transcript, not the encoded protein.

claims.text: The transcript's strand, 1 for forward and -1 for reverse.

frames.text: The value is an integer; in 26.09 it is 1 on 324,621 rows and -1 on 319,671.

limitations.text: Do not compare it with the '+'/'-' strings used by some other releases.

claims.text: The transcript's transcription start site coordinate.

frames.text: It is per transcript; the target node's tss is the gene-level canonical value.

limitations.text: A TSS coordinate is not a measured promoter or an active regulatory element.

claims.text: One TranscriptNode per row of transcript.
transcript.transcriptId, the ENST accession. All 644,292 rows have a distinct id, so no row is dropped.

frames.text: The row is one transcript. proteinId is the translation, null for non-coding biotypes. The target is bound as a separate edge, not as a node property.

limitations.text: A null transcriptId cannot be keyed and would be dropped; there are none in 26.09. A target with no transcript rows has no transcripts in the release.
The flags and exons arrays stay in the source: 5,078,384 exon intervals and four flag vocabularies are not published. The node is not a protein, a structure or an expression observation.

variant.variantId, spelled chromosome_position_reference_alternate (for example 1_17005_A_G). rsIds are cross-references, not the key.

frames.text: MostSevereConsequence is a separate edge to an SO term. A variant's effects are target- and transcript-specific records, not properties of the variant alone.

limitations.text: A variant absent here has no phenotypic information in the release; it is not absent from the human genome.

claims.text: One-based leftmost GRCh38 coordinate of the variant representation.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Indels are left-anchored representations, not unique biological points; never join on position alone.

claims.text: Reference allele string on the GRCh38 forward strand.

frames.text: Nucleotide letters or indel gap representation; multi-base values occur.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
It reproduces variantId only with chromosome, position and alternateAllele; it is not a transcript effect.

claims.text: Alternate, or effect, allele string on the GRCh38 forward strand.

frames.text: The allele against which allele frequencies and effect directions are measured.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.

claims.text: Genomic HGVS description taken from the first transcript consequence, or the first intergenic consequence.

graph_declaration.name: open_targets
graph_declaration.description: A knowledge graph of the Open Targets Platform 26.09 release. Nodes are entities the release identifies; edges are relations the release reports, derives or lets a consumer read from its records. The graph is a semantic index over the release, not a replacement for the release's own data.

claims.text: A knowledge graph of the Open Targets Platform 26.09 release. Nodes are entities the release identifies; edges are relations the release reports, derives or lets a consumer read from its records. The graph is a semantic index over the release, not a replacement for the release's own data.
What the 26.09 files were measured to contain, never what an upstream authority permits or what an earlier release contained.
A target-disease relation reported by the release from one or more evidence sources, with a score and evidence count. It is not a causal claim and it is not a prediction made by this graph.

A source-specific observation that a target is linked to a disease or phenotype. The observation carries the source's own method and score; the graph does not harmonise those meanings into one quantity.
The spelling of an ontology accession in the release: PREFIX_accession and PREFIX:accession are different strings. A join, filter or resolver must use the form the column actually carries.
A source-specific numeric judgement. Different datasets call different statistics score; a score is not comparable across datasets unless the graph states the comparison.
Ensembl gene identifiers (ENSG) are stable human gene accessions.
Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO), MONDO, HPO, GO, SO and Reactome accessions denote ontology terms in their respective namespaces.
A target-disease association score is a weighted aggregate over evidence sources; its scale and weighting are release-specific.

purpose.text: Target-disease evidence review and prioritisation over the Open Targets 26.09 release. For one target, disease or other entity, a consumer asks which relations the release reports, what each relation means, where it came from, and what it does not imply. The graph supports triage and prioritisation; it does not validate a target or establish causation.

frames.text: in this release

limitations.text: Do not read this as what an upstream authority permits or what an earlier release contained.

frames.text: association

limitations.text: Do not read this as a statistical association in a study, or a causal relation.

frames.text: evidence

limitations.text: Do not read this as one harmonised quantity comparable across evidence sources.

frames.text: identifier form

limitations.text: Do not read this as the Platform resolver, which normalises the separator on lookup.

frames.text: score

limitations.text: Do not read this as a probability, a p-value, or one universal confidence measure.

nodes.name: entity
nodes.description: A thing the release identifies and a consumer can ask about.

claims.text: An entity with its own identity in the release: a target, disease, molecule, variant, study, credible set or another identified record.
The concrete node's own release identifier.

frames.text: Read the concrete node for its properties and limits.

limitations.text: No node means the release does not identify the entity in this build.
An edge between two entities records the relation the concrete edge declares; it does not make the entities interchangeable.

nodes.name: adverse_event

claims.text: The MedDRA preferred-term label for the adverse event.

frames.text: event is the MedDRA preferred-term label. meddra_code is retained as a property and carries the release's empty string.

limitations.text: An event absent here had no significant signal for any molecule in the release; it is not absent from MedDRA or from clinical practice.
The term is a MedDRA vocabulary item, not an Open Targets disease or phenotype id. It does not join DiseaseNode without a mapping the release does not supply.

nodes.description: A term in an ontology the release uses, identified by its accession.

claims.text: An ontology term the release uses as a controlled vocabulary entry.

frames.text: Read the concrete term for its vocabulary and hierarchy.

limitations.text: An absent term is outside the release's ontology subset.
A term is vocabulary, not an assertion about any entity.

nodes.name: biosample

claims.text: The class's label as the contributing ontology writes it.

frames.text: Present on every row; 35,273 distinct names cover 35,477 rows. 710 values are URLs rather than readable anatomical text.

limitations.text: Not a key: one name can stand for up to three classes. The column holds only the ontology's label, never a study's or datasource's own tissue wording.

claims.text: The class definition as the contributing ontology publishes it.

frames.text: Null on 7,414 of 35,477 rows, which records that the contributing ontology publishes no definition for the class; its name and parents are intact.

limitations.text: A null description does not mark a class the Platform failed to annotate, and a non-null description is ontology prose, not a measured property of a sample.

nodes.description: A tissue or cell type in the release's biosample ontology.

claims.text: A class in the release's merged biosample vocabulary: a tissue, cell type, cell line or another ontology class used to describe an experimental context.
biosample.biosampleId: 35,477 rows and 35,477 distinct ids, never null. 34,120 are PREFIX_accession CURIEs, 1,338 are full ontology URLs, and 19 are other OBO or bare forms such as uberon#LATIN.

frames.text: biosampleName is a label; the id is the join key. Direct ontology parents are BiosampleIsAEdge; ancestors and descendants stay in the source as precomputed closures and are not published as edges.

limitations.text: A biosample absent here is outside the release's vocabulary. A null description is the contributing ontology publishing no definition, not an absent class.

A tissue, a cell type and a cell line share this node type; the id prefix is not a kind discriminator, and parents cross ontology prefixes (anatomy classes have GO, CL and SO parents). Use the hierarchy and cross-references, not the label, to tell kinds apart.

nodes.name: cell_line

claims.text: Display name of the cell line used in the screen.

frames.text: A label for plots and tooltips, not a stable identifier.

limitations.text: Never null in the screens; the build falls back to the CCLE name and then to a disease-derived label.
Not unique, because fallback labels merge distinct lines; group on depmapId instead.

claims.text: Tissue or lineage category label of the screen group.

frames.text: A curation-file label for a group of cell lines, not a measured tissue.

limitations.text: The build substitutes 'other' for an unnamed lineage, so a value exists rather than a hole.
A lineage group pools many cell lines and diseases; it is not a biosample.

claims.text: Ontology accession for the tissue or lineage category of the screen group.

frames.text: Mostly UBERON accessions in underscore form, with one CL accession, so the namespace matters.

limitations.text: Null when the lineage had no ontology match, which is the 'other' bucket.
Not biosample.biosampleId despite the release's declared join; it is an ontology term.

claims.text: Primary disease the cell line was derived from, in DepMap's Oncotree vocabulary.

frames.text: A source label, not a disease id; it includes Non-Cancerous.

limitations.text: Never null in the screens, because no disease mapping is applied.
It does not join disease.id; a dependency in a line labelled with a disease is not evidence about that disease.

nodes.description: A cell line used in an assay or a dependency screen.

claims.text: A cell line named by an assay, essentiality screen or CRISPR experiment. It is the experimental model, not the tissue it came from.
The release's cell-line identifier where supplied; otherwise the cell-line name. The same line can appear in several screens.

frames.text: Tissue and disease labels describe the line's origin. A dependency measured in one line is not a target-level fact.

limitations.text: A line absent here was not used by the release's assays.
A cell-line dependency is an in-vitro observation. It does not establish essentiality in a human tissue or a therapeutic window.

nodes.name: clinical_side_effect
nodes.description: A side-effect term named by a drug-warning report.

claims.text: A side-effect or toxicity term that a drug-warning report names, identified by the ontology accession the report carries. It is a term node, not a disease and not an observed event in a trial.
The term accession from clinical_report.sideEffects.diseaseId, used unmodified: EFO_, HP_, MONDO_, PATO_, NCIT_, OMIT_, ZP_, MP_ or MPATH_ prefixed. 199 accessions occur.

frames.text: The node carries no label because six accessions occur under more than one source spelling; the report's own wording is on the HAS_SIDE_EFFECT edge. 118 of the 199 accessions are also DiseaseNode keys and join by string equality; 81 are absent from the release's disease set.

limitations.text: An accession absent here was not named by a warning report in this release. That is not a claim the drug has no other adverse effects.

The vocabulary covers warning-recorded side effects only, not trial-observed events, and is not a MedDRA coding; it is a different node type from ADVERSE_EVENT, which holds openFDA MedDRA labels. A named warning term is not evidence that the drug caused the event.
