properties.name: qualityControls
properties.description: Flags naming a reason a consumer may drop the report (NO_DISEASE, UNVALIDATED_INDICATION, INDIRECT_PRIMARY_PURPOSE, PHASE_IV_NOT_APPROVED, SAFETY_REPORT); flagged rows stay published.

claims.text: Flags naming a reason a consumer may drop the report (NO_DISEASE, UNVALIDATED_INDICATION, INDIRECT_PRIMARY_PURPOSE, PHASE_IV_NOT_APPROVED, SAFETY_REPORT); flagged rows stay published.

nodes.description: A clinical report: a trial, label, approval or warning record about a drug.

claims.text: One document a clinical source published: a registered trial, a drug label, an approval record, or a withdrawal or warning notice. The row is the source document, not a drug-disease pair, a study arm or a trial site.
clinical_report.id, the source's own identifier lower-cased: a registry number, a UUID, a 64-hex hash, a product number or a bare name. It is unique over all 289,954 rows.
The report's drugs and diseases are lists, not a pairing: one report naming two drugs and two diseases asserts no individual drug-disease pair.

frames.text: origin separates registry trials (CLINICAL_TRIAL) from curated resources, drug labels and regulatory records; only registry rows carry trial columns. reportType is the document class (INDICATION or SAFETY) and is a different axis from origin. clinicalStage is the release's harmonised code, trialPhase the registry's own spelling. year dates a warning, trialStartDate a study.

limitations.text: A report absent here is outside the release's clinical sources. A null trial column means a non-registry row or an unrecorded fact, never a zero. A null diseases container is a list the build withdrew whole (qualityControls NO_DISEASE), not proof the document named none.

58,965 of the 289,954 rows are labels, approvals and warnings rather than trials. clinicalStage is not a development ladder: it is a 13-code label and APPROVAL folds in registry statuses and reference lists. No column records a trial's outcome or target.
Each drug in a report is studied for each disease in the same report.
A COMPLETED report is not a successful one and a TERMINATED one is not a failed one; no field records whether the study worked.
Trial status measures efficacy or safety.
On registry rows the drug and disease names come from an extraction model, not from the registry's intervention and condition fields.
diseaseFromSource quotes the condition the sponsor registered.

nodes.name: publication

claims.text: PubMed Central identifier of the publication where a PMC deposit exists.

frames.text: PMC-prefixed text used as a cross-reference, not as the node key.

limitations.text: Null when the paper has no PMC deposit, so no full text was mined.
Absence is not a missing publication record; the PMID remains the identity.

nodes.description: A literature entry identified by its PubMed identifier.

claims.text: A literature entry the release cites, identified by the release's literature key. The same entry is one node regardless of how many studies or evidence rows cite it.
The release literature key, normally a PubMed id but also PPR, PMC, IND, CAIN, ADL, FNI and other Europe PMC keys. A PMCID is a cross-reference and can be absent.

frames.text: Most keys are PubMed ids; 899,451 of 21,938,364 are not. The key is the release's spelling, not a promise that a PubMed record exists.

limitations.text: An evidence row with no PMID has no publication node; it is not a publication with an empty title.
A publication node records that the release cites the paper. It does not mean the paper's claims were verified by this graph.

nodes.name: disease

claims.text: Full ontology IRI of the disease term, copied from the source.

frames.text: Use for external links; the base address varies within one prefix family.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Not the join key and a weaker identity test than disease.id.

claims.text: Preferred label of the ontology term.

frames.text: Display text spanning diseases, phenotypes, measurements and non-Latin scripts.

limitations.text: Never null or empty in 26.09.
Not a join key; whitespace padding and re-labelling break exact matching.

claims.text: Free-text definition asserted by the term's owning ontology.

frames.text: Unstructured context whose voice and length vary by ontology.

limitations.text: Null when the ontology supplies no definition, not evidence that the concept is undefined.
Do not parse prose thresholds or treat it as a curated disease summary.

claims.text: Whether the term is one of the release's therapeutic-area grouping roots.

frames.text: Boolean from the ontology subset tag; true marks a grouping root, not a graph root.

limitations.text: Never null; false is a definite non-membership.
Some flagged terms are not diseases, so the flag is not a clinical-content filter.

claims.text: Leaf flag on the disease ontology record.

frames.text: Reads false on every 26.09 row because the build evaluated it before children were populated.

limitations.text: Never null; false therefore carries no information.
Do not infer a leaf from this flag; test the children or descendants edge instead.

claims.text: Source URL of the ontology term, taken from disease.ontology.sources.url.

frames.text: External address; it often equals code but may use a different base.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
It corroborates nothing beyond the source pointer and is not an independent identifier.

claims.text: Short source identifier stored in disease.ontology.sources.name.

frames.text: Despite the property name it is the term's accession, not its label.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Do not render it as a name or join on it; use disease.id for identity.

nodes.description: A disease, phenotype, biological process or measurement in the release.

claims.text: A disease or phenotype term used by the release. The node includes EFO, MONDO, Orphanet, HPO and other ontology accessions; it is one term, not a rolled-up therapeutic area.
disease.id, the ontology accession as written in the release.

frames.text: The id space is mixed-prefix. Read ontology.isTherapeuticArea and ontology.leaf to distinguish a therapeutic area, a leaf term and an internal ontology term.

limitations.text: A term absent here is not in the release's disease vocabulary; it is not evidence that the disease does not exist.
disease.id is not a MONDO-only identifier and the same biological concept can appear under more than one accession. Do not assume a single hierarchy or a single namespace.

nodes.name: molecule

claims.text: ChEMBL's preferred molecule name, falling back to the first ChEMBL synonym and then the molecule id.

frames.text: Mostly upper-case ChEMBL house style.

limitations.text: Never null; the build coalesces to the id when no name exists.
Not unique, because unrelated ChEMBL records share names; never join on it.

claims.text: ChEMBL molecule_type, the therapeutic modality or chemical class of the molecule.

frames.text: Title-case categorical vocabulary; the literal 'Unknown' marks a ChEMBL silence.

limitations.text: Never null; 'Unknown' means ChEMBL stated no molecule type.
Modality only: it says nothing about approval, druggability or drug-admission route.

claims.text: Most advanced clinical stage the molecule reached in any clinical report, across all indications.

frames.text: Ordinal SCREAMING_SNAKE stages; APPROVAL is most advanced and UNKNOWN last, with withdrawal and phase 4 collapsed to APPROVAL.

limitations.text: Never null; UNKNOWN covers both no report and unmappable source stages.
Not indication-specific and not evidence of efficacy; the roll-up uses unfiltered clinical reports.

claims.text: ChEMBL's canonical SMILES line notation for the molecule structure.

frames.text: Structural lookup text; read with inchiKey and molblock.

limitations.text: Null when ChEMBL holds no structure record, largely for biologics; it is not an empty structure.
Not a molecule identity key and not what the drug-page image renders.

claims.text: ChEMBL's InChIKey hash of the molecule structure.

frames.text: Fixed structural lookup value, not sortable and not decomposable into fields.

limitations.text: Null exactly when canonicalSmiles is null, because the key derives from structure.
Identifies a structure, not this row or a salt family.

claims.text: Build-generated sentence giving the molecule's modality, maximum clinical stage and approved and investigational indication counts.

frames.text: A rendering rather than source text; its counts come from all clinical reports without a QC filter.

limitations.text: Never null; clauses drop when data is missing.
Its indication counts do not reconcile with clinical_indication rows; never parse it as data.

nodes.description: A drug or clinical candidate molecule in ChEMBL.

claims.text: A bioactive molecule in the release's ChEMBL-derived drug set. It may be an approved drug, a clinical candidate or a tool compound.
drug_molecule.id, the ChEMBL molecule identifier.

frames.text: drugType and maximumClinicalStage describe the molecule across all indications; neither is an indication-specific approval.

limitations.text: A molecule absent here is outside the release's drug universe; it is not necessarily inactive or absent from ChEMBL.
A molecule is not a product or a salt: parent and child molecules are separate nodes and the parent relation is explicit.

nodes.name: constraint_type

claims.text: The constraint metric family reported on this node.
The node key.

frames.text: mis is missense, lof is loss of function, syn is synonymous.

limitations.text: The release's constraint array never carries a null constraintType.
The three families are separate metrics; their scores are not comparable.

nodes.description: One constraint metric family reported for targets.

claims.text: A constraint metric family: missense (mis), loss of function (lof) or synonymous (syn). The node names the family; each target's values are on the HAS_CONSTRAINT edge.
constraint_type::constraintType, one of mis, lof and syn.

frames.text: The same gene has up to three constraint edges, one per family. Compare values only within one family.

limitations.text: A gene with no constraint edge has no metric in the release, which is not a value of zero.
Constraint is a population-variation depletion signal, not a measured essentiality or a statement that loss of function is pathogenic.

nodes.name: credible_set

claims.text: GRCh38 chromosome of the set's lead variant, stored without a chr prefix.

frames.text: Categorical string from 1-22, X and Y; read it with position.

limitations.text: Never null; unusable chromosomes reject the row rather than nulling it.
Its value set differs from the variant and colocalisation chromosome columns; it is not the locus span.

claims.text: One-based GRCh38 position of the set's lead variant.

frames.text: Base pairs; always paired with chromosome.

limitations.text: Never null.
The lead's position, not the fine-mapped interval and not a causal coordinate.

claims.text: Text start and end of the fine-mapped region, in one of two incompatible formats.

frames.text: Either chr-prefixed or bare and zero-based text; parse tolerantly.

limitations.text: Null on every PICS row, whose method publishes no window here.
Null does not mean the set has no region; prefer the integer locus bounds where populated.

claims.text: Effect size of the lead variant with respect to its alternate allele.

frames.text: Sign gives ALT-allele direction; scale comes from the producing pipeline and is comparable only within a study.

limitations.text: Null when the source published no estimate, not a measured zero.
Never pool across finemappingMethod; a SuSiE beta is a shrunk posterior mean.

claims.text: Signed association statistic for the lead variant, beta divided by its standard error.

frames.text: Standard-error units, sharing beta's polarity.

limitations.text: Null on every non-SuSiE-inf row, so a null is a method boundary rather than an absence of association.
It describes only the SuSiE-inf subset and cannot characterise the whole file's signal strength.

claims.text: Mantissa half of the lead variant's study p-value, with p equal to mantissa times ten to the exponent.

frames.text: Range 1.0 to 10.0; read it only with pValueExponent.

limitations.text: Never null at lead level in 26.09.
An unconditioned study p-value, not a posterior probability; sorting on it alone gives the wrong order.

claims.text: Base-10 exponent half of the lead variant's study p-value.

frames.text: Negative integer; smaller means stronger and it is read with the mantissa.

limitations.text: Never null at lead level in 26.09.
Not the set's posterior evidence; a null here would mean the member-level field was read instead.

claims.text: Frequency of the lead variant's effect allele as the source study reported it.

frames.text: Proportion from 0 to 1, specific to the study's ancestry and allele coding.

limitations.text: Null when the source published no frequency, overwhelmingly molecular-QTL and curated-top-hit rows; not frequency zero.
Not a reference-panel frequency; filtering non-null restricts analysis to studies that reported it.

claims.text: Standard error of the lead variant's beta.

frames.text: Effect-size units; beta divided by it approximates the z-score, and zero is suspect.

limitations.text: Null when the source published no standard error, not a precision of zero.
Some pipelines publish placeholder or member-level values, so it is not always the study's estimate.

claims.text: Fine-mapping algorithm that produced the set's posteriors.

frames.text: Categorical values SuSie, SuSiE-inf and PICS; case-sensitive, and the method predicts which columns are populated.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
A pipeline label, not a model specification or a quality rank.

claims.text: One-based ordinal of this set among the sets returned for its study region, up to ten.

frames.text: Ordinal position, not an importance ranking; most populated rows are index 1.

limitations.text: Null on every PICS row, whose method does not enumerate signals.
The first index is not the causal set, and a non-null filter is a method filter in disguise.

claims.text: Base-10 log Bayes factor that the credible set contains a causal variant.

frames.text: Unbounded model evidence; higher is stronger and values span many orders of magnitude.

limitations.text: Null on every PICS row, which returns no model evidence; null is not weak evidence.
Orthogonal to resolution; read it with set size and never as a probability.

claims.text: Mean pairwise linkage-disequilibrium R-squared among the set's member variants.

frames.text: Zero to one; near one means little internal resolution, while a low value means the set spans weakly linked variants.

limitations.text: Null where the pipeline computed no within-set LD; not a purity of zero.
Read it with set size; high purity is not good resolution.

claims.text: Minimum pairwise linkage-disequilibrium R-squared within the credible set.

frames.text: Zero to one; a single-member set reads 1 trivially.

limitations.text: Null where no within-set LD was computed, not zero LD.
Method-specific floors are not global; do not threshold the whole column.

claims.text: Study-level sample size copied onto the credible set.

frames.text: Rough study attribute; many rows share a few values.

limitations.text: Null where the study index surfaced no usable total, not a small study.
Not for power calculations and not always a real cohort size.

claims.text: Fine-mapping framework and linkage-disequilibrium source behind the set, as a four-value label.

frames.text: Ordinal provenance, best first; 26.09 stores long labels such as 'SuSiE fine-mapped credible set with in-sample LD'.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09; the documented unknown class does not occur.
Not association strength or effect size; never sort the labels alphabetically.

claims.text: Study design behind the credible set: gwas or one of five molecular QTL classes.

frames.text: Lower-case categorical code copied from the study; read it with isTransQtl.

limitations.text: Never null; unknown designs are excluded upstream.
Says nothing about tissue or condition; read the joined study for those.

claims.text: Whether the molecular-QTL lead variant lies more than five megabases from the gene whose molecular trait is measured.

frames.text: Boolean cis/trans flag from a fixed five-megabase window.

limitations.text: Null on exactly the GWAS rows, where cis and trans are undefined; false is measured cis.
Populated on all molecular-QTL classes despite the name, and the deciding distance is not published.

nodes.description: A fine-mapped credible set for one study locus.

claims.text: A 95% credible set from a GWAS or molecular QTL study, with the lead variant, fine-mapping method and summary statistics.
credible_set.studyLocusId. It is unique in the release and names one study-locus credible set, not one variant.

frames.text: credibleSetIndex orders sets within a study locus. The lead variant is the variant with the highest posterior probability, not the causal variant.

limitations.text: No credible set means the study has no fine-mapped locus in the release, not that no association exists.
A credible set is a statistical set, not a biological mechanism. Membership does not establish causality; the L2G edge is a prediction.

nodes.name: variant

claims.text: GRCh38 chromosome label of the variant, stored without a chr prefix.

frames.text: Categorical string from 1-22, X, Y and MT; cast before numeric sorting.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
A chr-prefixed or numeric filter matches nothing; it is not the gene's chromosome property.

claims.text: One-based leftmost GRCh38 coordinate of the variant representation.

frames.text: Base pairs; meaningful only with chromosome and both alleles.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Indels are left-anchored representations, not unique biological points; never join on position alone.

claims.text: Reference allele string on the GRCh38 forward strand.

frames.text: Nucleotide letters or indel gap representation; multi-base values occur.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
It reproduces variantId only with chromosome, position and alternateAllele; it is not a transcript effect.

claims.text: Alternate, or effect, allele string on the GRCh38 forward strand.

frames.text: The allele against which allele frequencies and effect directions are measured.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Only SNVs and small indels are represented; it is not a genotype or haplotype.

claims.text: Genomic HGVS description taken from the first transcript consequence, or the first intergenic consequence.

frames.text: Genomic-level label independent of any chosen transcript.

limitations.text: Null on a few rows where no genomic description was produced.
Not unique and not a key; coding and protein HGVS forms are different strings.

claims.text: Build-generated sentence summarising the variant's most severe consequence and nearest gene context.

frames.text: Display text assembled from consequence, transcript and distance fields.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
It names whichever transcript sorted first, adds no information beyond its source columns and is unstable across builds.

nodes.description: A DNA variant identified by chromosome, position and alleles.

claims.text: A variant in the release's variant universe. The identity is the release's variant id, not an rsID or a normalized VCF record.
variant.variantId, spelled chromosome_position_reference_alternate (for example 1_17005_A_G). rsIds are cross-references, not the key.

frames.text: MostSevereConsequence is a separate edge to an SO term. A variant's effects are target- and transcript-specific records, not properties of the variant alone.

limitations.text: A variant absent here has no phenotypic information in the release; it is not absent from the human genome.
The id is build-dependent and allele-spelled; a liftover or a different representation is a different string. Do not join on rsID without an explicit cross-reference.

nodes.name: target

claims.text: HGNC's current approved gene symbol, with the Ensembl gene id as the fallback.

frames.text: Display label; HGNC renames propagate between releases.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09; an ENSG-shaped value marks a missing HGNC symbol.
Not unique; shared symbols occur, so never join on it. Use target.id.

claims.text: HGNC's approved full gene name, falling back to the Ensembl description and then the empty string.

frames.text: Search and display text; trim before exact comparison.

limitations.text: Never null but empty when neither HGNC nor Ensembl supplies a name.
Not unique; many pseudogenes share a description, so do not use it as identity.

claims.text: Ensembl gene biotype after the build removes the substring 'tec' from the stored string.

frames.text: Categorical Ensembl vocabulary; 'protein_coding' is the usual drug-target subset.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09; the empty string is the renamed tecRNA class, not an unknown biotype.
Non-protein-coding does not mean non-target; transcript biotype is a separate unstripped vocabulary.

claims.text: UniProt free-text descriptions of the gene product's function, one element per function block.

frames.text: Context only; the text retains UniProt citation markers and line-join artefacts.

limitations.text: Null when no UniProt entry is mapped, or empty when the entry has no function block.
Not a controlled annotation and not evidence of a role in any disease.

claims.text: GRCh38 chromosome of the gene's genomic span, stored without a chr prefix.

frames.text: Categorical string from 1-22, X, Y and MT; lexical sorting is wrong.

limitations.text: Never null for a keyed target; unmapped scaffolds are absent rather than labelled.
A variant inside this span is not necessarily in a transcript.

claims.text: Lowest one-based GRCh38 coordinate of the gene's genomic span.

frames.text: Base pairs; always less than or equal to end within one row.

limitations.text: Never null for a keyed target.
The gene span includes introns and UTRs; it is not a transcript or coding start.

claims.text: Highest one-based GRCh38 coordinate of the gene's genomic span.

frames.text: Base pairs; read together with chromosome and start.

limitations.text: Never null for a keyed target.
Not the end of a translated product; the span includes introns and UTRs.

claims.text: Direction of transcription as the signed integer 1 (forward) or -1 (reverse).

frames.text: No zero or unknown state; it selects start or end as the transcription start site.

limitations.text: Never null for a keyed target.
Not a transcript-level strand and not interchangeable with the '+'/'-' spelling used elsewhere.

claims.text: Transcription start site of the gene's canonical transcript on GRCh38.

frames.text: One-based coordinate; equals start on the forward strand and end on the reverse strand.

limitations.text: Never null for a keyed target.
Canonical is GENCODE's display choice, not MANE Select; the coordinate is not a promoter boundary.

nodes.description:
A human gene or protein product that the release treats as a drug target.

The release's target is an Ensembl gene, not a protein structure or a
transcript. One row describes one gene; protein identifiers, transcripts
and pathways are related records, not alternative targets.

claims.text: A human gene/protein product with an Ensembl gene identifier. The target is the gene the release's evidence and drug records refer to; it is not a specific protein isoform or transcript.
target.id, the Ensembl gene accession (ENSG...). A target row is one gene; the identifier is stable while symbols and coordinates move.

frames.text: Use approvedSymbol for display and id for joins. biotype separates protein-coding genes from non-coding and pseudogene targets.

limitations.text: A gene absent from this node set is not a target in the release; it may still exist in Ensembl. A null symbol is a release gap, not a non-gene.
Target membership is the release's target universe, not all human genes. Protein-level claims need the protein identifiers, not this node.

nodes.name: crispr_cell_line

claims.text: The cell-line name supplied by the CRISPR screen.

frames.text: A source label for display; the SIDM id is the key.

limitations.text: Null when the screen supplies no name.
Do not use the label as identity; names are not unique.

claims.text: The tissue label supplied by the CRISPR screen.

frames.text: A source label, not a biosample ontology key.

limitations.text: Null when the screen supplies no tissue label.
Tissue labels are not normalised and do not replace a biosample id.

claims.text: The tissue identifier supplied by the CRISPR screen.

frames.text: An ontology-style id where supplied; it is not a biosample id.

limitations.text: Null when the screen supplies no tissue id.
No crosswalk to BiosampleNode is supplied by the release.

nodes.description: A cell line named by a CRISPR screen, keyed by the release's SIDM id.

claims.text: A cell line used by a CRISPR screen, identified by the release's SIDM cell-line id in evidence_crispr.diseaseCellLines.
diseaseCellLines.id (SIDM). The release supplies no crosswalk to the DepMap ACH ids used by target_essentiality, so these are a separate node space from CELL_LINE.

frames.text: The name/tissue fields are source labels, not ontology keys.

limitations.text: A screen without a cell-line id emits no TESTED_IN edge.
A SIDM line is not a DepMap line; do not join the two id spaces. The screen result is an in-vitro observation.

nodes.name: cross_reference

claims.text: Authority or namespace that issued the cross-reference identifier.

frames.text: Names the authority, such as Ensembl, UniProt, Reactome, DrugBank or ClinVar, not the entity type.

limitations.text: An absent value means the release listed no authority for the identifier.
Casing and vocabulary differ by dataset, so the source alone does not prove the external record exists.

claims.text: Accession or identifier string within the namespace named by source.

frames.text: Meaningful only together with source; identifier formats are namespace-specific.

limitations.text: An absent identifier means the release listed no accession for that authority.
Not necessarily a resolvable or unique accession, and two entities sharing it are not thereby identical.

nodes.description: An identifier in an external namespace, independent of the entity using it.

claims.text: An external identifier, stored once per (source, identifier) pair. It is the join surface between the release's entities and external namespaces.
(source, identifier), written source:identifier in edges.

frames.text: The source names the authority (Ensembl, UniProt, Reactome, DrugBank, ClinVar, ...), not the entity type.

limitations.text: An absent cross-reference means the release did not list it.
Two entities sharing a cross-reference are not thereby the same entity; the edge means 'has this identifier', not identity.

nodes.name: obsolete_term

claims.text: The retired ontology accession as the release spells it.
The node key, prefixed obsolete_term::.

frames.text: Values use the release's underscore separator, for example GO_0033490 or CHEBI_22318, and are not CURIEs.

limitations.text: The release's obsoleteTerms arrays never carry a null element.
The string is retained for historical matching only; the namespace prefix does not prove a current record exists.

nodes.description: A retired ontology accession listed by a disease or phenotype term.

claims.text: A retired ontology accession that a disease or phenotype term lists as an obsolete term. It is an accession, not a term record of the dataset that lists it.
The accession as written, keyed obsolete_term::accession. The same accession listed by several current terms is one node.

frames.text: None of the 9,852 obsoleteTerms elements in disease resolves to a disease.id or a disease_hpo.id, and none of the 5,955 in disease_hpo resolves to a disease_hpo.id; 297 of the disease_hpo values are disease rows. The node set keeps the retired accession addressable instead of dangling or being dropped.

limitations.text: No node means the release lists no such retired accession. The release names no successor, merging or split for a retired accession.

A retired accession is not a synonym of its replacement and cannot be resolved to a current term from this dataset. The 297 disease_hpo obsoleteTerms values that also occur in the disease table stay retired accessions, so the edge does not link to the DISEASE node of the same string.

nodes.name: phenotype

claims.text: Preferred label of the phenotype term in its source ontology.

frames.text: HPO or MP label; casing follows the source vocabulary.

limitations.text: Never null or empty in both source datasets.
The same label need not denote the same term across HP and MP; join on the accession.

nodes.description: A phenotype term (HPO or MP).

claims.text: A phenotype or ontology term used by the release's disease-phenotype and mouse-phenotype records. The vocabulary is mixed: disease_hpo contains HP, UBERON, GO, CHEBI, CL, PATO, PR, MPATH and other accessions, and mouse records use MP terms.
The ontology accession, prefixed phenotype:: in keys. Different vocabularies must not be merged even when accessions collide.

frames.text: The label is the term's preferred name; the accession is the key. A disease-phenotype relation and a mouse-phenotype relation are different edges.

limitations.text: A term absent here is outside the release's phenotype subset.
A phenotype annotation is an association, not a diagnosis. A mouse phenotype mapped to a human term is a model inference.

nodes.name: disease_synonym

claims.text: The synonym string as the release spells it.
Part of the node key, with kind.

frames.text: Case, punctuation and whitespace are as supplied; there is no normalization.

limitations.text: The release's four synonym arrays never carry a null element.
Two disease terms can share a label, and the same label can appear under two classes; the node is a vocabulary entry, not a disease.

claims.text: The synonym class the string was recorded under.
Part of the node key, with label.

frames.text: exact comes from exactSynonyms, related from relatedSynonyms, narrow from narrowSynonyms and broad from broadSynonyms.

limitations.text: Every synonym node names exactly one class.
The four classes are release fields, not an ontology of synonym scopes; their definitions are not restated in the dataset.

nodes.description: One name listed for a disease term, in one synonym class.

claims.text: A name the release lists for a disease term, qualified by the synonym class it was recorded under.
(kind, label), keyed disease_synonym::kind::label. The same string under two classes is two nodes, because the release records the classes separately.

frames.text: kind is the release's synonym class: exact, related, narrow or broad. disease.synonyms repeats the four flat arrays field for field (93,524 exact, 14,670 related, 1,909 narrow and 1,523 broad elements, with no row differing), so the struct supplies no additional nodes.

limitations.text: No node means the release lists no such name for any disease term. The synonym arrays carry no source, curator or date, so a name node cannot say who asserted the name.

A synonym is a naming fact, not an equivalence claim: an exact synonym does not merge two DISEASE nodes, a broad synonym is wider than the term and a narrow synonym is narrower. The release supplies no synonym source field, so source is unresolved for this domain.

nodes.name: drug_warning

claims.text: The release's toxicity category for the warning, for example hepatotoxicity or cardiotoxicity.

frames.text: The release's toxicity category for the warning, for example hepatotoxicity or cardiotoxicity.

limitations.text: Null for 246 rows; that is a release gap, not 'no toxicity'.
The category is a label given by the source, not a severity grade.

claims.text: The regulatory jurisdiction or jurisdictions named by the warning, sometimes a semicolon-separated list.

frames.text: Read the string as a list when it contains semicolons; it is not an ISO code.

limitations.text: A jurisdiction is not a marketing authorisation for the molecule.

claims.text: Free-text description of the warning as published.

frames.text: Free-text description of the warning as published.

limitations.text: Null for 1,024 rows; the warning still exists as a node.
The text is quoted source prose, not a normalised statement of effect.

nodes.description:
One source row asserting a target-disease relationship.

The common properties are the release's uniform evidence envelope.  They are
declared once here so every source node carries the same provenance fields;
a source that lacks a field carries null on that node, not a missing property.

claims.text: One row of a target-disease evidence dataset, kept as a node so its target, disease and provenance can be traversed. The node is the source's assertion, not an aggregate target-disease score.
The dataset's own id field. Every evidence id in 26.09 is a build-assigned hash, unique within the released table but not a provider accession and not stable across releases.

frames.text: Every source node has one HAS_TARGET and one HAS_DISEASE edge. Source-specific provenance edges are HAS_VARIANT, FROM_STUDY, SUPPORTED_BY, TESTED_IN, FROM_MODEL, HAS_MODEL_PHENOTYPE, HAS_HUMAN_PHENOTYPE, HAS_MOLECULE and IN_PATHWAY.

limitations.text: A missing source row is absent evidence, not a tested negative. A null provenance field means the source did not supply it.
An evidence node is not the aggregate association between its target and disease; the aggregate layer is separate and is not linked back to individual rows by the release.

frames.text: Every row names at least one cell line; diseaseCellLines expands to TESTED_IN edges keyed by the SIDM cell-line id. The cell-line tissue fields live on the cell-line node, not this row. The TESTED_IN edge does not assert that the screen was successful.

nodes.name: go_term

claims.text: The term name as GO publishes it, including the 'obsolete ' prefix.

frames.text: Display, not identity: 48,318 distinct labels cover 48,340 rows, and each of the 22 repeated labels belongs to two retired terms.

limitations.text: Labels are not unique, so grouping annotations by label can merge two retired classes. All 10,248 retired labels begin 'obsolete ' and no live label does.

claims.text: The GO branch the term belongs to.

frames.text: Exactly three lowercase values: biological_process (30,885 terms), molecular_function (12,855) and cellular_component (4,600), with no nulls and no fourth value.

limitations.text: The branch is an ontology branch, not an identifier prefix or a resolver namespace. It is not preserved across all relations: 786 of 7,058 part-of edges join terms from different branches, so filtering a walk by namespace cuts real part-of links.

claims.text: True when GO retired the class; the release keeps the row.

frames.text: True on 10,248 of 48,340 rows: 6,911 biological_process, 2,814 molecular_function and 523 cellular_component terms. Every retired row has empty isA, partOf, regulation, ancestor and descendant arrays.

limitations.text: Retirement is not a successor: no column names the term that replaced a retired class. Counting rows without this flag counts retired classes as current biology.

claims.text: Retired GO accessions that the release records as alternatives for this term.

frames.text: 3,646 values on 2,434 rows; the other 45,906 rows hold an empty array. No value equals any go.id in this release, so an alt id resolves to no row here.

limitations.text: An alt id is not an alternative key: to address the term, use its current id. The array sits on the current term and points back to retired accessions, so it cannot be read backwards to resolve a retired id.

nodes.description: A Gene Ontology term.

claims.text: A Gene Ontology term: a biological process, molecular function or cellular component. The term is the ontology unit, not an annotation of one gene. Retired classes keep a row.
go.id, the GO accession in colon form (GO: plus seven digits). One row per id: 48,340 rows and 48,340 distinct ids in 26.09.

frames.text: namespace separates the three branches. altIds are retired accessions recorded on the current term, not separate terms. isObsolete marks the 10,248 rows GO retired, which the release keeps for historical annotations.

limitations.text: A term absent from go is outside the release's GO subset. No id, label or namespace is null, so a missing value is not a release gap here.

A GO annotation is an edge from a target with its own evidence, aspect and qualifier; the term alone does not say a gene is annotated with it. A retired term is a class GO no longer curates, not a synonym of its replacement.

nodes.name: hallmark

claims.text: Which hallmark record shape the node carries.
One component of the node key.

frames.text: attribute is a free-text observation under a named category; cancerHallmark is an assignment to a cancer-hallmark label.

limitations.text: Every hallmark node names one kind.
The two kinds are not comparable statements about the same evidence.

claims.text: The attribute category name for an attribute record, or the cancer-hallmark label for a cancerHallmark record.
One component of the node key.

frames.text: Attribute names include function summary, role in cancer and clinical impact; cancer-hallmark labels include angiogenesis and genome instability and mutations.

limitations.text: The release's hallmark arrays never carry a null category.
The two vocabularies are distinct; do not group attribute names and hallmark labels together.

claims.text: The curator's free-text statement supporting the hallmark annotation.
Last component of the node key; the text distinguishes statements.

frames.text: It is prose written by the release's curators, not an abstract or a result field.

limitations.text: The release's hallmark arrays never carry a null description.
The text is not normalized and can mention several genes or contexts.

claims.text: The PubMed identifier of the publication cited for the statement.
One component of the node key. Three attribute records have no PMID; the key substitutes 0 for the missing value.

frames.text: A PMID is a publication, not a study id in this release.

limitations.text: Null means the release listed the statement without a publication id.
The PMID is not linked to a publication node by this edge.

claims.text: The direction word a cancerHallmark record assigns to the hallmark.
One component of the node key for cancerHallmark records.

frames.text: Observed values are promotes, suppresses and promotes or suppresses, with trailing whitespace in some rows.

limitations.text: Null for every attribute record and for cancerHallmark rows whose impact the release left empty.
The word is a curator's direction, not a measured effect size or a clinical claim.

nodes.description: One cancer-hallmark statement attached to a target.

claims.text: One hallmark annotation of a target. The release stores two kinds: attribute records, a categorised free-text observation with a PubMed reference, and cancerHallmark records, an assignment to one of the release's cancer-hallmark labels with an impact word.

The node key: hallmark::kind::category::pmid::description for an attribute record, with ::impact inserted before the description for a cancerHallmark record. One target can carry several statements for the same hallmark category under different publications.

frames.text: kind separates the two record shapes. category is the attribute name (for example function summary) or the cancer-hallmark label. impact is set only for cancerHallmark records.

limitations.text: A target with no hallmark edge has no hallmark annotation in the release. An empty hallmark struct and a missing one are equivalent here.
Attribute text is free prose and is not normalized or scored. A cancer-hallmark label is a curator's interpretation; impact is a direction word, not a measured effect size.

nodes.name: homology_gene

claims.text: NCBI taxonomy id of the species the homologue gene belongs to, as text.

frames.text: 13 values: 9606 Human (3,552,256 rows), 9598 Chimpanzee, 9544 Macaque, 10090 Mouse, 10116 rat, 9986 Rabbit, 10141 Guinea Pig, 9615 Dog, 9823 Pig, 8364 frog, 7955 Zebrafish, 7227 fruit fly, 6239 C. elegans.

limitations.text: The id names a species, not an organism or a strain; 10116 is labelled 'Norway rat - BN/NHsdMcwi', a strain-qualified name under the rat taxon.

claims.text: The release's display name for the species.

frames.text: One name per speciesId, so the two properties are redundant by construction; the names mix common names, a strain and a parenthetical authority.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Not a controlled vocabulary; 'Norway rat - BN/NHsdMcwi' and 'Caenorhabditis elegans (Nematode, N2)' are display strings, so never group or join on the name.

claims.text: The homologue gene's accession in its own species, as the source writes it; the source names the column targetGeneId because the gene is the homology query's target.

frames.text: Ensembl accessions for 12 species and FlyBase (FBgn) or WormBase (WBGene) ids for the other two.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
It is not a target id: only the 20,910 human values live in the same namespace as target.id, and 46 of those name no target row.

claims.text: The homologue gene's symbol in its own species.

frames.text: 97,163 distinct values. On the 3,544,075 resolved human rows it equals target.approvedSymbol exactly.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Symbols are not unique across species and are renamed between releases; never join on the symbol.

claims.text: The release's ordinal rank of the gene's species, ascending from Human at 0 to C. elegans at 12.

frames.text: 13 values, constant within a species; every gene node of a species carries the same integer.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
A species rank, not a per-pair or per-gene score. It is ordinal (the gaps are not measured distances), so do not average it across nodes.

nodes.description: A gene in one species that the release lists as a target's homologue.

claims.text: A gene the release records as a homologue of a target, identified in its own species. It is a gene record, not a TargetNode: 12 of the 13 species use gene namespaces outside the release's human target set.

speciesId|targetGeneId: 228,395 nodes over the 3,817,240 homology rows. 20,910 are human ENSG ids and 207,485 are ids in 12 non-human namespaces (ENSPTRG, ENSMMUG, ENSMUSG, ENSRNOG, ENSSSCG, ENSCAFG, ENSCPOG, ENSOCUG, ENSDARG, ENSXETG, FBgn, WBGene). The species is part of the identity because the node is a gene in species, not a free-floating accession.
The node exists so the 207,485 non-human homologue genes have an identity without being minted as targets.

frames.text: targetGeneSymbol is the homologue's own symbol and equals the target's approvedSymbol on every resolved human row. priority is the species' rank in the release: Human 0, Chimpanzee 1, Macaque 2, Mouse 3, rat 4, Rabbit 5, Guinea Pig 6, Dog 7, Pig 8, frog 9, Zebrafish 10, fruit fly 11, C. elegans 12. It is constant per species and identical on every node of that species.

limitations.text: A gene absent here was reported as a homologue of no target in this release; it is not absent from its species' genome. Null speciesId, speciesName, targetGeneId, targetGeneSymbol or priority never occur in 26.09.

Organism gene accessions are not resolvable inside the release: 207,485 of the 228,395 nodes are outside target.id and carry no cross-reference here, so the graph cannot say more about those genes than the symbol. priority ranks species, so it must not be averaged, summed or read as a quality score for a gene or a pair.
A HOMOLOGY_GENE is a drug target of the release.

nodes.name: interaction

claims.text: The database that contributed the interaction record.

frames.text: Four values: 'string' (13,205,373), 'intact' (1,310,951), 'reactome' (56,076) and 'signor' (39,799).

limitations.text: Null on no row.

'string' is a literal placeholder written by the build and must not be read as the STRING database's curated name; the row's evidence type and detection methods live in interaction_evidence, which is not bound.

claims.text: The number of interaction_evidence rows the release aggregates into this interaction.

frames.text: 1 to 227 in 26.09; it equals the number of interaction_evidence rows with this interactionId on all 14,612,199 interactions. Two evidence rows is the common case (6,566,211 interactions).

limitations.text: Never null.
It counts source records, not independent experiments: one study reported by three databases can contribute three rows. It is not a confidence, a citation count or a strength.

claims.text: The interaction score the release reports for the pair.

frames.text: 0.15-1.0 on the string and intact rows; it equals the maximum interactionScore among the pair's evidence rows on 14,516,323 of 14,612,199 interactions.

limitations.text: Null on 95,875 rows, which are the reactome and signor interactions: those databases supply no score.
The score does not share a scale across databases and is not a probability. Absence on reactome and signor rows is a source property, not a low score.

claims.text: The short species name recorded for participant A.

frames.text: 'human' on every row in 26.09.

limitations.text: Never null.
The field is constant, so it carries no discrimination; the B side is the informative species.

claims.text: The scientific species name recorded for participant A.

frames.text: 'Homo sapiens' on every row.

limitations.text: Never null.
A constant field; do not use it to distinguish interactions.

frames.text: 9606 on every row.

limitations.text: Never null.
A constant field; taxon ids elsewhere in the release can be negative placeholders.

claims.text: The short species name recorded for participant B.

frames.text: 'human' for the 14,566,853 human-human rows, with viral, bacterial and other mnemonics for the rest.

limitations.text: Never null.
A non-human mnemonic marks a host-pathogen interaction, not a non-human target.

claims.text: The scientific species name recorded for participant B.

frames.text: Mostly Homo sapiens; the rest name viruses, bacteria and one chemical synthesis placeholder.

limitations.text: Null on 33 rows.
Strain-qualified names occur, so equality on the string is stricter than equality of species.

claims.text: The NCBI taxon id recorded for participant B.

frames.text: 9606 for human-human rows; other taxa include 2697049 (SARS-CoV-2) and -2 for a chemical-synthesis placeholder.

limitations.text: Never null.
Negative taxon ids are placeholders, not NCBI taxa.

nodes.description: One aggregated molecular interaction between two participants.

claims.text: An aggregated molecular interaction as the release's interaction dataset reports it: two participants, the species each was observed in, the contributing database and the evidence count. It is a pair-level record, not a single experiment.

interaction.interactionId, an opaque signed 64-bit hash rendered as text; 14,612,199 rows and 14,612,199 distinct ids, so the release key is unique. It is not derived from the participants: 13,578,595 distinct (targetA, targetB) pairs cover the 14.6M rows, and 340,613 rows share even (targetA, targetB, sourceDatabase) with another row.

frames.text: count is the number of interaction_evidence rows behind the pair: it agrees with the evidence count on all 14,612,199 interactions. scoring is the maximum evidence interactionScore on 14,516,323 rows and null on 95,875, which are the reactome and signor rows that carry no score. sourceDatabase names the contributing database; speciesA and speciesB are the participants' species, and the participants themselves are the HAS_PARTICIPANT_A and HAS_PARTICIPANT_B edges.

limitations.text: No node means the release has no aggregated interaction for that pair. A null scoring means the source database does not score interactions, not a score of zero.

A node per interaction is 14.6M nodes plus about 29M participant edges: the interaction cannot be a bare target-target edge because one pair can carry several ids and because a two-sided record needs a place for both roles and both species. 'string' is the literal sourceDatabase on 13,205,373 rows, an upstream placeholder rather than a database name. interaction_evidence is materialised only where the release identifies a row: INTERACTION_EVIDENCE nodes and HAS_EVIDENCE edges cover the 2,447,776 rows that carry an interactionIdentifier, while 24,948,510 rows (91%) carry none and stay in the source. This node already states the full evidence count and a near-maximum evidence score (the max matches on 14,516,323 of 14,612,199 interactions), so the evidence layer adds detection method, host organism and citation for the identified subset only. Physical interaction is not functional modulation, pathway membership or a target-disease assertion.
An INTERACTION node aggregates evidence rows for one participant pair from one database.
The two targets bind each other in a human cell, or that the interaction is direct, functional or disease-relevant.

nodes.name: interaction_evidence

claims.text: The source database's identifier for this interaction evidence row.

frames.text: Opaque source string; paired with interactionId for the node key.

limitations.text: Null on 24,948,510 of the 27,396,304 rows; only the non-null subset is carried.
It is not a global interaction id and is not unique without interactionId.

claims.text: The database that supplied the evidence row.

frames.text: A source label; the aggregate InteractionNode carries its own sourceDatabase.

limitations.text: Null when the resource block is absent.
Do not assume a score scale is shared with another source database.

claims.text: The version of the source database.

frames.text: A source version string, not the release version.

limitations.text: Null when the resource block is absent.
Different versions can change the detection vocabulary.

claims.text: The source's interaction score for this evidence row.

frames.text: Source-specific scale; compare only within the same source database.

limitations.text: Null when the source supplies no score.
Not a probability and not comparable across source databases.

claims.text: The source's evidence score for this supporting row.

frames.text: Source-specific scale; it is not the aggregate interactionScore.

limitations.text: Null when the source supplies no evidence score.
Do not compare with interactionScore or another database's score.

claims.text: The short name of the interaction detection method.

frames.text: A PSI-MI vocabulary label; pair it with the MI identifier.

limitations.text: Null when the source supplies no detection method.
The label is not a controlled key; use the MI identifier for joins.

claims.text: The PSI-MI identifier of the detection method.

frames.text: The stable identifier for the method vocabulary.

limitations.text: Null when the source supplies no method identifier.
It does not say whether the method detects direct physical binding.

claims.text: The short name of the method used to expand the interaction.

frames.text: A source label; pair it with the MI identifier.

limitations.text: Null when no expansion method is stated.
Expansion is not the primary detection assay.

claims.text: The PSI-MI identifier of the expansion method.

frames.text: The stable identifier for the expansion vocabulary.

limitations.text: Null when no expansion method is stated.
Expansion does not establish a direct physical interaction.

claims.text: The short name of the interaction type.

frames.text: A PSI-MI label for physical or functional interaction.

limitations.text: Null when the source supplies no type.
The label does not establish the biological mechanism.

claims.text: The PSI-MI identifier of the interaction type.

frames.text: The stable identifier for the interaction-type vocabulary.

limitations.text: Null when the source supplies no type identifier.
An interaction type is not a direction or a causal claim.

claims.text: Scientific name of the host organism used in the assay.

frames.text: A species label for the experimental host.

limitations.text: Null when the source supplies no host organism.
The host is not necessarily either interaction participant.

claims.text: NCBI taxonomy id of the host organism.

frames.text: A taxonomy identifier; pair it with the scientific name.

limitations.text: Null when no host organism is stated.
It does not identify either participant in the interaction.

claims.text: The PubMed identifier cited by the evidence row.

frames.text: A citation key; the SUPPORTED_BY edge carries it.

limitations.text: Null on 24,948,514 of the 27,396,304 rows; no empty string occurs.
A citation does not verify the interaction.

nodes.description: One supporting evidence row for an aggregated interaction.

claims.text: A supporting interaction-evidence row, keyed by the release's interactionId and interactionIdentifier. It is the evidence behind an InteractionNode, not a second interaction pair.

(interactionId, interactionIdentifier): 2,447,776 distinct pairs from the 2,447,794 rows that carry an identifier. The other 24,948,510 rows of interaction_evidence carry no identifier and emit no node.

frames.text: Scores, detection methods and host organism belong to the evidence row; the interaction node carries the aggregate count and pair.

limitations.text: A null interactionIdentifier cannot key the row, so 91% of the evidence table is not represented: only the subset the sources identify gets a node. The interaction's count still counts every evidence row.

The evidence layer qualifies 2.45M of the 27.4M supporting rows, so an interaction with count 3 can have no HAS_EVIDENCE edge at all. The participant detection-method arrays and host tissue stay in the source; the row does not repeat the two participant target ids.

nodes.name: molecule_name

claims.text: The recorded name string, as written by the naming source.

frames.text: Names are not normalised; compare the recorded text, not a case-folded form.

limitations.text: The same string can be a synonym for one molecule and a trade name for another; the kind prefix keeps those names distinct.

claims.text: The authority that supplied the name, for example ChEMBL, DrugBank or WHO.

frames.text: The source is a naming authority, not the molecule's origin or the dataset name.

limitations.text: Two authorities can use different strings for the same product.

nodes.description: A synonym or trade name recorded for a molecule, with its kind and source.

claims.text: A name recorded for a molecule, either a synonym or a trade name, together with its kind and naming authority.
The (kind, source, label) triple, keyed kind::source::label, where kind is synonym or trade_name. The relation type is part of identity because the release records the two name classes separately.

frames.text: label is the recorded string and source is the naming authority (for example ChEMBL, DrugBank or WHO). A molecule's preferred name is MoleculeNode.name, not a node in this set.

limitations.text: No name node means the release lists no synonym or trade name with a usable label and source. Rows with a null label or source cannot be keyed and are dropped.
Sharing a name is not chemical, regulatory or therapeutic equivalence. Do not join two molecules on a name node; use the explicit cross-reference edges.

nodes.name: pgx_annotation

claims.text: ClinPGx's clinical-annotation accession, as a decimal string.

frames.text: 5,190 distinct values over 33,479 rows; the largest annotation (1184757183, CYP2D6 and bufuralol) has 270 rows.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Not the release's study: none of the 5,190 values occurs in study.studyId, and it is not unique per row.

claims.text: The data provider that supplied the annotation.

frames.text: The constant 'clinpgx' on every row.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
One value means the property cannot partition the annotations; the release integrates no other pharmacogenomics source in 26.09.

claims.text: The ClinPGx dump date the annotations were taken from.

frames.text: The constant '2026-07-05' on every row, an ISO date.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
It dates the ClinPGx feed, not the Open Targets release (published 2026-09-18) and not the release's own files.

claims.text: The record-type stamp of the pharmacogenomics file.

frames.text: The constant 'clinical_annotation' on every row.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
It is not a member of the association datasets' datatype vocabulary, so it must not be unioned with their values.

claims.text: The allele-function label ClinPGx gives the annotated genotype or haplotype: how it changes the gene product.

frames.text: Ten values in three schemes: function terms (No function 3,111, Decreased function 1,420, Normal function 1,226, Uncertain function 773, Increased function 343, Unknown function 6), a copy-state 'Presence' (112) and class pairs (IV/Normal 20, III/Deficient 10, II/Deficient 5). Null on 26,453 rows.

limitations.text: Null means ClinPGx left the cell blank, not that function is unchanged: 'No function' and 'Normal function' are separate populated values.
It describes the allele, not the drug response; the three schemes are not ordered, so the values must not be sorted by severity.

claims.text: ClinPGx's evidence grade for the annotation as a whole.

frames.text: Six codes: 1A (4,992 rows), 1B (353), 2A (510), 2B (131), 3 (25,871) and 4 (1,622). The order 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B, 3, 4 is ClinPGx's, not alphabetic.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.

3 is the modal low-evidence bucket and 4 means the evidence does not support the association, so a high code is not a missing score. The grade is not a strength estimate and does not transfer between drugs.

claims.text: The genotype or allele as ClinPGx writes it.

frames.text: 418 distinct labels over 33,479 rows: star-allele diplotypes such as *1/*1, single alleles such as *48, repeat counts, and the literal 'null/null' for deletion alleles on 38 rows.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
A label, not a key: '*1/*1' occurs for many genes. It is part of the annotation's identity because it separates rows that share every other field.

claims.text: The VCF-style genotype spelling chr_pos_reference_allele1,allele2 that the release records for the row.

frames.text: 8,568 distinct values, null on 9,634 rows: all 9,548 haplotype-anchored rows plus 86 rsID-anchored rows without coordinates. Example: 10_119371801_A_A,G.

limitations.text: Null is a row with no coordinates to write down (the haplotype-anchored branch), not a genotype whose annotation failed to resolve.
A genotype is not a variant: it holds both alleles, and variantId is the build's reduction of it. Never join genotypeId to variant.variantId.

claims.text: ClinPGx's full sentence explaining the genotype's clinical significance.

frames.text: Repeats across every row one annotation fans out to, so it is not unique. 29,818 of the 32,349 non-null phenotypeText values are substrings of it.

limitations.text: Null on 1,130 rows.
Prose, not a term: do not group by it and do not parse dosages from it. It is the source sentence behind phenotypeText, not a second phenotype.

claims.text: The allele or diplotype name ClinPGx uses for the row's subject.

frames.text: 593 distinct values such as CYP2C19*17 and CYP1A1*1/*1; null on 23,931 rows, exactly the rows that name a variant by rsID instead.

limitations.text: Null marks the rsID-anchored branch, not an annotation without a subject.
A name, not an accession, and it can be a pair of alleles; there is no haplotype table in the release to resolve it against.

claims.text: ClinPGx's own haplotype accession, PA followed by 8 or 9 digits.

frames.text: 422 distinct PA accessions on 8,248 rows; null on 25,231 rows, which include the rsID-anchored rows and haplotypes ClinPGx left without an accession.

limitations.text: Null is a missing ClinPGx accession, not a missing haplotype name.
It is not a release identifier and joins to no table in this release; the node keeps it as the source's accession only.

claims.text: ClinPGx's curated role of the annotated phenotype in drug response.

frames.text: Six lower-case codes: toxicity (11,846 rows), efficacy (10,948), metabolism/pk (7,401), other (1,823), dosage (1,442) and pd (19).

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
An annotation with several categories contributes one row per category, so rows count categories, not annotations. 'pd' (pharmacodynamic) holds 19 rows, too few to stratify on.

claims.text: The drug-response phrase the release publishes for the annotation.

frames.text: 5,037 distinct strings over 32,349 non-null rows, for example 'decreased clearance of bufuralol'. 29,818 are literal substrings of the row's genotypeAnnotationText; the other 2,531 are not, so the wording is not always a verbatim excerpt.

limitations.text: Null on 1,130 rows means the extraction returned nothing, not a genotype with no response.
Extracted prose, not a controlled term: different strings state one phenotype, so do not group on it. It is not ClinPGx's own phenotype wording and no ontology term is attached to it directly.

claims.text: The release's disease accession for the row's phenotype phrase.

frames.text: 30 accessions over 724 rows, mixing MONDO, EFO, GO, HP and NCIT; MONDO_0018493 alone covers 581 rows. All 30 resolve to disease.id.

limitations.text: Null on 32,755 rows (97.8%) means the phrase matched no disease label; the phenotype text is still present on 31,625 of those rows.
The mapping is sparse and many-to-one, so it is not a substitute for phenotypeText and does not make the annotation a disease association.

claims.text: The dbSNP rsID ClinPGx names for the variant.

frames.text: 2,843 distinct rs-prefixed values, null on 9,548 rows; 2,829 of the distinct values occur in variant.rsIds and 14 do not.

limitations.text: Null marks the haplotype-anchored branch, not a variant without an rsID.
It is not a key: nothing in the release is keyed by rsID and 14 values resolve to no variant row. The variant edge uses variantId, not this.

claims.text: The release's variant key for the row, derived by the build from genotypeId by splitting the two alleles and dropping any equal to the reference.

frames.text: 16,169 non-null rows over 2,882 distinct chromosome_position_ref_alt values; all 2,882 resolve to variant.variantId. Example: 10_119371801_A_G from genotypeId 10_119371801_A_A,G.

limitations.text: Null on 17,310 rows for two reasons: the 9,548 haplotype-anchored rows have no genotypeId coordinates (genotypeId is null on all of them), and 7,762 rsID-anchored genotypes reduce to the reference and leave no alternate allele.
Derived, not supplied: a row holds one allele and one genotype can yield two variants, so the row's variant is not necessarily the subject the annotation was curated about.

claims.text: The Ensembl gene id of the pharmacogene the annotation is about.

frames.text: 1,152 distinct ENSG values on 31,910 rows; 1,101 resolve to target.id and 51 do not (6,615 rows). The column is already an Ensembl id, not a symbol or UniProt accession.

limitations.text: Null on 1,569 rows means upstream gene resolution returned nothing.
The 51 unresolved genes are the release's own resolution gap, so the target edge dangles for those rows rather than inventing a target.

claims.text: The Sequence Ontology accession of the variant's consequence in the row's gene context, in the release's underscore spelling SO_0001583.

frames.text: 21 distinct accessions on 22,362 rows; SO_0002073 (no sequence alteration) is the commonest with 7,191, ahead of intron (5,374) and missense (5,046).

limitations.text: Null on 11,117 rows: every haplotype-anchored row plus rsID-anchored rows with no consequence term.
The term describes the variant read in the row's gene, not the variant alone, and it is not joined to a SO term node by this layer.

claims.text: Whether the row's gene is a mechanism-of-action target of a drug in the row; computed by the build, not curated by ClinPGx.

frames.text: True on 1,612 rows and false on 31,867; no nulls.

limitations.text: Never null. False is not evidence of absence: an unmapped drug id, a null gene id or a drug with no mechanism row also give false.

The test runs per drug inside the row's array, so a multi-drug row where only one drug matches splits into two rows. It says nothing about whether the drug acts through the gene in the annotated phenotype.

nodes.description: One ClinPGx clinical annotation as the release publishes it.

claims.text: One pharmacogenomic clinical annotation: a statement that a genotype or haplotype changes a drug's behaviour for one gene, curated under one phenotype category and graded by ClinPGx. It is the release's pharmacogenomics row, not a study, a variant or a drug label.

studyId|genotype|variantId|variantFunctionalConsequenceId|targetFromSourceId|pgxCategory|phenotypeText|phenotypeFromSourceId|drug set: 33,479 nodes for 33,479 rows. studyId alone is not the key: it is the ClinPGx clinical-annotation accession with 5,190 distinct values and up to 270 rows each, because one annotation fans out over genotypes, phenotypes and drugs. All nine parts are needed: dropping studyId leaves 32,551 distinct keys, phenotypeText 29,503, the drug set 26,558, targetFromSourceId 24,997, genotype 23,929, pgxCategory 32,495, variantId 33,366, variantFunctionalConsequenceId 33,473 and phenotypeFromSourceId 33,471. The drug set is the sorted drugId|drugFromSource pairs of the row. genotypeId, variantRsId and haplotypeId do not discriminate further and stay properties.
The node is keyed by the annotation's subject plus its fan-out axes.

frames.text: pgxCategory is the curated role of the phenotype (toxicity, efficacy, metabolism/pk, dosage, other, pd). directionality is the allele-function label of the genotype, not the direction of the drug response. evidenceLevel grades the whole annotation on ClinPGx's scale, 1A highest and 4 meaning the evidence does not support the association. phenotypeText is the drug-response phrase, and phenotypeFromSourceId is the disease accession the release mapped it to. isDirectTarget is build-computed: true when the gene is a mechanism-of-action target of a drug in the row. variantId is derived by the build from genotypeId, not supplied by ClinPGx.

limitations.text: Nulls are source gaps with different causes: phenotypeFromSourceId is null on 32,755 rows (the label lookup matched nothing, although phenotypeText is still present on 31,625 of them), variantId on 17,310 (the 9,548 haplotype-anchored rows plus 7,762 rsID-anchored genotypes that reduce to the reference), variantRsId on 9,548, variantFunctionalConsequenceId on 11,117, directionality on 26,453, targetFromSourceId on 1,569, haplotypeId on 23,931 and phenotypeText on 1,130.

studyId is ClinPGx's annotation accession and joins to no row of the release's study dataset (0 of the 5,190 values occur there): the shared name is a collision. genotypeId is a genotype spelling (chr_pos_ref_allele1,allele2), not a variant id, and one genotype can name two variants. variantAnnotation (47,749 elements, 1-80 per row, 10,288 distinct ids) stays in the source: it holds the per-publication variant statements and is not a graph relation here. genotypeAnnotationText is ClinPGx's sentence for the genotype; phenotypeText is the release's phrase cut from it on 29,818 of the 32,349 non-null rows and different from it on 2,531, so it is neither always the source sentence nor a ClinPGx term, and never a controlled vocabulary. An annotation grades evidence; it is not a prescription, a dose recommendation or a clinical guideline.
The number of PGX_ANNOTATION nodes is the number of ClinPGx clinical annotations, or of variant annotations.
evidenceLevel is ClinPGx's grade of the annotation.
A level-1A annotation is a clinical guideline recommendation, or a level-3 annotation is an unscored record.
phenotypeFromSourceId is a sparse mapped disease term.
A null phenotypeFromSourceId means the annotation states no drug-response phenotype.

nodes.name: prioritisation_profile

claims.text: The release's membrane-localisation flag for the target.

frames.text: 1 on 4,195 profiles, 0 on 14,828 and null on 59,710.

limitations.text: Null means the release did not assess localisation, not that the target is not membrane-bound.
An integer flag, not a boolean: null is unassessed and must not be coerced to false. It summarises localisation evidence and is not a measured topology.

claims.text: The release's secreted-protein flag for the target.

frames.text: 1 on 1,991 profiles, 0 on 17,032 and null on 59,710.

limitations.text: Null means the release did not assess secretion, not that the target is intracellular.
An integer flag with an unassessed state; not a measured secretion assay.

claims.text: Whether the target has at least one target_safety_event row. The column is encoded as -1 and never as 1 or 0.

frames.text: Exactly 954 profiles carry -1 and 77,779 are null; those 954 are exactly the 954 targets with a target_safety_event row, so -1 is the release's true.

limitations.text: Null means the target has no safety event in the release, not that it was assessed and cleared.
Read -1 as present, not as a missing-value code or a negative assessment. The flag hides event identity, direction, dosing and source, which are on the HAS_SAFETY_EVENT edges.

claims.text: Whether the target has a high-quality small-molecule pocket in the tractability assessment.

frames.text: 1 on 982 profiles, 0 on 17,887 and null on 59,864; it reproduces the tractability bucket SM/High-Quality Pocket exactly.

limitations.text: Null means no tractability assessment, not the absence of a pocket.
A summary of one tractability bucket, not structural evidence; the bucket value stays on the HAS_TRACTABILITY edge.

claims.text: Whether the target has a high-quality small-molecule ligand in the tractability assessment.

frames.text: 1 on 2,352 profiles, 0 on 16,517 and null on 59,864; it reproduces the tractability bucket SM/High-Quality Ligand exactly.

limitations.text: Null means no tractability assessment, not the absence of a ligand.
A roll-up of one bucket, not a measured binding affinity.

claims.text: Whether the target has a small-molecule binder in the tractability assessment.

frames.text: 1 on 3,047 profiles, 0 on 15,822 and null on 59,864; it reproduces the tractability bucket PR/Small Molecule Binder exactly.

limitations.text: Null means no tractability assessment, not the absence of a binder.
A roll-up of one bucket; it does not say the binder is potent, selective or safe.

claims.text: The release's signed genetic-constraint score for the target.

frames.text: Continuous in [-1, 1]; 18,245 distinct values, 9,121 negative, null on 60,488 profiles.

limitations.text: Null means no constraint metric, not an unconstrained gene.

The release does not state which constraint family (mis, lof, syn) or which signed statistic it summarises; the per-family metrics are on the HAS_CONSTRAINT edges. The single -1.0 value cannot be told apart from a real extreme score.

claims.text: The release's maximum identity among the target's paralogues. The field is described as a percentage but is stored as a sign-flipped fraction.

frames.text: Negative fractions in [-1, 0]: -0.997265 means 99.7% identity, 0.0 means no identity and -1.0 occurs on 676 profiles. Null on 57,861.

limitations.text: Null means no homolog data, not the absence of a paralogue.

The sign and scale are release artefacts: the stored values are negative fractions, not the 0-100 percentage the field description names, and they do not reproduce homology.queryPercentageIdentity (median gap 31.5 percentage points over 20,872 targets). The meaning of -1.0 is unresolved.

claims.text: The release's maximum identity between the target and its mouse orthologue, stored as a positive fraction rather than the percentage its description names.

frames.text: Continuous in [0, 1], 0.0 on 7,018 profiles, null on 59,481.

limitations.text: Null means no mouse orthologue was assessed; 0.0 is a measured zero.

The opposite sign convention to paralogMaxIdentityPercentage in the same row, and also not the percentage its description names. It does not reproduce homology identity (mean gap 47 percentage points), so it is a Target Engine input, not a homology value.

claims.text: Whether the target is a cancer driver gene. The column is encoded as -1 and never as 1 or 0.

frames.text: Exactly 336 profiles carry -1 and 78,397 are null. 332 of the 336 are targets in evidence_cancer_gene_census; 4 are not, so the flag also has an input outside that dataset.

limitations.text: Null means the release does not call the target a cancer driver gene; it is not an assessed negative.
Read -1 as present. The flag collapses the census's driver role, direction and tumour types, which are on the evidence layer.

claims.text: The release's mouse knockout score for the target.

frames.text: Continuous in [-0.994, 0], 9,224 negative, null on 66,864 profiles; 0.0 is the maximum.

limitations.text: Null means no knockout data was scored, not a score of zero.
The release does not state the sign convention or the phenotype scale, so a more negative value cannot be read as stronger evidence from this column alone.

claims.text: Whether the target has at least one high-quality chemical probe.

frames.text: 1 on 516 profiles, 0 on 160 and null on 78,057; it reproduces chemical_probe.isHighQuality on exactly 516 targets.

limitations.text: Null means no probe record, not that no high-quality probe exists.
A presence flag; probe identity, scores and origin stay on the HAS_CHEMICAL_PROBE edges.

claims.text: The release's score derived from the highest clinical stage any molecule against the target has reached.

frames.text: Ordinal fractions 0.01, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.5, 0.7 and 1.0 on 1,552 profiles and null on 77,181. 1.0 covers 1,075 profiles.

limitations.text: Null means no clinical assessment for the target, not stage zero.

The release describes it as a score derived from the highest stage reached for any indication, not as a stage: it publishes no labels behind the fractions, and they are not probabilities. It is a target-level roll-up across molecules, not an approval for an indication.

claims.text: The Target Engine's tissue-specificity score for the target.

frames.text: Continuous in [-0.907, 1.0], 15,409 negative, null on 22,970 profiles.

limitations.text: Null means no expression-based score, not that the target is broadly expressed.
A Target Engine roll-up over expression sources; it is not the per-context baseline_expression specificity_score and the two are not on a common scale.

claims.text: The Target Engine's tissue-distribution score for the target.

frames.text: 119 distinct values: fractions in (0, 1] plus -1.0 on 10,010 profiles, null on 22,970.

limitations.text: Null means no expression-based score, not zero distribution.
The release does not state what -1.0 encodes; it is not a fraction and must not be averaged with the positive values.

claims.text: The Target Engine's cell-type-specificity score for the target.

frames.text: Continuous in [-0.920, 1.0], 13,696 negative, null on 35,623 profiles.

limitations.text: Null means no cell-type expression score, not that the target is ubiquitous.
A Target Engine roll-up, not the per-context baseline_expression specificity_score and not comparable with it.

claims.text: The Target Engine's cell-type-distribution score for the target.

frames.text: 171 distinct values: fractions in (0, 1] plus -1.0 on 957 profiles, null on 35,623.

limitations.text: Null means no cell-type expression score, not zero distribution.
The release does not state what -1.0 encodes; it is not a fraction and must not be averaged with the positive values.

nodes.description: The Target Engine's per-target prioritisation feature vector.

claims.text: One target's prioritisation profile: the Target Engine's computed feature vector over tractability, safety, constraint, homology, clinical stage, chemical probes and expression specificity. It is a derived summary of the target, not an independent entity.
target_prioritisation.targetId: 78,733 rows and 78,733 distinct ids, exactly one profile per target in the release, all resolving to a TargetNode.

frames.text: The attributes sit on a node rather than on the edge because the row identifies only the target: an edge carrying them would need a second endpoint and would degenerate to a target self-loop the release does not state. The node gives the attribute bag an address, is total over the 78,733 targets, and keeps 17 computed columns out of TARGET; it carries no fact that is independent of its target.

limitations.text: No node means the release computed no profile for that target; none occur in 26.09, where the profile covers all 78,733 targets. A null attribute is the feature not being computed, not a negative value.

There is no evidence trail: the profile is the release's computed roll-up, and its inputs are the tractability, safety, essentiality, probe and baseline-expression datasets, which are separate graph layers. Values must not be treated as independent facts about the target, and the negative sentinels (-1) are not measurements; see each property. 59,710 targets have no isInMembrane or isSecreted value and 77,779 have no hasSafetyEvent value.
A prioritisation profile is the Target Engine's derived vector for one target.
The profile is an independent assessment, evidence, or a ranking produced by this graph.

nodes.name: protein

claims.text: The namespace that issued the protein identifier.
One component of the node key (source, identifier).

frames.text: Observed values are ensembl_PRO, uniprot_swissprot, uniprot_trembl and uniprot_obsolete.

limitations.text: The release's proteinIds array never carries a null source.
The value is a namespace label, not a database version or release date.

claims.text: The protein accession in the namespace named by source.
One component of the node key (source, identifier).

frames.text: Use together with source; an accession alone does not name a record.

limitations.text: The release's proteinIds array never carries a null identifier.
Retired UniProt accessions are kept under uniprot_obsolete and do not resolve to a current UniProt entry.

nodes.description: A protein identifier that the target gene maps to.

claims.text: A protein-record identifier listed for a target: a current UniProt accession, a retired UniProt accession, or an Ensembl protein id. It names a protein record, not the gene that encodes it.
(source, identifier), written source:identifier. One node per identifier in the namespace named by source.

frames.text: source separates current UniProt entries from retired ones and from Ensembl protein ids. identifier is the accession as the release spells it; the same string under two sources is two identifiers.

limitations.text: A target with no protein edge is a gene for which the release lists no protein identifier; it is not evidence that the gene encodes no protein.
