A protein identifier is not a structure, an isoform function or proof of expression. One gene can map to several protein identifiers, and a retired accession does not resolve to a current entry.

nodes.name: regulatory_element

claims.text: GRCh38 chromosome label of the interval, without a chr prefix.

frames.text: Categorical string; 1-22, X, Y and MT style labels as the release writes them.

limitations.text: Never null.
Not sortable numerically as text and not an Ensembl region name.

claims.text: Lowest one-based GRCh38 coordinate of the interval.

frames.text: Base pairs; always less than end. Interval length is 501-6,637 bp.

limitations.text: Never null.
One-based inclusive coordinates, not a BED half-open interval.

claims.text: Highest one-based GRCh38 coordinate of the interval.

frames.text: Base pairs; read with chromosome and start.

limitations.text: Never null.
One-based inclusive, not a BED end.

claims.text: The E2G model's classification of where the interval sits relative to the linked gene.

frames.text: Three values: promoter, genic, intergenic. Promoter rows always have distanceToTss 0.

limitations.text: Never null.
A model label, not an ontology term and not a validated promoter or enhancer call.

claims.text: The datasource's evidence score for the element-gene link; the release states that higher values indicate stronger support.

frames.text: Continuous in [0.6, 1.0] in 26.09.

limitations.text: Never null.
A within-model score, not a probability, an effect size or a validated interaction. Scores from different studies in the same biosample are separate predictions and are not merged by this node.

claims.text: Distance in base pairs from the interval to the linked gene's transcription start site, as a non-negative magnitude.

frames.text: 0 for every promoter row; up to 55,760,344 for intergenic rows. No negative value occurs, so the sign is not in the data.

limitations.text: Never null.
Because the sign is absent, the value cannot tell an upstream from a downstream element; use the coordinates against the gene's strand.

claims.text: The release's datasource for the prediction.

frames.text: One value in 26.09: E2G.

limitations.text: Never null.
The dataset has no other contributor, so the property carries no discrimination today.

claims.text: The ENCODE accession of the experiment that produced the prediction.

frames.text: 1,439 distinct ENCFF accessions; up to 39,800 rows each.

limitations.text: Never null and never empty.
An ENCODE experiment accession is not an Open Targets studyId; it joins nothing in the genetics layer.

claims.text: The component names of the model's resourceScore array, in array order.

frames.text: Always exactly two elements in the order [DNase, HiC_contacts] on all 48,808,491 rows.

limitations.text: A graph property cannot hold an array of structs, so the scores are split into two parallel arrays; resourceScoreName[i] belongs to resourceScoreValue[i] and neither array may be sorted alone.

claims.text: The values of the model's resourceScore array, in array order.

frames.text: Two values per row and never null: DNase in [0.30001, 1.0], HiC_contacts in [0.000355, 0.95732].

limitations.text: Positional pairing with resourceScoreName is the only reading the release supports; the release does not state which component drives the link score.

claims.text: The source's quality-control flags for the prediction.

frames.text: An empty array on all 48,808,491 rows, so it never qualifies a node.

limitations.text: Never null; present and empty.
An empty array records that no QC flag was attached, not that the prediction passed a threshold.

nodes.description: One ENCODE E2G prediction linking a regulatory interval to a gene.

claims.text: A regulatory interval as the release's E2G model reports it for one biosample and one study, with the gene it is predicted to regulate. It is a prediction record, not a validated enhancer or promoter.

enhancer_to_gene.intervalId, a 32-hex-character hash: 48,808,491 rows carry 48,806,245 distinct ids, and the 2,246 repeated ids are exact duplicate rows. The id is not a genomic-interval id: 38,343,584 distinct (chromosome, start, end, biosampleId) intervals exist, and one interval linked to one gene recurs once per study (up to 255 times for one such interval). Read the node as the release's element-gene-study record.

frames.text: chromosome, start and end are GRCh38 coordinates in the release's own spelling (no chr prefix). intervalType is the model's classification of the interval: promoter (24,407,590 rows), genic (13,257,251) or intergenic (11,143,650). score is the E2G link score; distanceToTss is a non-negative distance to the gene's TSS, zero for every promoter row. The gene is the REGULATES edge, the biosample and publication are separate edges.

limitations.text: No node means no E2G prediction for that interval in this release. A gene absent from this node set has no predicted element in the 322 covered biosamples.

The node is biosample- and study-specific: the same genomic interval and gene appear once per ENCODE study with the same coordinates and different scores, so counting nodes counts predictions, not elements. Only 20,088 targets have any prediction and only 322 biosamples are covered. Nothing here is a measured enhancer-gene interaction, a variant effect or a disease mechanism.
An intervalId is one study's element-gene prediction.
The graph contains 48.8M distinct regulatory elements, or that two nodes with the same coordinates are two elements.

nodes.name: safety_event

claims.text: The event text as the contributing datasource writes it.

frames.text: Free text: 1,459 distinct strings over 4,387 rows. The labels mix clinical events, assay readouts and model-organism observations.

limitations.text: Do not group by event text as if it were a MedDRA, HPO or EFO term. Identical strings from different datasources are not the same curated term; eventId is the accession where the source supplies one.

claims.text: The ontology accession the source supplies for the event, in underscore form such as HP_0001649 or MONDO_0005252.

frames.text: Present on 2,211 of 4,387 rows over 435 distinct accessions from eight prefixes: MONDO, HP, EFO, GO, NCIT, CHEBI, MP and OBA. The prefixes mix diseases, phenotypes, biological processes, a chemical and model-organism terms. The build carries the accession as a property and does not resolve it to a DiseaseNode or GO term.

limitations.text: Null on 2,176 rows, mostly ToxCast and ClinPGx, which name an event without an accession. A null id is a source gap, not a claim that the event has no ontology term.
The accessions are not filtered to the release's disease vocabulary, and the event string is not checked against the accession's label.

claims.text: The source that contributed the observation: a program, a study or a paper, for example ClinPGx, ToxCast, AOP-Wiki or Lynch et al. (2017).

frames.text: Nine values cover the 4,387 rows. ClinPGx (1,590) and Lynch et al. (2017) (1,341) supply most rows.

limitations.text: The values are not normalised across programmes or papers and do not name a release dataset. Two spellings of one source would be two datasources here.

claims.text: The PubMed id cited for the observation, as a decimal string.

frames.text: Non-null on 1,941 rows over 5 distinct PMIDs; every value is numeric. It is a citation attached to the observation, not a PublicationNode edge in this layer.

limitations.text: Null on 2,446 rows, which record a source page or program instead of a paper. A null citation is a source gap, not an uncited finding.
One PMID can back hundreds of rows; the field does not say which part of the paper supports the observation.

claims.text: The source page recorded for the observation.

frames.text: Non-null on 2,446 rows and null on 1,941. The value is also part of the node key, where null is written as the empty string.

limitations.text: A null url means the source supplied no page, not that no source exists.
A locator is not proof that the page supports the row. ToxCast reuses one page across many events and targets, so the url is not unique to an event.

nodes.description: One datasource's safety observation for one target.

claims.text: A safety observation row from target_safety_event: one datasource reporting that a target is associated with an event, with the source's event accession, citation and page where supplied.

targetId|event|datasource|eventId|url, with the empty string where eventId or url is null: 4,387 rows and 4,387 distinct keys. The target is part of the identity because each row is a target-specific observation, but it is not a property; the incoming HAS_SAFETY_EVENT edge carries it. (targetId, event, datasource) has only 4,337 distinct values, and adding eventId still gives 4,337: 31 repeated (target, event, datasource, eventId) groups, 15 of them with a null eventId, are separated only by url. eventId is null on 2,176 rows overall, and rows with both extra fields null still have distinct target, event and datasource triples.

frames.text: event is free text as the datasource writes it, not an ontology label. eventId, where present, is an accession in underscore form from several vocabularies (MONDO_, HP_, EFO_, GO_, NCIT_, CHEBI_, MP_, OBA_). datasource is the contributing source, not a release dataset. literature is a PubMed id as text. url is the source page.

limitations.text: No node means the release records no such observation for that target. A null eventId, literature or url is a source gap, not an empty event, citation or page.

The node is the observation, not a controlled event vocabulary: the same event text from the same datasource for another target is a different node, and two datasources writing the same clinical event are not merged. Two nodes can therefore share every stored property and differ only by their incoming target edge. Effects and biosamples are separate edges. studies is a documented limit: its 5,561 elements form 3,448 distinct description/name/type triples. name is null on 642 elements, carries an HP_, EFO_, MONDO_ or GO_ accession on 1,764, and free text (for example 'cyclophosphamide induced effect') on the rest; description is free text on 5,119; type is biochemical, cell-based, clinical or preclinical, with one null. The triple is not an identified study, so it produces no node or edge and stays in the source. Nothing here asserts causality, incidence, severity or a dose-response.

nodes.name: safety_event_effect

claims.text: The signed direction of the reported effect.

frames.text: Two values only: Activation/Increase/Upregulation (1,162 elements) and Inhibition/Decrease/Downregulation (1,187 elements).

limitations.text: The wording combines activation, increase and upregulation into one bucket; it does not distinguish pharmacology from physiology.

claims.text: The dosing context in which the effect was reported.

frames.text: acute (1,286 elements), general (560), chronic (61), developmental toxicity (36) or null (406).

limitations.text: Null means the source states no dosing context, not that dosing was zero.
The values are coarse context labels, not doses, schedules or exposures, and they are not ordered by severity.

nodes.description: One direction-and-dosing descriptor reported for a safety observation.

claims.text: An effect descriptor: the direction in which modulating the target is reported to change the event, together with the dosing context. It is a shared nine-value vocabulary, not an assay, study or measured effect.
direction|dosing, with the empty string where dosing is null: 9 distinct pairs over 2,349 array elements. direction is never null; dosing is null on 406 elements.
The nine descriptors are a closed vocabulary for this release.

frames.text: direction is one of two statements: Activation/Increase/Upregulation or Inhibition/Decrease/Downregulation. dosing is acute, general, chronic or developmental toxicity, or null.

limitations.text: No effect node means no effects element names the pair. A null dosing is a source gap, not a no-dose context.

The descriptor exists so that direction and dosing are not flattened into variable-length properties of the observation; it has no identity beyond the pair. direction describes the reported effect of modulating the target on the event, not the event's direction in a patient. dosing is a coarse context, not a dose, duration or exposure. The edge, not the node, ties a descriptor to an observation.
A descriptor is a curated ontology term.

nodes.name: so_term

claims.text: The SO term name copied verbatim, words joined by underscores.

frames.text: 2,612 distinct labels cover 2,620 rows; 8 labels cover two accessions each. Two labels contain a space and are not spaced prose.

limitations.text: Not a key: a label-to-id join can return two rows. One row carries the upstream placeholder '<new term>', which is a label but not a usable term name.

nodes.description: A Sequence Ontology term.

claims.text: A Sequence Ontology term used to describe a variant consequence.
so.id, the SO accession in colon form: 2,620 rows and 2,620 distinct ids from SO:0000000 to SO:3000000.

frames.text: The term names a consequence class; severity is not encoded by the term alone. Released consequence columns write the underscore form (SO_0001583), so a join must convert the separator.

limitations.text: A term absent from so is outside the release's SO subset. No id or label is null.

All 7,886,761 non-null variant.mostSevereConsequenceId values resolve here after SO_ becomes SO:; the conversion is required for every consequence join. A consequence edge names a predicted effect, not an observed functional assay.

nodes.name: study

claims.text: Study design: gwas or one of five molecular QTL classes, eqtl, pqtl, sqtl, tuqtl or sceqtl.

frames.text: Lower-case categorical code; it selects which other study fields are populated.

limitations.text: Never null; studies of unknown design are excluded upstream.
Not the full API enum and says nothing about trait, tissue or condition.

claims.text: Trait exactly as the source reported it, from a disease name to an opaque molecular feature id.

frames.text: Two kinds of value share the column, so read it with studyType.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Not the standardised trait; use traitFromSourceMappedIds for that.

claims.text: Source project collection that supplied the study metadata.

frames.text: Provenance handle, not an accession or a quality mark.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
The project's vintage or assay version is not encoded; do not infer quality from it alone.

claims.text: Title of the publication referencing the study, where the source supplied one.

frames.text: Raw title text that may still contain inline HTML.

limitations.text: Null on studies without GWAS-Catalog publication metadata, not a missing study.
Coverage is GWAS-Catalog-only, so it is not a literature index for the whole release.

claims.text: First author of the study's publication, as the source wrote it.

frames.text: Surname and initials text with mixed ordering conventions.

limitations.text: Null on studies without GWAS-Catalog publication metadata.
Not a stable author identifier and not available for molecular studies.

claims.text: Publication date of the study's paper, stored as YYYY-MM-DD text.

frames.text: Sortable in this form; the range includes genuinely old and future-dated records.

limitations.text: Null on studies without GWAS-Catalog publication metadata.
Not the study or evidence date; do not use it to compute novelty.

claims.text: Abbreviated journal name where the study's publication appeared.

frames.text: The source's own abbreviation, not a normalised journal name.

limitations.text: Null on studies without GWAS-Catalog publication metadata.
One journal can have several abbreviations, and no journal entity exists to join.

claims.text: Free-text account of the study's starting cohort, as reported by the source.

frames.text: Human-readable string that may be a cross-reference rather than a count.

limitations.text: Null when the source supplied no starting-cohort description.
Never parse it as the analysed sample size; use nSamples, nCases and nControls.

claims.text: Number of cases the study analysed, as a whole-study total.

frames.text: Count; zero is a real value, and it is read with nControls.

limitations.text: Null on non-GWAS rows and on GWAS rows without case counts.
Not an ancestry stratum; the interface may hide a genuine zero.

claims.text: Number of controls the study analysed, as a whole-study total.

frames.text: Count; zero is a real value, and it shares nulls with nCases.

limitations.text: Null on non-GWAS rows and on GWAS rows without control counts.
Not an ancestry stratum and not derivable from nSamples.

claims.text: Total number of samples tested in the study analysis.

frames.text: Count; the analysed total, not a case-control sum.

limitations.text: Null on a few GWAS rows where the source supplied no analysed total, not a zero-sample study.
It can be smaller than nCases plus nControls on some rows; never derive one from the others.

claims.text: Whether the source publishes summary statistics for the study.

frames.text: Boolean; true is a precondition for a statistics location and QC, not a usability guarantee.

limitations.text: Null only for studies split from one catalogue accession, where availability was never asserted.
True does not mean the statistics are analysable or that the study can be fine-mapped.

claims.text: Path or URL where the source publishes the study's summary statistics.

frames.text: Free-text URI whose scheme names the host.

limitations.text: Null when the release carried no source path, including many GWAS Catalog studies that do have statistics.
Not evidence that statistics are unavailable; read it with hasSumstats.

claims.text: Experimental condition of a molecular-QTL study, in the source's own label.

frames.text: Categorical stimulus and exposure shorthand; '+' marks combined stimulation and 'naive' means unstimulated.

limitations.text: Null on GWAS rows and some pQTL rows, where the design has no condition rather than a missing value.
No controlled vocabulary; do not treat the same label from two projects as the same experiment.

nodes.description: A GWAS or molecular QTL study in the release.

claims.text: One study record: a GWAS, eQTL, pQTL, sQTL or other molecular QTL analysis. A study is the unit that carries sample size, ancestry, publication metadata and the disease or trait it measures.
study.studyId. The id is unique in the release; a molecular QTL study is split by its target trait and biosample, so it is not the same unit as a publication.

frames.text: studyType separates GWAS from molecular QTL types. nCases/nControls apply to case-control designs; nSamples is the general sample count.

limitations.text: A null sample size or ancestry is missing release metadata, not a zero-sample study. A study absent here is outside the release.
A study is not a publication: several studies can share one PMID, and a study can have no PMID. Do not treat the study id as a publication id.

nodes.name: subcellular_location

claims.text: The localisation statement as free text, including topology and membrane-pass qualifiers.
First component of the node key.

frames.text: The string is not an accession; join to the ontology through termSL when a normalized term is needed.

limitations.text: The release's subcellularLocations array never carries a null location.
The same free-text location can differ from the ontology label in labelSL.

claims.text: The resource that reported the localisation statement.
One component of the node key.

frames.text: Observed values are uniprot, HPA_main, HPA_additional and HPA_extracellular_location.

limitations.text: The release's subcellularLocations array never carries a null source.
The resource is not a confidence level; the release supplies no score.

claims.text: The subcellular-location ontology accession assigned to the statement.
One component of the node key.

frames.text: termSL is often a broad term such as a cellular-component class while location carries the specific text.

limitations.text: Null when the release did not map the statement to an ontology term.
A shared termSL does not make two statements the same localisation.

claims.text: The label of the ontology term named by termSL.
One component of the node key.

frames.text: Read it as the ontology label, not as a normalized form of location.

limitations.text: Null when termSL is null.
The label repeats across distinct free-text locations; do not group by it.

claims.text: The isoform qualifier the release attaches to the localisation, for example Isoform 2.
One component of the node key.

frames.text: Most statements have no modifier and apply to the gene product generally.

limitations.text: Null means the statement is not isoform-restricted in the release; it does not mean every isoform was tested.
The modifier is a release string, not a transcript or protein accession.

nodes.description: One subcellular-localisation statement listed for a target.

claims.text: A localisation statement reported for a target by UniProt or the Human Protein Atlas. The node is the statement, including its free-text topology qualifier and any isoform restriction.

subcellular_location::location::source::termSL::labelSL::targetModifier, with the empty string for a null component. The same location is reported by several sources and isoforms, so the source and modifiers are part of the identity.

frames.text: location is the free-text statement; termSL and labelSL map it to the release's subcellular-location ontology. targetModifier names an isoform when the statement applies to one isoform only.

limitations.text: A target with no location edge has no localisation statement in the release; it is not evidence that the protein has no location.
Localisation is a reported observation, not a measurement made by this release. A free-text location can include membrane-pass and topology qualifiers that termSL does not capture.

nodes.name: synonym

claims.text: The synonym string as the release spells it.
Last component of the node key.

frames.text: Case and punctuation are as supplied; there is no normalization.

limitations.text: The release's three synonym arrays never carry a null label.
Two targets can share a label; the node is a vocabulary entry, not a target.

claims.text: The synonym array that supplied the string.
One component of the node key.

frames.text: synonym is the general synonym list, symbolSynonym an alternative gene symbol and nameSynonym an alternative gene name.

limitations.text: Every synonym edge names one kind.
The kinds are release fields, not an ontology of synonym scopes.

claims.text: The vocabulary that supplied the synonym.
One component of the node key.

frames.text: Observed values are HGNC, uniprot and NCBI_entrez.

limitations.text: The release's three synonym arrays never carry a null source.
The source is not a confidence or an indication that the name is official.

nodes.description: One synonym string, in one synonym kind and source.

claims.text: A name or symbol the release lists for a target, qualified by the kind of synonym array it came from and the vocabulary that supplied it.
synonym::kind::source::label. The same string can occur in several kinds or sources and remains a distinct node.

frames.text: kind is the array that carried the string: synonym, symbolSynonym or nameSynonym. source names the vocabulary (HGNC, uniprot, NCBI_entrez).

limitations.text: A synonym absent here was not listed for any target in the release; it may still be an accepted name elsewhere.
A synonym is a naming fact. It does not mean the string is approved, current or unique to one target; obsolete symbols are a separate field.

nodes.name: target_class

claims.text: The release's numeric identifier for a target-class node.
One component of the node key, with label and level.

frames.text: The same id appears at several levels with different labels, so it must not be used as a class identifier on its own.

limitations.text: The release's targetClass array never carries a null id.
The id is internal to the release and is not an ontology accession.

claims.text: The class name at this hierarchy level.
One component of the node key.

frames.text: Read the label together with level; the same label can recur at other levels.

limitations.text: The release's targetClass array never carries a null label.
A label is not unique across levels or releases; do not join on it alone.

claims.text: The hierarchy tier of the class, written l1 to l6.
One component of the node key.

frames.text: l1 is the root tier; higher numbers are more specific classes.

limitations.text: The release's targetClass array never carries a null level.
The tiers are the release's own depth labels, not ontology ranks.

nodes.description: One node of the release's target-classification hierarchy.

claims.text: A node in the release's target-classification tree: a class label at one hierarchy level, with the release's numeric class id.
target_class::id::label::level. The numeric id is reused across levels with different labels, so the id alone is not the identity.

frames.text: level is the hierarchy tier (l1 to l6). A gene carries one edge per ancestor class from the most specific tier up to the root.

limitations.text: A target with no class edge is unclassified in the release, not classless in biology.
The classification is a curated descriptor for target assessment. It is not a functional assay, a protein family membership proof or a drug tractability claim.

nodes.name: tractability_bucket

claims.text: The drug-modality code the assessment applies to.

limitations.text: The codes are abbreviations whose expansions the release does not define in this dataset; do not infer them from the letters.

claims.text: The tractability evidence axis the assessment applies to.

frames.text: Nineteen labels such as Approved Drug, Phase 1 Clinical, High-Quality Pocket, High-Quality Ligand and UniProt loc high conf. Each label is reported under a subset of the four modalities.

limitations.text: Labels are free-text source names, not a controlled vocabulary: 'High-Quality Pocket' and 'Med-Quality Pocket' are separate buckets, and a bucket does not imply the others.

nodes.description: One modality-by-category tractability assessment axis.

claims.text: A tractability bucket: one (modality, category) axis on which the release reports a yes/no assessment for a target.
modality|category: 28 buckets over 4 modality codes and 19 categories. Every one of the 18,869 assessed targets has exactly one row per bucket, 528,332 rows in total.
The bucket node exists so the modality and category vocabulary is shared instead of repeated on 528,332 edges.

frames.text: modality is the source code as written: AB, SM, PR, OC. category names the evidence axis, for example High-Quality Pocket, Approved Drug or UniProt loc high conf.

limitations.text: A bucket absent here is not an assessment axis in this release.

The release does not expand the modality codes in this dataset; do not read AB, SM, PR or OC as a spelled-out modality without external documentation. Bucket names are source labels, not a hierarchy, and they mix structural, localisation, ligand and clinical evidence.
The bucket is a measured property of a target.

nodes.name: transcript

claims.text: The transcript biotype from the release's annotation.

frames.text: protein_coding (278,455 rows) separates coding transcripts from lncRNA, nonsense_mediated_decay and other non-coding biotypes.

limitations.text: The label is the release's biotype vocabulary, not a functional assay.

claims.text: The ENSP translation identifier of the transcript.

frames.text: Read it together with biotype; a non-coding transcript has no translation.

limitations.text: Null for 273,406 of 644,292 transcripts; that is the release's annotation, not a zero-length protein.
The identifier names a translation, not a UniProt entry or a folded structure.

claims.text: Whether the release marks the transcript as the Ensembl canonical transcript of its gene.

frames.text: True on 78,733 transcripts, exactly one per target gene.

limitations.text: Canonical is an annotation choice; it does not establish expression, dominance or clinical relevance.

claims.text: The chromosome of the transcript's genomic span.

frames.text: Compare with the target's chromosome; a transcript lies on the gene's chromosome in this release.

claims.text: The transcript span's start coordinate on the chromosome.

frames.text: Coordinates are the release's chromosome coordinates; strand tells the direction. Do not compare them with another assembly without a liftover.

claims.text: The transcript span's end coordinate on the chromosome.

frames.text: start/end describe the transcript, not the encoded protein.

claims.text: The transcript's strand, 1 for forward and -1 for reverse.

frames.text: The value is an integer; in 26.09 it is 1 on 324,621 rows and -1 on 319,671.

limitations.text: Do not compare it with the '+'/'-' strings used by some other releases.

claims.text: The transcript's transcription start site coordinate.

frames.text: It is per transcript; the target node's tss is the gene-level canonical value.

limitations.text: A TSS coordinate is not a measured promoter or an active regulatory element.

nodes.description: A transcript annotated to a target gene.

claims.text: One transcript of a target gene: the release's transcript row, with its biotype, translation and genomic span. A transcript is a product of the gene, not the gene and not the protein.
transcript.transcriptId, the ENST accession. It is unique across the 644,292 transcript rows; the target is not part of the key.

frames.text: biotype is the transcript biotype. proteinId is the ENSP translation and is null for the 273,406 non-coding transcripts. isEnsemblCanonical is the Ensembl canonical choice; exactly one transcript per target is canonical. The transcript's target is the HAS_TRANSCRIPT edge, not a property.

limitations.text: A transcript absent here is outside the release's transcript set; it is not an unannotated isoform. A target with no transcript rows has no transcript annotation in the release.

The release carries flags (appris, gencode_primary, ensembl_canonical, mane) and 5,078,384 per-exon intervals as arrays on the transcript row. Only the canonical flag is published; the per-flag values and exon intervals stay in the source. A canonical transcript is the Ensembl choice, not a claim about the dominant isoform in a tissue.

edges.name: biosample_is_a
edges.description: A biosample's parent term.

claims.text: The child biosample is a subtype of, or otherwise classified under, the direct parent ontology class.
child biosampleId and parent biosampleId joined by '|': 64,085 edges over 32,752 child terms, with unique pairs.

frames.text: Direct parents only; a row has several parents when the class belongs to several ontology branches. 2,725 rows carry a null parents array, which does not distinguish an ontology root from a class whose parents the build dropped. 109 parent elements (19 distinct ids) name no biosample row and land on no node. 617 parent elements are full URLs, and parents cross ontology prefixes.

limitations.text: A parent is an ontology class, not a measured tissue or sample. The parents and children arrays are not exact inverses in this release: 6,907 parent edges have no reverse child entry and 963 child entries no reverse parent, so a down-walk and an up-walk disagree. ancestors and descendants stay in the source as precomputed closures and are not published as edges.

edges.name: clinical_trial_has_side_effect

properties.name: termFromSource
properties.description: The side-effect label the warning source wrote: the term's own label or, failing that, its warning class.

claims.text: The side-effect label the warning source wrote: the term's own label or, failing that, its warning class.

edges.description: A warning report names an adverse-event term.

claims.text: A drug-warning report names the adverse-event term as a side effect of its drug. One edge per report and term.
(clinical_report.id, sideEffects.diseaseId).

frames.text: termFromSource is the report's own wording for the term; the label varies in case across reports, which is why it sits on the edge and not on the node.

limitations.text: Only the 2,744 SAFETY reports carry this edge type; a report with no edge recorded no warning-derived side effect in the release.
A warning term is not a trial-observed adverse event and does not establish that the drug caused it. The term is not always a disease accession.

edges.name: clinical_trial_published_in

properties.name: referenceType
properties.description: The registry's role for the reference: BACKGROUND, DERIVED or RESULT.

claims.text: The registry's role for the reference: BACKGROUND, DERIVED or RESULT.

edges.description: A report cites a publication.

claims.text: The registry lists the publication under the study. One edge per report and PubMed id.
(clinical_report.id, trialLiterature.id).

frames.text: referenceType is the role the registry assigns the reference: BACKGROUND, DERIVED or RESULT. A report and PMID pair never occurs under two roles.

limitations.text: 204,952 of 289,954 reports cite nothing. 5,488 of 340,418 array elements carry no id and produce no edge.

The edge records a citation, not that the paper reports this study's result; BACKGROUND is the majority role (202,742 of 340,418 elements). Publication nodes come from literature_entity_lut: 231,944 of the 258,671 cited PMIDs have one, and the other edges name a PMID with no node in the graph.

edges.name: clinical_trial_studies_disease
edges.description: A report names a disease it studied, approved, withdrew or warned against.

claims.text: The report names the disease as a condition its drugs were studied, approved, withdrawn for or warned against. One edge per report and mapped disease.
(clinical_report.id, diseases.diseaseId).

frames.text: The edge is report-level: a report naming two diseases yields two edges, with no claim about which drug belongs to which disease. 1,944 duplicate array pairs collapse to one edge.

limitations.text: A report with no edge here named no disease the release could map: 79,872 of 360,046 array elements have a null id, and 21,983 reports have the container withdrawn whole.
The disease label the source used is not carried, only the mapped accession. The edge does not say the trial succeeded, that a drug is effective, or which drug-disease pair the report supports.

edges.name: clinical_trial_studies_molecule
edges.description: A report names a molecule it studies, labels or warns about.

claims.text: The report names the molecule as an intervention, the subject of a label, or the target of a warning. One edge per report and resolved drug id.
(clinical_report.id, drugs.drugId).

frames.text: Drug ids are resolved by the release from the source name, so the edge exists only where resolution succeeded. 2,435 duplicate array pairs collapse to one edge.

limitations.text: 78,746 of 459,471 array elements carry no drug id; those names are not nodes and produce no edge, and the report is not drug-free.
Do not count edges as trials per drug: one report naming three drugs yields three edges. The edge is a mention, not an arm, a dose or an assignment.

edges.name: credible_set_colocalises_with

claims.text: The colocalisation method that produced the row.

frames.text: Only COLOC_PIP_ECAVIAR occurs in 26.09, so the property does not partition the edges.

limitations.text: Do not read the value as a comparison of methods; a future release may ship several.

claims.text: The colocalisation posterior probability for the pair.

frames.text: Values run from 3.7e-10 to 1.0; higher means stronger evidence of a shared signal.

limitations.text: It is model output under the release's priors, not a direct measurement or a replication.

claims.text: The posterior probability that the two sets have two distinct causal variants.

frames.text: Read h3 against h4: h3 high with h4 low argues against a shared variant.

limitations.text: The hypotheses are model-defined and their priors are not on the edge.

claims.text: The posterior probability that the two sets share one causal variant.

frames.text: h4 is the hypothesis behind the colocalisation claim; it is not a probability that a specific variant is causal.

limitations.text: A high h4 does not identify the shared variant; the membership edges do not carry that identity.

claims.text: The average sign of the beta ratio across the colocalising variants.

frames.text: Its sign indicates whether the two studies' effects point the same way.

limitations.text: An average sign is not an effect size and does not test for a shared direction.

claims.text: The number of variants in the shared signal.

frames.text: Measured 1-3,077; larger values mean a wider shared signal.

limitations.text: A count of variants is not a count of independent causal variants.

claims.text: The chromosome of the colocalising locus.

frames.text: Measured equal to both endpoint credible sets' chromosome on every row.

limitations.text: It is a locus-level fact, not a claim about a specific variant.

claims.text: The study type of the right credible set.

frames.text: 26.09 values are gwas, eqtl, sqtl, tuqtl, pqtl and sceqtl; measured equal to the right credible set's studyType on every row. The left set's study type is not supplied on the row.

limitations.text: It describes the right endpoint only; do not read it as the type of the pair.

edges.description: A colocalisation between two credible sets.

claims.text: A colocalisation the release reports between a left and a right credible set: evidence that the two loci share a causal variant under the release's colocalisation method.

(leftStudyLocusId, rightStudyLocusId, colocalisationMethod). The release ships one method (COLOC_PIP_ECAVIAR) and 0 duplicate pair+method rows over 283,303,467 rows. The pair is also unique and no row exists in the reverse orientation, so left and right are the release's roles, not an arbitrary ordering.

frames.text: clpp is the colocalisation posterior probability. h3 is the posterior probability of two distinct causal variants and h4 of one shared variant. betaRatioSignAverage is the average sign of the beta ratio and is null on 119,431,152 rows. rightStudyType names the right set's study type; the release supplies no left study type. numberColocalisingVariants counts variants in the shared signal.

limitations.text: No edge means the release reports no colocalisation for the pair under the method it ships. Both endpoints resolve to credible sets in 26.09.

283,303,467 edges, the largest relation in this graph; carrying it in full is a deliberate scale decision and dominates the build. A single method means the method property cannot discriminate. Colocalisation is not proof of a shared causal variant: h3 can exceed h4, and clpp is model output. The relation is stored left->right and has no reciprocal rows, so undirected queries must traverse both directions.

edges.name: credible_set_contains_variant

claims.text: The probability the variant belongs to the credible set under the release's fine-mapping.

frames.text: Values run from 5.4e-06 to 1.0; a value is per variant and per set.

limitations.text: It is a membership probability, not the probability that the variant is causal.

claims.text: The variant's log Bayes factor for belonging to the credible set.

frames.text: Larger supports inclusion more strongly.

limitations.text: Null on 24,500,428 of 110,940,745 elements.
Log Bayes factors are not comparable across studies with different priors and models.

claims.text: The study's effect-size estimate for the variant.

frames.text: The scale and effect allele are study-specific; read it with the study and credible set.

limitations.text: Null on 23,813,059 elements.
A beta from one study is not an effect on a target or a disease in general.

claims.text: The standard error of the variant's beta.

frames.text: Use it with beta; it is not a confidence interval.

limitations.text: Null on 15,809,462 elements.
It inherits the study's model and sample size; it is not comparable across studies.

claims.text: The mantissa of the variant's association p-value, p = mantissa x 10^exponent.

frames.text: Read it with pValueExponent; neither part is meaningful alone.

limitations.text: Null on 32,391,750 elements.
A p-value is not an effect size and does not establish causality.

claims.text: The base-10 exponent of the variant's association p-value.

frames.text: Negative values are the usual case; use it only with pValueMantissa.

limitations.text: Null on 32,391,750 elements, always together with pValueMantissa.
Do not compare exponents across studies as a strength ranking without the mantissa.

claims.text: The variant's overall LD r² to the credible set's lead variant.

frames.text: Measured 0.50-1.0 where present, so these are variants in LD with the lead.

limitations.text: Null on 86,440,317 of 110,940,745 elements; a null r² is not zero LD.
r² depends on the study's LD reference population; it is not a functional similarity.

edges.description: A variant's membership in a credible set.

claims.text: One variant's membership in a fine-mapped credible set, carrying the variant-level statistics the release reports for that membership.

(studyLocusId, variantId). The pair is unique for every membership whose variant exists in the release (0 duplicates over 110,939,251 resolvable rows). 21 pairs occur more than once (27 rows), all for three symbolic <DEL> variant ids that have no VARIANT node.

frames.text: posteriorProbability is the variant's membership probability inside the set, not a causal probability outside it. beta and standardError are the study's effect estimate, and pValueMantissa/pValueExponent encode the p-value. r2Overall is LD r² to the set's lead variant and is absent for most rows.

limitations.text: No edge means the variant is not in that credible set. 1,494 membership rows name 651 variant ids with no VARIANT node (630 symbolic structural-variant alleles and 21 alt-contig coordinates), so those edges dangle.

110,940,745 edges; membership is a statistical set, not a causal claim. A variant can be in several sets, and the same set's lead variant is a separate edge. Null statistics are release gaps: logBF is null on 24,500,428 rows, beta on 23,813,059, standardError on 15,809,462, the p-value on 32,391,750 and r2Overall on 86,440,317.

edges.name: credible_set_lead_variant
edges.description: The lead variant of a credible set.

claims.text: The credible set's lead variant, the variant with the highest posterior probability.
studyLocusId -> variantId.

frames.text: Every credible set names exactly one lead variant in this release.

limitations.text: The lead variant is a summary of the set, not a causal variant and not the only member. Membership edges are separate.

edges.name: association
edges.description: An aggregate relation the release reports over evidence.

claims.text: An aggregate relation the release computes over evidence.
The concrete edge's endpoint pair and scope.

frames.text: Read the concrete edge for its scope and score meaning.

limitations.text: No edge means the release reports no aggregate at that scope.
An aggregate is not a direct observation and is not causal.

edges.name: predicts_target

claims.text: L2G model's estimate that the credible set's causal gene is this target.

frames.text: Probability-like value from 0 to 1; predictions below 0.05 are not published.

limitations.text: Never null; a missing pair was filtered below 0.05 or was never a candidate.
A prediction, not association strength or experimental causation, and not comparable across releases.

claims.text: SHAP baseline for the L2G prediction, the model value with no feature information.

frames.text: Model baseline; the per-feature SHAP contributions add to it in reaching the score.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
One of a small discrete set, constant within a study-locus; not a locus fingerprint or a confidence.

edges.description: A Locus-to-Gene prediction from a credible set to a target.

claims.text: The L2G model's prediction that the credible set's causal gene is the target. One edge per credible set-target pair.
(studyLocusId, geneId).

frames.text: score is the model's probability-like output; shapBaseValue is the model baseline. The features behind the score are model explanations, not evidence.

limitations.text: No edge means the model made no prediction for the pair, not that the gene is not in the locus.
L2G is a prediction, not an observed mechanism. A high score is not experimental evidence and does not establish causality.

edges.name: has_cross_reference
edges.description: An entity carries an external identifier.

claims.text: The source entity lists the target identifier in its cross-references.
(entity, source, identifier).

frames.text: Read the edge from the entity to the identifier.

limitations.text: No edge means the release did not list that identifier for the entity.
The edge asserts a listed identifier, not that two entities are the same or that the external record was verified in this release.

edges.name: disease_has_cross_reference
edges.description: An external identifier listed in a disease term's cross-references.

claims.text: The disease term's record lists the external identifier.
disease -> source:identifier, keyed disease::HAS_CROSS_REFERENCE::source:identifier. The 127,496 elements are 127,496 distinct pairs within a term.

frames.text: source is the part before the first colon (PMID, UMLS, MEDGEN, GARD, DOID, Orphanet, SCTID, OMIM, MESH, NCIT, ICD9, icd11.foundation, uniprot, EFO, NANDO and others); identifier is the remainder, which may itself contain separators.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no such identifier for the term. A value without a colon cannot name a namespace: one element (EFO_0020991, the sentence 'Quantification of ethanolamine in a sample.') is kept with that sentence as source and an empty identifier rather than dropped.

The edge asserts a listed identifier, not that the external record was verified or describes the same concept. Namespace spelling differs across datasets (NCIT beside NCIt, Orphanet beside ORPHA), so the same authority can yield several nodes.

edges.name: disease_has_obsolete_cross_reference
edges.description: A retired external identifier listed in a disease term's cross-references.

claims.text: The disease term's record lists the external identifier as one it no longer uses.
disease -> source:identifier, keyed disease::HAS_OBSOLETE_CROSS_REFERENCE::source:identifier. The 24,527 elements are 24,207 distinct pairs; 320 pairs repeat within a term.

frames.text: A separate edge type keeps the retirement assertion: 12,183 pairs are listed both here and in dbXRefs for the same term, so one combined edge type could not carry both states without a qualifier that the shared cross-reference identity does not have.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no retired identifier. A retired identifier can still be the term's current identifier in the external namespace or in another term's dbXRefs.
Retirement is the release's assertion about its own mapping, not proof that the external record was withdrawn. The release names no replacement identifier.

edges.name: disease_has_obsolete_term
edges.description: A retired ontology accession listed by a disease term.

claims.text: The disease term lists the accession as one it has retired.
disease -> accession, keyed disease::HAS_OBSOLETE_TERM::accession. The 9,852 elements are 9,838 distinct pairs; 14 accessions repeat within a term.

frames.text: Verified resolution: none of the 9,852 elements is a disease.id or a disease_hpo.id, so the target is an ObsoleteTermNode rather than a DISEASE node; a DISEASE target would dangle on every element.

limitations.text: No edge means the term lists no retired accession.
The edge preserves a historical accession. It does not state that the retired term was merged, split or replaced by this term, and it cannot be traversed backwards to a current term.

edges.name: disease_has_phenotype

claims.text: The single-letter aspect code the release assigns to the evidentiary record.
A qualifier of the record, not part of the edge key.

frames.text: Observed values are P (199,385 records), I (10,728), C (10,684), M (112) and H (61).

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
The dataset ships no legend for the letters, so a category must not be inferred from the letter. The code describes the record, not the phenotype term.

claims.text: Curator identity and curation date of the source annotation.
One component of the edge key.

frames.text: Values pair a curator and a date in brackets, for example HPO:probinson[2012-05-01], HPO:iea[2009-02-17] or ORCID:0000-0002-0736-9199[2025-03-05]. 57,569 records list several curations in one semicolon-separated string, up to six; 23,799 records mention an ORCID.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
An ORCID names an annotator and an HPO:iea value marks an inferred electronic annotation; neither is a publication. The date is the curation date, not the observation date.

claims.text: Accession of the source disease record the annotation was curated from.
One component of the edge key.

frames.text: 220,685 records cite an OMIM accession and 285 a DECIPHER accession; one source record can support many phenotypes of one disease.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Not a disease.id join key: the values use OMIM and DECIPHER namespaces, and one release disease term can aggregate several source records. Use the edge's disease endpoint to reach the DISEASE node.

claims.text: Disease label as the source record spells it.
A qualifier of the record, not part of the edge key.

frames.text: Free text in the source's naming style, for example 'Megabladder, congenital' or 'Spermatogenic failure 93'.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
It is the source's name for the source record, not the preferred label of the edge's disease endpoint and not proof that the source concept is identical to the release term.

claims.text: HPO evidence code stating how the annotation was made.
A qualifier of the record, not part of the edge key.

frames.text: Three values occur: PCS (148,236 records), IEA (43,528) and TAS (29,206).

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
IEA marks an inferred electronic annotation and is not equivalent to a curated PCS assertion. The code is not a confidence score and the dataset does not define the abbreviations.

claims.text: Frequency of the phenotype in the disease as the source states it.
One component of the edge key; a null value is written as the empty string there and stays null on the edge.

frames.text: Two shapes occur: a ratio such as 1/14 or 3/3, and an HPO frequency term such as HP_0040283 (3,658 records). 88,055 records carry no frequency.

limitations.text: Null means the source stated no frequency, not a frequency of zero.
Ratios, HPO terms and free text are not comparable without a conversion the release does not carry. Frequency is the source's claim about the disease, not a measured cohort prevalence.

claims.text: HPO clinical-modifier accessions the source attaches to the annotation.
A qualifier of the record; the array is not part of the edge key.

frames.text: Values are colon-form HPO accessions such as HP:0012825. 1,360 records carry a modifier and 219,610 carry an empty array.

limitations.text: An empty array means no modifier was stated; it is the norm.
The colon form is not the underscore form used by disease_hpo ids, so these values do not key a PHENOTYPE node.

claims.text: HPO onset accessions the source attaches to the annotation.
One component of the edge key, joined with |; an empty array is an empty string there.

frames.text: Values are colon-form HPO accessions such as HP:0003577. 4,019 records carry an onset and 216,951 carry an empty array.

limitations.text: An empty array means no onset was stated, not an onset at birth.
The colon form is not the underscore form used by disease_hpo ids. One record can state several onsets, and their order is not meaningful.

claims.text: Free-text qualifier the source attaches to the annotation.
A qualifier of the record, not part of the edge key.

frames.text: Null on all 220,970 records in 26.09.

limitations.text: Null on every record, so the property carries no information in this release.
Do not read a null as 'no qualifier stated' as opposed to 'not populated': the release never populates the field, so both readings are indistinguishable.

claims.text: Whether the annotation asserts the negation of the phenotype.
A qualifier of the record, not part of the edge key.

frames.text: False on all 220,970 records in 26.09.

limitations.text: Never null; false is the only observed value.
A constant false says the release recorded no negated annotation, not that the phenotype was excluded by study design.

claims.text: Records cited for the annotation, one accession per element.
One component of the edge key, joined with |; the array is never empty.

frames.text: Values are PMID accessions with a minority of OMIM or other accessions; 208,467 records cite one record and the longest list holds 26.

limitations.text: Never null or empty in 26.09.
The citations are not resolved to publication nodes, and a cited record is not proof that it supports the annotation.

claims.text: Sex the annotation is restricted to.
A qualifier of the record, not part of the edge key.

frames.text: MALE on 683 records and FEMALE on 266; 220,021 records are null.

limitations.text: Null means the record states no sex restriction, not that both sexes were studied.
The vocabulary has two values and no unknown state; the release does not record how a mixed-sex cohort is represented.

claims.text: Dataset that supplied the annotation record.
A qualifier of the record, not part of the edge key.

frames.text: The value is HPO on all 220,970 records in 26.09.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Constant in this release, so it cannot separate records; it is not the source of the disease label, which is diseaseFromSource.

edges.description: One disease-to-phenotype evidence record.

claims.text: The disease term has the phenotype, as asserted by one evidence record of disease_phenotype. The edge is the record; the endpoint nodes are the disease and the phenotype.

disease -> phenotype, discriminated by the curating record and the assertion's own fields: disease::HAS_PHENOTYPE::phenotype::diseaseFromSourceId::bioCuration::frequency::onset::references, arrays joined with | and a null frequency written as the empty string. The tuple yields 178,888 distinct keys over 220,970 evidence elements, equal to the number of distinct full evidence tuples, so it separates every pair of non-identical records. 42,082 elements (19.0%) repeat an identical record for the same pair and collapse onto one key.

frames.text: One edge per evidence element, so the 163,973 disease-phenotype pairs expand to 220,970 edges; one pair (MONDO_0019588 - HP_0000007) carries 83, distinguished by source record. bioCuration names the curator and date (HPO:probinson[2012-05-01] or ORCID:...), diseaseFromSource(Id) the source disease record (OMIM or DECIPHER), frequency a ratio such as 1/14 or an HPO frequency term such as HP_0040283, and references the cited records.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no phenotype annotation for the pair. A null disease or phenotype cannot key an endpoint and drops the row; the release carries none. A null frequency stays null on the edge and is written as the empty string in the key.

22,759 of the 220,970 evidence elements (10.3%), which collapse to 18,325 of the 178,888 edges (10.2%), name one of 285 phenotype accessions absent from disease_hpo; every one is a MONDO or EFO disease term, so those edges point at no PHENOTYPE node and the disease-side term is reachable only through the DISEASE node of the same accession. An annotation is not a diagnosis, prevalence or causal claim, and frequency text is not a normalized proportion. diseaseName is not carried: it is a display variant of diseaseFromSource, differing on 189,979 records.

edges.name: disease_has_synonym
edges.description: A name listed for a disease term under one synonym class.

claims.text: The disease term is known by the name under the synonym class.
disease -> (kind, label), keyed disease::HAS_SYNONYM::kind::label. The 111,626 array elements are 111,626 distinct keys.

frames.text: The class is in the key, so the same label listed as exact and as broad produces two edges to two nodes.

limitations.text: No edge means the term lists no name in that class.
The edge is a naming fact and asserts neither equivalence with another term nor approval of the string. The release records no synonym source.

edges.name: disease_has_therapeutic_area
edges.description: Membership of a disease term in one therapeutic area.

claims.text: The disease term belongs to the therapeutic area named by the target term, as the release asserts in disease.therapeuticAreas.
disease -> area, keyed disease::HAS_THERAPEUTIC_AREA::area. The 71,009 array elements are 71,009 distinct pairs.

frames.text: Resolved choice: all 71,009 targets are disease-table rows, and every target is one of the 26 terms whose ontology.isTherapeuticArea is true, so the target is a DISEASE node and no separate therapeutic-area node type exists. The 26 areas include EFO, OTAR and MONDO grouping roots and GO_0008150 (biological_process); every one of the 45,896 terms carries at least one area and at most nine.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no area, which never happens in 26.09: every term has at least one. An area edge is not a disease classification and does not replace the IS_A hierarchy.

26 pairs are self-edges because an area lists itself; they carry no membership information beyond the term's own flag. The area is a release grouping root, not a clinical specialty, an indication or a body system, and the flag says nothing about whether the term is a disease.

edges.name: disease_is_a
edges.description: A direct parent of a disease term.

claims.text: The child disease term is a direct subtype of the parent term, as the release asserts in disease.parents.
child -> parent, keyed child::IS_A::parent. The 64,021 array elements over the 45,896 terms are 64,021 distinct pairs; 25 terms list no parent.

frames.text: One edge per listed parent, so a term with several parents carries several edges. Both ends are DISEASE nodes: the term set mixes EFO, MONDO, GO, HP, Orphanet and other accessions, so an edge can cross vocabularies.

limitations.text: No edge means the term lists no parent (25 terms) or is not in the release. The release does not distinguish a root from a term whose parents were left empty.

The release also ships children, ancestors and descendants. children is the exact inverse of parents (0 differences in either direction), and ancestors and descendants are the transitive closure of parents: a recursive walk reproduces all 401,908 ancestor pairs exactly, and descendants is the same set reversed. Those three arrays are not bound as edges, so parent edges are the only hierarchy edges and ancestors must be reached by traversal. A parent link is a classification, not causal, anatomical or temporal containment.

edges.name: drug_warning_has_reference
edges.description: The drug warning cites a document.

claims.text: The drug warning cites a document or record.
(drug_warning.id, references.source, references.id).

frames.text: Read warning -> reference. The url and namespace are on the reference node.

limitations.text: No edge means the warning's references array is empty.
Citing a document does not assert that the document supports every statement in the warning.

edges.name: evidence_cancer_biomarkers_has_disease
edges.description: The disease an evidence row is attributed to.

claims.text: The evidence row is attributed to this disease term. The edge is the resolved diseaseId, not the source label.
evidence id -> diseaseId; one edge per evidence row. 41,977,200 edges over the twenty sources.

frames.text: diseaseId resolves to disease.id on every row in all twenty sources. The disease is the release's term, not necessarily the source's original label.

limitations.text: No edge means the row had no diseaseId. This release has no such row in any source.
A disease term is not a patient cohort. The edge does not assert that the target causes the disease.

edges.name: evidence_cancer_biomarkers_has_molecule
edges.description: A molecule named by the evidence row.

claims.text: The evidence row names this ChEMBL molecule as the drug context for the target-disease assertion.
evidence id -> drugId; one edge per non-null drugId. 877,234 edges: 728 cancer-biomarker and 876,506 clinical-precedence rows.

frames.text: Every non-null drugId in both sources resolves to drug_molecule.id. cancer_biomarkers leaves drugId null on 573 rows where no released molecule matched the reported name.

limitations.text: No edge means the source stated no molecule id; it does not mean the assertion had no drug context.
The edge does not assert that the molecule treats the disease or that the trial succeeded. drugFromSource can be a drug class.

edges.name: evidence_cancer_biomarkers_has_target
edges.description: The target an evidence row is attributed to.

claims.text: The evidence row is attributed to this target. The edge is the resolved target, not the source symbol in targetFromSourceId.
evidence id -> targetId; one edge per evidence row. 41,977,200 edges over the twenty sources.

frames.text: targetId resolves to target.id on every row in all twenty sources. The edge records attribution; the evidence node carries the score and the source-specific context.

limitations.text: No edge means the row had no targetId. This release has no such row in any source.
The edge does not assert that modulating the target treats the disease, and it does not carry the source's direction or score.

edges.name: evidence_cancer_biomarkers_supported_by
edges.description: A publication the evidence row cites.

claims.text: The evidence row cites this publication, one edge per PMID element.
evidence id -> PMID; one edge per distinct non-empty literature element. 65,083,952 edges over the nineteen sources that carry a literature column.

frames.text: Null and empty PMID elements are dropped. The publication node is keyed by PMID from literature_entity_lut; an element whose PMID is absent from that file leaves a dangling edge, reported per source.

limitations.text: An evidence row with an empty literature array has no SUPPORTED_BY edge. clingen has no literature column at all.
A citation is not a verification of the source's claim. The edge does not carry the sentence, the section or the citation's role.

edges.description: A cell line the evidence assayed.

claims.text: The CRISPR evidence row was assayed in this cell line.
evidence id -> cell-line id; one edge per diseaseCellLines element. 18,556 edges over 517 rows.

frames.text: The key is diseaseCellLines.id (an SIDM id), which is non-null on every element. The release's CellLineNode is keyed by the DepMap depmapId (ACH), and 26.09 supplies no SIDM-to-ACH crosswalk, so all 18,556 edges are emitted but none resolves to a cell-line node.

limitations.text: No edge means the row named no cell line; this release has none. A cell line absent from the target-essentiality source has no node.

The edge does not assert that the screen succeeded or that the line is the disease's model. 5,774 of 18,556 elements also have no target_essentiality row with the same diseaseCellLineId, and the DepMap identity uses a different accession space.

edges.name: go_term_is_a
edges.description: A GO term's is-a parent.

claims.text: The child GO term is a subtype of the parent term.
child go.id and parent go.id joined by '|': 57,456 edges with 57,456 distinct pairs.

frames.text: One edge per direct is-a parent; several parents are GO's multiple inheritance. 38,089 live terms have at least one is-a parent and 3 live terms are roots. Every parent resolves to a go row, no term is its own parent, and no is-a edge crosses namespace.

limitations.text: An is-a parent is not an assertion that a gene annotated to the child is annotated to the parent; annotation inheritance is a separate inference. edges.name: go_term_negatively_regulates
edges.description: A GO term's negative regulation target.

claims.text: The term in go.id negatively regulates the term named in its negativelyRegulates array; the row is the regulator.
regulator go.id and regulated go.id joined by '|': 2,624 edges over 2,620 regulator terms, with unique pairs.

frames.text: The sign is in the edge type, not in the target value. Every regulated term resolves to a live go row and 73 edges cross namespaces.

limitations.text: Inhibition is not the complement of activation: 2,624 negative and 2,627 positive edges are curated independently, so one direction does not imply the other.

edges.name: go_term_part_of

child go.id and parent go.id joined by '|': 7,058 edges over 6,613 child terms, with unique pairs.

frames.text: Direct part-of parents only; 41,727 of 48,340 rows hold an empty array, which is normal for molecular-function terms. Every parent resolves to a go row and no term is its own parent. 786 edges (11.1%) join terms from different namespaces.

limitations.text: Part-of is not is-a and does not imply inheritance of annotations. The cross-namespace edges mean a namespace filter breaks part-of chains; do not treat an empty array as a source gap.

speciesId|targetGeneId -> targetGeneId, restricted to human rows: 20,910 edges, one per human gene node, of which 20,864 end at a TargetNode and 46 dangle. Emitting it from each of the 3,552,256 human rows collapses to the same 20,910 keys.

frames.text: Read homologue gene -> target. It is the only bridge from the homology layer into the target layer, and it exists only for human genes.

limitations.text: No edge means the gene is not human: the 207,485 non-human gene nodes never resolve, because their accessions are outside the release's target namespace. The 46 dangling edges are human Ensembl ids the target table does not hold.

The edge states accession identity, not homology: the HAS_HOMOLOGUE edge of the same pair carries type, confidence and identity. It also does not make the gene layer a target list: 46 human ids and all 207,485 non-human ids point at nothing.
Only the 20,864 resolved human genes are targets.
Every homologue gene resolves to a target, or the 207,485 non-human genes are targets of this release.

Roles are meaningful per database and per direction: 'regulator' and 'regulator target' only pair within one interaction, and the vocabulary is not an ontology.

interactionId|HAS_PARTICIPANT_B|targetB: 14,333,680 edges, one per interaction with a non-null targetB.

frames.text: targetB is null on 278,519 interactions, so those nodes have an A participant and no B participant. On the non-null rows 20,191 distinct values occur, of which 424 do not resolve to a TargetNode and produce a dangling endpoint. intB names what B actually is: an ENSP protein, a CHEBI molecule or another non-gene identifier.

The B side carries the informative species: host-pathogen pairs put a virus or bacterium here while A is always human. Absence of the edge is a resolution limit, not evidence about the interaction.

The interaction was not between two molecules, or that B is unknown.

edges.name: molecule_has_adverse_event

claims.text: The number of openFDA reports for the molecule that contain the event.

frames.text: A report count; one report can mention several drugs and events.

limitations.text: It is not a patient count, an incidence rate or a dose-response measure.

claims.text: The log-likelihood ratio of the disproportionality signal.

frames.text: Compare against critval; a larger value means the event is over-reported for the molecule.

limitations.text: The ratio depends on the openFDA background set and is not a probability.

claims.text: The llr threshold applied to the molecule's signal set.

frames.text: The threshold varies by molecule, so compare llr to critval rather than across molecules.

limitations.text: It is an inclusion threshold, not a p-value or a confidence level.

edges.description: The molecule has a significant openFDA disproportionality signal for an event.

claims.text: The molecule has a significant disproportionality signal for a MedDRA event in the release's openFDA analysis.
(chembl_id, event). meddraCode is an empty string on every row, so the event text is the only discriminator.

frames.text: count, llr and critval are on the edge: count is the number of reports, llr the log-likelihood ratio, critval the inclusion threshold for that molecule's signal set.

limitations.text: No edge means no significant signal for the pair; it does not mean the event was never reported.
A signal is a reporting-rate disproportion, not incidence, causality or a labelled effect. The MedDRA code cannot be used as a join key in 26.09 because it is empty.

edges.description: The molecule lists a child ChEMBL molecule.

drug_molecule.id -> each childChemblIds element.

properties.name: maxClinicalStage
properties.description: The best-ranked stage among the pair's contributing reports, with WITHDRAWAL and PHASE_4 folded into APPROVAL.

claims.text: The best-ranked stage among the pair's contributing reports, with WITHDRAWAL and PHASE_4 folded into APPROVAL.

edges.description: The release's clinical-development roll-up for a drug-disease pair.

claims.text: The release reports clinical development of the molecule in the disease, rolled up over the reports that name both. One edge per drug-disease pair in clinical_indication.
(drugId, diseaseId). The row's own id is a hash of the pair and adds nothing; 86,451 rows are 86,451 distinct pairs.

frames.text: maxClinicalStage is the best rank among the pair's contributing reports, with WITHDRAWAL and PHASE_4 folded into APPROVAL and UNKNOWN kept as a published value. It is not the stage of the latest or largest trial.

limitations.text: No edge means the release formed no pair. Reports flagged PHASE_IV_NOT_APPROVED or INDIRECT_PRIMARY_PURPOSE were excluded before pairs were formed, so absence is not a negative clinical finding.

A pair is not a trial and not an approval: APPROVAL means approval-status evidence from any report family. The release also lists the contributing report ids (321,785 pair-report memberships, all resolving in clinical_report.id); they are not materialised as edges, because a report already names its own drugs and diseases and the roll-up is QC-filtered, so it is not reproducible from them (11,948 of 86,451 pairs differ from a report-array reconstruction).
