The edge is an association between a drug and a target, not an indication through that target.

frames.text: maxClinicalStage is the drug's roll-up, repeated identically on every target row of that drug (4,684 drugs, 1 to 79 targets each), not a stage reached through this target.

limitations.text: A pair missing here has no mechanism target in the release's mechanism table, or its drug had no QC-passing report: reports flagged PHASE_IV_NOT_APPROVED, UNVALIDATED_INDICATION or INDIRECT_PRIMARY_PURPOSE are dropped.

The source row's diseases array and clinicalReportIds are per-drug roll-ups; its 54,648 drug-disease pairs are a subset of HAS_CLINICAL_INDICATION pairs and add no pair, so they are not carried here and cannot be read as this target's indications. The edge carries no direction, selectivity or score, and a target id can be a complex member that the mechanism table exploded.
The drug treats the molecule's diseases by acting on this target.

edges.name: molecule_has_cross_reference
edges.description: The molecule lists an external identifier.

claims.text: The molecule lists an external identifier in drug_molecule's crossReferences under the named source.
(drug_molecule.id, crossReferences.source, crossReferences.ids element).

frames.text: The edge points at a shared CrossReferenceNode keyed source:identifier. source is the authority (drugbank, Probes&Drugs), not the entity type.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no such identifier for the molecule.

A listed identifier is not a verified identity: two molecules citing the same cross-reference are not thereby the same molecule, and the release does not re-resolve the external record. Source spellings are not normalised across datasets, so the same authority can appear as drugbank here and DrugBank on a target.

edges.name: molecule_has_drug_warning
edges.description: The molecule is named by a drug warning.

claims.text: The molecule is named by a drug warning row.
(drug_warning.chemblIds element, drug_warning.id).

frames.text: Read molecule -> warning. Country, warning type, year and disease context are on the warning node.

limitations.text: No edge means no warning row names the molecule.

The edge says the warning names the molecule, not that the molecule caused the effect. Five chemblIds in drug_warning are absent from the molecule rows, so those edges point outside the molecule node set.

edges.name: molecule_has_mechanism_of_action

claims.text: The role the molecule plays at the target, for example INHIBITOR or AGONIST.

frames.text: Direction is not implied by mechanismOfAction text; read actionType.

limitations.text: The vocabulary is source-controlled and mixes pharmacodynamic and modality terms.

claims.text: The curated free-text mechanism label on the row.

frames.text: Many molecule-target pairs share one label; it is not a row identifier.

limitations.text: Text alone cannot distinguish rows; the edge key adds molecule, target, action type and target labels.

claims.text: The target-group name written on the mechanism row, for example a protein family.

frames.text: This is not TargetNode.approvedSymbol; one row can name a group containing several targets.

limitations.text: Do not join targetName to a target symbol; use the edge's target id.

claims.text: The kind of target group named by the row, for example single protein, protein family or protein complex.

frames.text: It qualifies targetName and says how the row's targets relate to it.

limitations.text: It is not the target's Ensembl biotype.

edges.description: The release curates a mechanism of action from the molecule to the target.

claims.text: The release curates a mechanism of action relating the molecule to a target.

(chemblId, target Ensembl id, actionType, mechanismOfAction, targetName, targetType). The tuple is unique across the 14,718 expanded molecule-target pairs, so rows with identical mechanism text stay distinct.

frames.text: actionType is the molecule's role at the target (INHIBITOR, AGONIST, ...). mechanismOfAction is free text shared by many rows; targetName and targetType describe the curated target group, not the target's symbol or biotype.

limitations.text: No edge means the release states no mechanism for that molecule-target pair. 670 mechanism rows name no target and produce no edge.

A mechanism is a curated assertion, not an assay result, potency or clinical effect. TargetNode membership is narrower than the target table, so an edge can point outside the target node set; a molecule can likewise lack a molecule node.

edges.name: molecule_has_parent
edges.description: The molecule's parentId names a parent ChEMBL molecule.

claims.text: The molecule's parentId names another molecule the release treats as its parent.
drug_molecule.id -> drug_molecule.parentId, one edge per non-null parentId.

frames.text: Read child -> parent. In ChEMBL the parent is the parent structure of a salt or derivative; this is not a pharmacological class.

limitations.text: No edge means parentId is null, not that the molecule has no chemical parent.
212 parent ids are absent from the release's molecule rows, so those edges point outside the molecule node set. Parent/child is a ChEMBL record hierarchy, not therapeutic equivalence.

edges.name: molecule_has_synonym
edges.description: The molecule has an alternative name recorded as a synonym.

claims.text: The molecule has an alternative name that the release records as a synonym.
(drug_molecule.id, synonyms.source, synonyms.label).

frames.text: Read molecule -> name. The name node carries the string and its authority; this edge says the release classified the pair as a synonym.

limitations.text: No edge means no synonym with a usable label and source. The molecule's preferred name is not a synonym edge.
A synonym is not a trade name and does not establish that two molecules are the same substance.

edges.name: molecule_has_trade_name
edges.description: The molecule has a marketed product name recorded as a trade name.

claims.text: The molecule has a product name that the release records as a trade name.
(drug_molecule.id, tradeNames.source, tradeNames.label).

frames.text: Read molecule -> name. A trade name labels a marketed product; it is not the active ingredient's preferred name.

limitations.text: No edge means no trade name with a usable label and source.
A trade name is a product label, not an approval, an indication or a statement that the molecule is marketed in a jurisdiction.

edges.name: mouse_model_has_phenotype
edges.description: An MP phenotype observed in a mouse model.

claims.text: The mouse model was observed with this Mammalian Phenotype term. The term is the observation on the row, not a class of the model.
biologicalModels.id|HAS_PHENOTYPE|modelPhenotypeId: 243,341 distinct model-phenotype pairs over the 256,254 model entries. Repeated rows collapse to one edge.

frames.text: modelPhenotypeId is an MP accession in colon form and is never null; 10,584 distinct terms occur and each has a PhenotypeNode from the evidence layer. modelPhenotypeLabel is the term's label on the same row and is not stored, because the term's node carries it.

limitations.text: No edge means the model has no recorded MP phenotype; none occur.

The observation is a curated MP term for one model in one genetic background, not a measured effect size. MP and HP terms are different vocabularies and are not merged, so this edge never reaches an HPO term.

edges.name: mouse_model_has_phenotype_class
edges.description: An MP phenotype class the model's observed phenotype belongs to.

claims.text: The model's phenotype belongs to this MP class term, the system-level category the source records alongside the observation (for example nervous system phenotype). It is a classification of the observed phenotype, not a second observation.
biologicalModels.id|HAS_PHENOTYPE_CLASS|modelPhenotypeClasses.id: 127,802 distinct model-class pairs from 344,055 model-element and class-element combinations over the 28 class terms.

frames.text: A closed 28-term vocabulary (MP:0001186 pigmentation phenotype, MP:0005367 renal/urinary system phenotype, ...). 60,824 of the 203,583 rows carry more than one class, up to five. 21 of the 28 class terms also occur as observations; 7 occur only here, so this edge is their only binding.

limitations.text: No edge means the row records no class for its phenotype; none occur.

The class is the source's broad system label, not an ontology parent walk: the release publishes no MP hierarchy, so an IS_A edge between the observed term and its class does not exist. The class does not add a phenotype beyond the observation.

edges.name: mouse_model_supported_by_publication
edges.description: A publication the model's record cites.

claims.text: A publication cited on the model's biologicalModels entry. The release stores literature as a PMID array per model entry; the graph models it as an edge rather than a string array property.

biologicalModels.id|SUPPORTED_BY|pmid: 130,911 distinct model-pmid pairs from 1,249,431 PMID elements and 24,380 distinct pmids; a model cited by several phenotype rows repeats its PMIDs and collapses.

frames.text: Derived from a 1:1-consistent release field: the array holds 1-8 PMIDs on 215,502 model entries and is null on 40,752. 23,437 of the 24,380 distinct PMIDs resolve to a PublicationNode; the remaining 943 leave a dangling endpoint.

limitations.text: No edge means the model entry cites no PMID or cites one outside the release's literature corpus. 96 model ids carry more than one distinct literature array across their rows.
The edge says the model record cites the paper, not that the paper reports this phenotype. It is not the IMPC evidence citation, which lives on the IMPC evidence node.

edges.name: pgx_annotation_has_drug

claims.text: The drug name as ClinPGx writes it.

frames.text: 1-3 names per row; 660 distinct names for 532 ChEMBL ids.

limitations.text: Never null on the 33,707 drug elements in 26.09.
A name, not a key: never join on it, and it can be a metabolite (n-desmethyltamoxifen).

edges.description: One drug named by the annotation.

claims.text: A drug the annotation concerns, one edge per element of the row's drugs array. A multi-drug annotation keeps one row and therefore several edges.

annotation key|HAS_DRUG|drugId: 29,613 edges over the 29,391 rows that name a ChEMBL id. 29,328 resolve to drug_molecule.id and 285 dangle on three ChEMBL ids the molecule table does not hold (CHEMBL4525767, CHEMBL170365, CHEMBL501680).

frames.text: Read annotation -> molecule. The edge carries drugFromSource, the name ClinPGx uses; drugId is the release's ChEMBL id. 660 names map to 532 ChEMBL ids.

limitations.text: 4,094 array elements (on 4,088 rows) carry no drugId and emit no edge, because a MoleculeNode is a ChEMBL molecule. No row has an empty drugs array.
The edge names the drug the response was observed with, not an indication, a dose or an approval. A drug absent from ChEMBL stays a name in the source rather than becoming a graph node.

edges.name: pgx_annotation_has_phenotype
edges.description: The disease term the release mapped the phenotype phrase to.

claims.text: The disease or phenotype term the release matched to the annotation's phenotype phrase.
annotation key|HAS_MAPPED_PHENOTYPE|phenotypeFromSourceId: 724 edges, all resolving to disease.id; 30 distinct terms.

frames.text: Read annotation -> disease term. MONDO_0018493 carries 581 of the 724 edges; the rest spread over 29 terms in MONDO, EFO, GO, HP and NCIT.

limitations.text: No edge for 32,755 rows (97.8%) because the phrase matched no disease label; phenotypeText is still present on 31,625 of those rows.

The mapping is the release's label lookup, not ClinPGx's own disease assignment and not a diagnosis. It is sparse and many-to-one, so absence is not a healthy outcome and presence is not an established association.
A HAS_MAPPED_PHENOTYPE edge records a matched ontology term.
A pharmacogenomic annotation with a disease term is evidence that the genotype causes or treats that disease.

edges.name: pgx_annotation_has_target
edges.description: The annotation's pharmacogene.

claims.text: The gene the annotation says the genotype acts through.
annotation key|HAS_TARGET|targetFromSourceId: 31,910 edges, one per row with a gene id. 25,295 edges end at a TargetNode; 6,615 dangle on 51 Ensembl ids the target table does not hold.

frames.text: Read annotation -> target. The gene id is the release's resolved Ensembl id, so it needs no symbol mapping. isDirectTarget on the node says whether the gene is a mechanism-of-action target of a row drug.

limitations.text: No edge means targetFromSourceId is null (1,569 rows). A dangling edge means the release named an Ensembl gene that is not in its target universe; that is a resolution gap, not a different gene.

The binding cannot look up the target table, so it emits the edge for every non-null id and reports the 51 unresolved ids instead of silently dropping or inventing a target. The edge is annotation context, not evidence that the drug acts on the gene in patients.

edges.name: pgx_annotation_has_variant
edges.description: The annotation's variant, where the row states one.

claims.text: The release variant the annotation is about: the variantId derived from the row's genotype. The edge exists only for rows that yield a single resolvable variant.
annotation key|HAS_VARIANT|variantId: 16,169 edges, one per row with a non-null variantId; all 2,882 distinct ids resolve to variant.variantId.

frames.text: Read annotation -> variant. The 16,169 edges cover 48.3% of the rows; the other 17,310 rows state no variantId.

limitations.text: No edge means the row has no variantId: 17,310 rows (51.7%), the 9,548 haplotype-anchored rows and 7,762 rsID-anchored genotypes that reduce to the reference. It does not mean the annotation is not about a variant.

variantRsId is not used as a fallback, because nothing in the release is keyed by rsID and 14 of the 2,843 rsIDs resolve to no variant row. The edge is the build's derived variant, not necessarily the allele the clinician annotated.

edges.name: pgx_annotation_supported_by
edges.description: A publication cited for the annotation.

claims.text: A publication the annotation cites, one edge per element of the row's literature array.
annotation key|SUPPORTED_BY|pmid: 140,757 edges; 135,223 end at a PublicationNode and 5,534 dangle on 220 PubMed ids absent from literature_entity_lut. No pair repeats within a row.

frames.text: Read annotation -> paper. literature is never null or empty and is sorted and de-duplicated by the writer; 5,952 distinct PMIDs back the 5,190 annotations.

limitations.text: No edge would mean the row cites nothing; that does not occur in 26.09. A dangling edge means the release cites a paper outside its text-mined publication corpus.
The citation is for the whole annotation, not for one genotype, drug or phenotype row, so edges repeat the same paper across the annotation's rows. Citing a paper is not a verification of its claim.

edges.name: phenotype_has_cross_reference
edges.description: An external identifier listed in a phenotype term's cross-references.

claims.text: The phenotype term's record lists the external identifier.
phenotype -> source:identifier, keyed phenotype::accession::HAS_CROSS_REFERENCE::source:identifier. The 43,966 elements are 43,966 distinct pairs within a term.

frames.text: Identifiers come from FMA, CALOHA, MESH, GO, BTO, EMAPA, UBERON and other anatomy and cell-ontology namespaces; every value carries a colon.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no such identifier for the term.

A listed identifier is not verification of the external record and does not merge two phenotype terms. The node type is shared with the target and disease domains, so a shared identifier is one node with several inbound edges.

edges.name: phenotype_has_obsolete_term
edges.description: A retired ontology accession listed by a phenotype term.

claims.text: The phenotype term lists the accession as one it has retired.
phenotype -> accession, keyed phenotype::accession::HAS_OBSOLETE_TERM::accession. The 5,955 elements are 5,955 distinct pairs; none is a disease_hpo.id.

frames.text: 297 of the elements are disease.id values, but they are listed as retired accessions of a phenotype term, so they resolve to ObsoleteTermNode and not to the DISEASE node with the same string.

limitations.text: No edge means the term lists no retired accession.
The edge preserves a historical accession without a successor link; it is not a synonym edge and does not merge terms.

edges.name: phenotype_is_a
edges.description: A phenotype term's parent.

claims.text: The child phenotype term is a subtype of the parent term.
child accession -> parent accession.

frames.text: Direct parent edges; ancestors are reachable transitively.

limitations.text: Subtype does not imply that every annotation of the parent applies to the child.

edges.name: publication_mention

claims.text: The release's within-paper relevance of this grounded mention: a harmonic sum of section weights, each weight divided by its section rank squared, over the sections that mentioned the entity.

frames.text: Observed 0.01 to 1.510077108820886 in 26.09, median 0.675. It is neither a share nor a probability and passes 1; a mention in a high-weight early section outranks repeated late mentions.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
The score ranks entities within one paper and does not measure how much the paper concerns the entity; sorting papers by it does not give the papers that discuss the entity most.

edges.description: A publication's text was matched to an entity of one keyword class.

claims.text: One entity mention that the release's literature matcher grounded in one publication. The edge exists per publication, entity class and grounded identifier; it records the text match, not the paper's use of the entity.

(pmid, keywordType, keywordId). literature_entity_lut is unique on (pmid, keywordId) — 173,137,629 rows and no duplicate pair in 26.09 — and every keywordId belongs to one keywordType, so the triple is the row identity. Edges are keyed pmid::<class>::keywordId.
26.09 has exactly three keyword classes, DS disease or syndrome, GP gene or protein and CD chemical or drug; there is no variant, pathway, phenotype or anatomy mention class.

frames.text: The edge type names the class: MENTIONS_DISEASE holds DS, MENTIONS_TARGET GP and MENTIONS_MOLECULE CD. relevance ranks this mention inside its own paper.

limitations.text: No edge means the matcher grounded no identifier of this class in the paper. A paper that names the entity by an unmatched string, a bare acronym, or an accession outside the release's vocabularies has no edge although it discusses the entity.

A text match is not the paper's stance: the paper may support, dispute or only mention the entity. Every grounded pair is emitted with no relevance cutoff, so a mention count counts matched papers, not supporting findings.
The LUT carries variant, pathway or phenotype mentions under another keywordType.

edges.name: publication_mentions_disease

claims.text: The release's within-paper relevance of this grounded mention: a harmonic sum of section weights, each weight divided by its section rank squared, over the sections that mentioned the entity.

frames.text: Observed 0.01 to 1.510077108820886 in 26.09, median 0.675. It is neither a share nor a probability and passes 1; a mention in a high-weight early section outranks repeated late mentions.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
The score ranks entities within one paper and does not measure how much the paper concerns the entity; sorting papers by it does not give the papers that discuss the entity most.

edges.description: A publication's text mentions a term in the release's disease vocabulary.

claims.text: The publication's text mentions a term of the release's disease vocabulary: a DS keyword grounded to disease.id.
(pmid, 'DS', keywordId), with keywordId equal to disease.id. All 81,182,673 DS pairs resolve to disease.id (14,069 distinct terms).

frames.text: DS is the matcher's bucket for every identifier that is neither a gene nor a ChEMBL molecule, so the term can be a MONDO or EFO disease, an HP phenotype, a GO or MP term, an UBERON anatomy term, an OTAR therapeutic area or an OBA variable — all DiseaseNode ids.

limitations.text: No edge means no DS identifier was grounded in this paper; it does not mean the paper says nothing about the disease.

A disease mention is not an association, a diagnosis or a claim by the paper; it may be background, a comorbidity list or a negation. A phenotype, anatomy or process term reached by this edge is not a disease.

edges.name: publication_mentions_molecule

claims.text: The release's within-paper relevance of this grounded mention: a harmonic sum of section weights, each weight divided by its section rank squared, over the sections that mentioned the entity.

frames.text: Observed 0.01 to 1.510077108820886 in 26.09, median 0.675. It is neither a share nor a probability and passes 1; a mention in a high-weight early section outranks repeated late mentions.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
The score ranks entities within one paper and does not measure how much the paper concerns the entity; sorting papers by it does not give the papers that discuss the entity most.

edges.description: A publication's text mentions a drug or chemical.

claims.text: The publication's text mentions a drug or chemical: a CD keyword grounded to drug_molecule.id.
(pmid, 'CD', keywordId), with keywordId equal to drug_molecule.id. All 36,002,868 CD pairs resolve to drug_molecule.id (14,043 distinct ChEMBL molecules); every CD identifier is a CHEMBL accession.

frames.text: Only ChEMBL-grounded molecules are mentioned; a drug named by brand, code or salt form without a ChEMBL grounding has no edge.

limitations.text: No edge means no ChEMBL identifier was grounded in this paper; it does not mean the paper does not discuss the drug.
A mention of a molecule is not a claim that the paper studies it, reports an effect or names an indication.

edges.name: publication_mentions_target

claims.text: The release's within-paper relevance of this grounded mention: a harmonic sum of section weights, each weight divided by its section rank squared, over the sections that mentioned the entity.

frames.text: Observed 0.01 to 1.510077108820886 in 26.09, median 0.675. It is neither a share nor a probability and passes 1; a mention in a high-weight early section outranks repeated late mentions.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
The score ranks entities within one paper and does not measure how much the paper concerns the entity; sorting papers by it does not give the papers that discuss the entity most.

edges.description: A publication's text mentions a gene or protein.

claims.text: The publication's text mentions a gene or protein: a GP keyword grounded to target.id.
(pmid, 'GP', keywordId), with keywordId equal to target.id. All 55,952,088 GP pairs resolve to target.id (30,464 distinct Ensembl genes); every GP identifier is an ENSG accession.

frames.text: The edge is the matcher's gene grounding; the release does not say which symbol or synonym in the text produced it.

limitations.text: No edge means no Ensembl gene identifier was grounded in this paper; a paper that names the gene by a symbol the matcher did not map is missed.
A mention of a gene is not the paper's finding about it and not experimental evidence for any association; a target named only as a control or in a citation list still gets an edge.

edges.name: pathway_is_part_of
edges.description: A Reactome pathway's parent.

claims.text: The child pathway is part of the direct parent pathway.
child reactome.id and parent reactome.id joined by '|': 2,899 edges with 2,899 distinct pairs.

frames.text: 2,854 pathways have at least one parent, 29 are roots, and a pathway has up to 6 parents. The parents and children arrays are exact inverses here: every parent element has its reverse child element.

limitations.text: ancestors, descendants and path stay in reactome and are not edges. ancestors and descendants are transitive closures that repeat what this walk already gives; path is an ordered route (up to 11 per row, 75 rows with more than one root) whose canonical order is a build choice, not a relation. To get ancestry, walk this edge. Pathway membership is not a target-disease assertion.

edges.name: regulatory_element_active_in_biosample
edges.description: The biosample an E2G prediction was made in.

claims.text: The regulatory element was predicted in this biosample, so the interval's activity is asserted for that tissue or cell type only.
intervalId|ACTIVE_IN|biosampleId: 48,806,245 edges, 1:1 with the element node.

frames.text: All 322 distinct biosampleId values resolve to a BiosampleNode, and biosampleName is the label on the same row. The same genomic interval recurs in other biosamples as a different intervalId.

limitations.text: No edge means the prediction names no biosample; none occur.
Activity in a biosample is the prediction's assay context, not measured chromatin state in a sample. biosampleFromSourceId is null on every row, so the source offers no finer sample identity.

edges.name: regulatory_element_regulates_target
edges.description: The gene an E2G prediction links a regulatory element to.

claims.text: The E2G model predicts that this regulatory interval regulates this gene. The direction is element -> target, matching the ontology regulation edges; the source row is gene-anchored.
intervalId|REGULATES|geneId: 48,806,245 edges. intervalId determines geneId in every row, so the edge is 1:1 with the node.

frames.text: All 20,088 distinct geneId values resolve to a TargetNode, so the binding leaves no dangling endpoint. score, distanceToTss and intervalType on the node qualify this link; the edge adds no property because it has exactly one object per node.

limitations.text: No edge means no predicted link. Every element node has one, so the edge carries no information beyond the node; it exists to attach the prediction to the target.

REGULATES states the model's prediction, not a measured regulatory effect, and it is not a target-disease assertion. The gene is the nearest or linked gene in the source's model, and one interval is predicted to regulate up to 20 genes.
The edge records an E2G prediction.
The element regulates the gene in vivo, or that modulating the element changes the target's expression.

edges.name: regulatory_element_supported_by_publication
edges.description: The publication the E2G predictions cite.

claims.text: The publication cited on an E2G prediction row.
intervalId|SUPPORTED_BY|pmid: 48,806,245 edges. pmid is the single value 38014075 on every row.

frames.text: 38014075 resolves to a PublicationNode, so the edge leaves no dangling endpoint. Because the value is constant, every element points at the same paper.

limitations.text: No edge means the row names no PMID; none occur.

The edge records the dataset's citation, not per-element experimental support: it adds 48.8M identical edges and no discrimination. Filter by datasourceId or start from the publication node instead of traversing it per element.

edges.name: safety_event_has_effect
edges.description: The safety observation reports an effect descriptor.

claims.text: The safety observation reports the direction-and-dosing descriptor.
safety event key|HAS_EFFECT|direction|dosing: 2,349 edges, unique per observation and descriptor.

frames.text: Read observation -> descriptor. 2,314 rows carry effects; 35 of them carry two, which produce two edges.

limitations.text: No edge means effects is null (2,073 rows) or empty. The observation still exists without an effect statement.
The edge does not rank the two effects of a row or state a mechanism. direction is source wording, not signed pharmacology or clinical benefit.

edges.name: safety_event_has_biosample
edges.description: The safety observation is reported in a tissue.

claims.text: The safety observation is reported in the tissue named by one biosample entry.
safety event key|OBSERVED_IN|normalised tissueId: 5,072 edges over the 2,601 observations that name a tissue, unique per observation and tissue.

frames.text: The entry's tissueId is converted from colon to underscore form (31 elements write UBERON:...), which makes all 5,072 non-null tissue ids name a BiosampleNode. An observation can list up to six tissues, so the edge count exceeds the observation count.

limitations.text: No edge means the observation names no tissue. 438 biosample elements are cell-only and carry no tissueId.

Only tissueId becomes an edge. cellId is null on all 5,599 elements, so no cell-line or cell-type node is created from this array; 438 elements carry only a cellFormat and 271 a cellLabel (mostly cell lines such as HepaRG and HepG2), and they produce no edge. The source tissueLabel is not carried: the node's name is the vocabulary label and can differ (UBERON_0004535 is 'cardiovascular' in the source and 'cardiovascular system' in biosample).

edges.name: study_has_credible_set
edges.description: One study's credible set.

claims.text: The credible set belongs to the study that produced it.
studyId -> studyLocusId.

frames.text: A study can have several credible sets; the set carries the locus.

limitations.text: The edge does not assert that the study's trait is caused by any variant in the set.

edges.name: study_measured_in
edges.description: The biosample context in which the study was measured.

claims.text: The biosample in which the study's molecular measurement was made.
(studyId, biosampleId). 2,838,730 edges over 128 biosamples; every biosampleId resolves to biosample.biosampleId and 0 keys duplicate.

frames.text: biosampleId is present on every QTL row and null on all GWAS rows. The biosample node's ontology ancestry, not this edge, separates tissue from cell type.

limitations.text: A GWAS study has no MEASURED_IN edge; it has no molecular assay context here.
128 distinct biosamples cover all QTL studies, so the edge is coarse. A measurement in a biosample is not evidence that the target is expressed there in every condition.

edges.name: study_measures_target
edges.description: The target a molecular QTL study measures.

claims.text: The target gene the study measures. On a molecular QTL this is the gene whose expression, splicing, transcript usage or protein level is the trait.
(studyId, geneId). 2,838,730 edges; every geneId resolves to target.id and 0 keys duplicate.

frames.text: geneId is present on every QTL row (eqtl, sqtl, tuqtl, sceqtl, pqtl) and null on all 165,517 GWAS rows.

limitations.text: A GWAS study has no MEASURES_TARGET edge; it measures a trait, not a gene.
The edge names the measured gene, not a target-disease association and not a drug target. A QTL study can have several credible sets but only one measured target here.

edges.name: study_published_as_publication
edges.description: The publication a study record cites.

claims.text: A study record's cited publication, taken from the study's own PubMed reference.
(studyId, pubmedId). A study carries at most one pubmedId; several studies, above all the gene-by-biosample molecular-QTL rows, can share one publication.

frames.text: The publication node carries the release's date, year and pmcid for the paper. The study keeps its own publicationTitle, journal and publicationDate copies. Every study pubmedId is a numeric PubMed number, so it can only match the numeric subset of the LUT keys.

limitations.text: A study with a null pubmedId has no edge: 2,953 of the 3,004,247 study rows in 26.09.

One citation can back thousands of study records, so edge counts do not count papers. The edge is complete for the study table but not for the publication node set: 7,529 of the 7,703 distinct study PMIDs (893,960 of 3,001,294 rows with a PMID) occur in literature_entity_lut; the other 174 PMIDs (2,107,334 rows, mostly three large QTL papers) are cited by the release but absent from its text-mined corpus, so their edges name a publication key with no PublicationNode.

edges.name: study_studies_disease
edges.description: A disease or trait the study is annotated with.

claims.text: A disease or trait term the study is annotated with.

frames.text: Continuous in [0,1] and never null; higher means the target is above the threshold in more biosamples.

limitations.text: The threshold is not published. The score is computed within one datasource, so values from the four sources are not comparable with each other.

claims.text: The release's measure of how specific the target's expression is to this biosample context.

frames.text: Continuous in [0,1] where present; higher means more concentrated in this context.

limitations.text: Null on 26,506,752 rows: every PRIDE row and parts of DICE, gtex and tabula_sapiens. Absence means the source did not compute it, not that specificity is zero.
It is per row and per datasource, not a target-level tissue specificity; the Target Engine's comparable roll-up is the PRIORITISATION_PROFILE's tissueSpecificity.

claims.text: The tissue ontology id the row records, whether or not the edge endpoint is that id.

frames.text: 1,239 distinct ids, all resolving exactly in biosample.biosampleId; null on the 10,847,985 cell-type-only rows.

limitations.text: It is not an ancestor of the cell-type id in the biosample hierarchy in general, so read it even when the endpoint is the cell type.

claims.text: The cell-type ontology id the row records, when the source resolved one.

frames.text: 1,286 distinct ids, all resolving exactly; present on 76,015,005 rows, and on those rows the edge endpoint is this id.

limitations.text: Cell type here is the source's annotation of the profiled cells, not a sorted population definition.

claims.text: The source's quality-control flags for the measurement.

frames.text: An empty array on all 83,290,030 rows in 26.09, so the property never qualifies an edge.

limitations.text: Never null; the array is present and empty.
An empty array means the release recorded no QC failure flag, not that the measurement passed a QC threshold.

edges.description: One measured expression distribution of a target in a biosample context.

claims.text: A baseline expression measurement: one datasource's distribution of this target's transcript or protein abundance in a tissue and/or cell type. The edge is the measurement, not a statement that the target is expressed in every cell of that class.

targetId|EXPRESSED_IN|tissueBiosampleId|celltypeBiosampleId|datasourceId|tissueBiosampleFromSource|celltypeBiosampleFromSource, with the empty string for a null component. The grain is therefore one edge per release row: target, datasource and the source sample label, resolved to the two biosample ids. The release's own declared key is (celltypeBiosampleId, tissueBiosampleId, targetId, datasourceId) and is not unique: 83,290,030 rows carry 83,223,889 distinct 4-tuples. The binding's 7-part key gives 83,289,724, and the 306 remaining rows differ only in the measured quantiles.

frames.text: Both biosample ids resolve exactly in biosample.biosampleId, so no separator normalisation is needed. The edge points at the most specific biosample: celltypeBiosampleId when present, otherwise tissueBiosampleId. Both ids are properties, because the cell type is a direct ontology child of the tissue in only 13 of 1,108 observed pairs, so a walk up the biosample hierarchy does not recover the tissue. unit separates the measurement scales and must be read before comparing any two edges.

limitations.text: No edge means the release carries no baseline measurement for that target in that context in any of the four sources. A null specificity_score is the source not computing it (all 504,046 PRIDE rows), not a specificity of zero. A null median means the distribution was not summarised; 164,481 rows carry no quantiles.

One edge per target+tissue+celltype is not possible: 1,051,867 of the 82,116,120 measured triples carry measurements from two or three datasources in different units (CPM pseudobulk counts, TPM, iBAQ protein abundance), and a single triple-keyed edge would have to pick one and drop the rest. 1,101,388 triples carry more than one row in total. Within gtex, 57,804 target-tissue pairs are two source labels mapped to one ontology term (Brain - Cerebellum and Brain - Cerebellar Hemisphere both UBERON_0002037), which is why the source labels are in the key rather than on the edge. The release's field description swaps the two fromSource labels (it calls tissueBiosampleFromSource the cell type); the values are the source's own sample names for the field they sit in. qualityControls is an empty array on every row, so it qualifies nothing. targetFromSourceId is non-null only on the 504,046 PRIDE rows and holds UniProt accessions, not Ensembl genes, so it is not carried. distribution_score and specificity_score are source scores in [0,1]; they are not probabilities and are not comparable with the Target Engine's tissue specificity on the PRIORITISATION_PROFILE.
A baseline expression edge is a measured distribution in a biosample class from one source.
The target is expressed in that tissue in health or disease, in every cell of the class, or at the level the median states.
The four datasources measure different quantities.
TPM, CPM and iBAQ values can be ranked or averaged together, or that a bulk tissue value is comparable with a single-cell value.

edges.name: target_has_chemical_probe

claims.text: The mechanism labels the probe source attaches to the probe.

frames.text: One to three strings on 886 rows (796 with one, 88 with two, 2 with three); null on 379. Values are free text such as inhibitor, agonist, degrader or allosteric modulator.

limitations.text: Null means the source gives no mechanism label, not an unknown mechanism.
The labels are not a controlled vocabulary, are unordered and are not a pharmacological proof of action.

claims.text: How the probe's assessment was obtained: experimental or calculated.

frames.text: One value on 900 rows and two on 365; only experimental and calculated occur.

limitations.text: Origin qualifies the scores; it is not the molecule's development stage or the evidence type of a clinical claim.

claims.text: The control compound or control note recorded for the probe row.

frames.text: Non-null on 210 rows. Values mix compound names (BI-6953, WEB2387) with notes such as 'No control'.

limitations.text: Null on 1,055 rows means the source records no control, not that none exists.
A control name is not a MoleculeNode link and does not establish that the pair was assayed together.

claims.text: The probe source's high-quality-probe flag.

frames.text: True on 858 rows and false on 407; no nulls.

limitations.text: It is the source's assessment, not a release grade, a potency threshold or a comparison across probe sources.

claims.text: The Probes & Drugs druggability score recorded for the probe.

frames.text: A numeric score with no nulls or NaN in 26.09.

limitations.text: The scale is the source's and is not normalised by the release; do not threshold it or compare it with isHighQuality as if they were the same quantity.

claims.text: The source's probe-activity score in cells.

frames.text: NaN on 454 rows; NaN is the source's missing marker, not a low score.

limitations.text: Null and NaN both mean no score; the release writes NaN.
It carries no unit or assay context and is not comparable with scoreInOrganisms.

claims.text: The source's probe-activity score in organisms.

frames.text: NaN on 454 rows; NaN is the source's missing marker, not a low score.

limitations.text: Null and NaN both mean no score; the release writes NaN.
It carries no species, dose or endpoint and is not comparable with scoreInCells.

edges.description: A chemical probe is reported for the target.

claims.text: A chemical probe for the target: a molecule that the probe source names as a tool compound or control, with the source's quality and activity assessments.

targetId|HAS_CHEMICAL_PROBE|drugId|drugFromSourceId: 1,199 edges for the 1,265 source rows. (targetId, drugId) has 1,263 distinct values; the two colliding pairs both have a null drugId, so drugFromSourceId is part of the key.

frames.text: The edge points at the ChEMBL MoleculeNode named by drugId. drugFromSourceId is the probe source's own identifier (PD...), not a ChEMBL id. mechanismOfAction and origin are lists on the edge; isHighQuality is the source's flag.

limitations.text: 66 rows have no drugId because the probe is named only by the source id; they emit no edge, since a MoleculeNode is a ChEMBL molecule. A null control (1,055 rows) is not 'no control'.

urls (1 to 6 niceName/url structs per row) stay in the source. targetFromSourceId is the pre-resolution symbol or accession and is not carried; every targetId resolves to a TargetNode. NaN in scoreInCells and scoreInOrganisms (454 rows each) is the source's missing marker, not a measured score. A probe annotation is a research-reagent classification, not an approved drug, a potency claim or clinical safety evidence.
A high-quality probe is a useful experimental reagent.
A high-quality probe is a drug candidate or evidence that the target is druggable in patients.

edges.name: target_has_constraint

claims.text: The release's constraint score for the target under this family.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.

frames.text: Higher means more constrained within this family's release scale.

limitations.text: Null for rows where the release did not compute a score.
Not a probability that the gene is essential and not comparable across families.

claims.text: The expected number of variants under the release's null model.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.

frames.text: Compare with obs; the pair underlies oe.

limitations.text: Null when the release did not compute an expectation.
The null model and its covariates stay in the source dataset.

claims.text: The observed number of variants for the target under this family.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.

frames.text: An integer count, not a rate.

limitations.text: Null when the release did not report the count.
The cohort behind the count is not carried on the edge.

claims.text: The observed-to-expected variant ratio.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.

frames.text: Values below one indicate depletion; the bounds are oeLower and oeUpper.

limitations.text: Null when obs or exp is missing.
The ratio is not a significance test; use the release's score for its ranking.

claims.text: The lower bound of the confidence interval on oe.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.

frames.text: Read together with oe and oeUpper.

limitations.text: Null when the release did not compute an interval.
The interval's method and level stay in the source dataset.

claims.text: The upper bound of the confidence interval on oe.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.

frames.text: Read together with oe and oeLower.

limitations.text: Null when the release did not compute an interval.
The interval's method and level stay in the source dataset.

claims.text: The gene's rank in the release's constraint distribution.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.

frames.text: A rank, not a percentile; ties and direction are defined by the source.

limitations.text: Null when the release did not rank the gene.
Do not compare ranks across constraint families.

claims.text: The gene's bin index in the release's constraint distribution.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.

frames.text: A coarse position derived from the rank.

limitations.text: Null when the release did not assign a bin.
The bin width is release-specific and not carried here.

claims.text: The gene's six-bin index in the release's constraint distribution.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.

frames.text: A coarser variant of upperBin.

limitations.text: Null when the release did not assign the six-bin index.
The bin boundaries are release-specific and not carried here.

edges.description: One constraint metric of a target under one constraint family.

claims.text: The target's constraint metrics under one constraint family (missense, loss of function or synonymous).
target.id -> constraintType: key = target::HAS_CONSTRAINT::constraint_type::constraintType. A target has at most one row per family in the release.

frames.text: obs and exp are observed and expected variant counts, oe the ratio with oeLower/oeUpper bounds, score the release's constraint score, and upperRank/upperBin/upperBin6 the gene's position in the distribution. A null metric is missing, not zero.

limitations.text: No edge means the release carries no metric for that family and target.
Constraint is a depletion signal over population variation. It does not establish essentiality, pathogenicity or a tissue-specific effect, and scores are not comparable across families.

edges.name: target_has_cross_reference
edges.description: An external identifier listed in the target's cross-references.

claims.text: The target's record lists the external identifier.
target.id -> source:identifier: key = target::HAS_CROSS_REFERENCE::source:identifier.

frames.text: source is the external namespace: PDB, InterPro, Reactome, HGNC, DrugBank, ChEMBL or signalP. identifier is the accession as listed.

limitations.text: No edge means the release did not list that identifier for the target.
A listed identifier is not proof that the external record describes the same molecule, and the release does not verify the external record.

edges.name: target_has_essentiality_screen

claims.text: The release's target-level essentiality flag, computed from the essentiality screens.

frames.text: True for 1,822 of 18,464 targets and false for the rest; no nulls. It is repeated on every screen edge of a target, so read it once per target.

limitations.text: It is not the cell-line-specific call and its computation is not in this dataset. A false flag does not mean the target has no dependency in any line.

claims.text: The DepMap gene-effect score for the target in the cell line.

frames.text: A continuous score; more negative means stronger dependency. The release's description treats values below -1 as dependencies. Non-null on all 22,171,776 screens.

limitations.text: It is not a p-value, effect size in physical units or a clinical endpoint. Compare screens only on the release's own scale; the build does not renormalise.

claims.text: The target's expression level in the cell line.

frames.text: A continuous expression value, non-null on 20,923,498 screens. It is the only field that distinguishes the repeated screens of one target-cell-line pair.

limitations.text: Null on 1,248,278 screens; a null is a source gap, not zero expression.
The unit and normalisation are the source's, and the value is not comparable with baseline_expression without an explicit mapping.

claims.text: The mutation label recorded for the screen.

frames.text: Only two values occur: damaging (85,430 screens) and hotspot (1,478); null on the other 22,084,868 screens.

limitations.text: Null means the source states no mutation label, not a wild-type line.
The dataset does not name the mutated gene, so read the label as screen context, not as a property of the target or of the cell line's genome.

edges.description: A DepMap CRISPR screen measures dependency on the target in a cell line.

claims.text: A DepMap CRISPR screen in one cell line, measuring how strongly the cell line depends on the target.

targetId|HAS_ESSENTIALITY_SCREEN|depmapId|expression: 22,171,776 edges. There are only 21,409,328 distinct target-cell-line pairs: 703,552 pairs occur twice and 29,448 three times, and the repeated rows differ only in expression, so the expression value completes the key.

frames.text: geneEffect is the DepMap gene-effect score; more negative means a stronger dependency, and the release's description treats values below -1 as dependencies, a threshold this edge does not apply. expression is the target's expression in the line. mutation is the screen's mutation label where present. isEssential is a target-level flag, identical on every screen edge of a target.

limitations.text: No edge means the release has no screen row for that target-cell-line pair. A null expression or mutation is a source gap, not a zero expression or a wild-type line.

This is the release's largest target annotation: 22,171,776 edges over only 1,208 cell lines. isEssential is target-level (1,822 true, 16,642 false) and must not be read as the cell-line-specific call; the per-line evidence is geneEffect. diseaseCellLineId (null on 9,354,641 screens and for 503 of the 1,208 lines) is not carried because CellLineNode has no property for it. A dependency is an in-vitro observation, not essentiality in a human tissue or a therapeutic window.
A dependency measured in a cancer cell line is a model observation.
A target that is essential in DepMap is essential in patients or cannot be safely modulated.

edges.name: target_has_go_annotation

claims.text: The GO reference or PubMed identifier cited for the annotation.
One component of the edge key.

frames.text: Values are GO_REF accessions or PMID identifiers for the cited source.

limitations.text: The release's go array never carries a null source.
A shared source does not make two annotations the same statement.

claims.text: The GO evidence code that states how the annotation was made.
One component of the edge key.

frames.text: Observed codes include IEA, IDA, IMP, TAS, NAS and ISS; the code is not a score.

limitations.text: The release's go array never carries a null evidence code.
IEA marks an inferred electronic annotation and is not equivalent to a manual assertion.

claims.text: The GO namespace the term belongs to, as a one-letter code.
One component of the edge key.

frames.text: P is biological process, F molecular function and C cellular component.

limitations.text: The release's go array never carries a null aspect.
The letter is the release's spelling; the term's own namespace is on the GO term node.

claims.text: The protein or RNA product the annotation is attached to.
One component of the edge key; the release never carries a null geneProduct in target.go.

frames.text: Values are UniProt accessions or RNAcentral URS identifiers.

limitations.text: No null value occurs in this release; an annotation without a named product is not represented.
The product is not a target identifier and can be a non-protein RNA product.

claims.text: The Evidence and Conclusion Ontology accession supporting the evidence code.
One component of the edge key; the empty string stands in for a null value, which occurs in about one percent of rows.

frames.text: Values are ECO accessions such as ECO:0000256. A null is most often a GO_REF annotation without an ECO mapping.

limitations.text: Null means the release lists no ECO accession for the annotation.
The ECO term refines the evidence code; it is not a confidence score.

edges.description: One GO annotation of a target.

claims.text: The target is annotated with the GO term by one cited source under one evidence code. The edge is the annotation record, not GO hierarchy.

target.id -> go.id, discriminated by (go.source, go.evidence, go.aspect, go.geneProduct, go.ecoId): key = target::HAS_GO_ANNOTATION::go.id::source::evidence::aspect::geneProduct::ecoId, with the empty string for a null ecoId; geneProduct is never null in the release.

frames.text: aspect is the GO namespace letter: P biological process, F molecular function, C cellular component. evidence is the GO evidence code (IEA, IDA, IMP, ...); ecoId is the ECO accession behind it; source is the GO_REF or PMID cited; geneProduct is the protein or RNA product the annotation attaches to.

limitations.text: No edge means the release does not list that annotation. A term can appear several times for one target with different evidence codes.
The annotation is an assertion by the cited source, not a result the release verified. Annotations to ancestor terms are not expanded: the edge names only the term the release lists.

edges.name: target_has_hallmark
edges.description: A cancer-hallmark statement attached to a target.

claims.text: The target carries the hallmark statement.
target.id -> hallmark node key: target::HAS_HALLMARK::hallmark::kind::category::pmid[::impact]::description, with impact present only for a cancerHallmark record.

frames.text: The statement fields sit on the node because one target can carry several statements for the same hallmark category. The edge asserts only that the target carries the statement.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no hallmark statement for the target; an empty hallmark struct produces no edge.
Neither attribute prose nor a cancer-hallmark label is a measured phenotype, and the release attaches no score to the statement.

edges.name: target_has_homologue

claims.text: The Ensembl compara classification of the pair.

frames.text: Six values: other_paralog (human-only, 3,484,279), ortholog_one2one (168,810, the 12 non-human species), within_species_paralog (human-only, 67,968), ortholog_many2many, ortholog_one2many and gene_split (9). Every non-human edge is an ortholog class; every human-query edge is a paralog or gene_split class.

limitations.text: The classes answer different questions: paralogues sit in one genome, orthologues across genomes, and many-to-many records a family-level correspondence with no one-to-one gene. Do not rank or pool the classes.

claims.text: The source's confidence flag for the pair, carried as the text the release writes: '1', '0' or null.

frames.text: '1' on 168,998 edges, '0' on 95,986 and null on 3,552,256. Null is exactly the human rows: the flag is only populated for cross-species orthologue pairs, so every human paralogue edge and all 9 gene_split edges carry null.

limitations.text: Null means the source states no confidence for this pair class, not low confidence; casting the column to boolean without keeping null makes 93.1% of the rows indistinguishable from '0'.
It is a source flag on a pair, not a probability, a score or a comparison between pairs of different classes.

claims.text: Percentage identity of the query gene (this target) to the homologue, on the source's 0-100 scale.

frames.text: 0-100 with no nulls; higher is closer. Measured 0.0-100.0 in 26.09.

limitations.text: Sequence identity is not functional equivalence, and the value is directional: the reverse edge carries the complement measurement.

claims.text: Percentage identity of the homologue to the query gene, on the source's 0-100 scale.

frames.text: 0-100 with no nulls. It is the same pair as queryPercentageIdentity measured from the other sequence, so the two values differ on 3,323,472 rows and are equal on 493,768.

limitations.text: Not the reverse edge's queryPercentageIdentity: that value belongs to a different row and a different alignment, so neither copy is redundant.

edges.description: The release records a homologue of the target in a species.

claims.text: One Ensembl compara homology pair: the target has the named homologue gene, with the pair class, the source's confidence flag and the two directional percentage identities.
targetId|HAS_HOMOLOGUE|speciesId|targetGeneId: 3,817,240 edges, one per source row, unique; 25,537 of the 78,733 targets have at least one edge (1-1,335 each, median 19).

frames.text: homologyType is the pair class: other_paralog 3,484,279, ortholog_one2one 168,810, within_species_paralog 67,968, ortholog_many2many 57,952, ortholog_one2many 38,222, gene_split 9. queryPercentageIdentity measures targetId against targetGeneId; targetPercentageIdentity is the same pair measured from the homologue's side. The two differ on 3,323,472 rows and agree on 493,768. isHighConfidence is the source's text flag, not a boolean.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no compara pair between the target and that gene; 53,196 targets have no homology row at all. That is a source gap, not evidence that the target has no homologue.

Human pairs are stored twice, once per direction: 3,544,066 of the 3,552,256 human rows have a reverse row with the two identity values swapped, the same homologyType and the same flag. Both directions are kept because each row is the release's own query measurement and the identity values are not symmetric; the cost is that the 1,772,033 undirected human pairs account for 3,544,066 edges, so counting edges double-counts pairs. 8,190 human rows have no reverse: 8,181 name one of the 46 human gene ids that are absent from target.id and 9 are gene_split. Only 20,864 of the 20,910 human gene ids are targets.
Each human paralogue pair is stored in both directions.
The number of HAS_HOMOLOGUE edges is the number of homologue genes, or the number of undirected pairs.
A non-human homologue is a gene record only.
A mouse or zebrafish homologue is a target of this release.

edges.name: target_has_mouse_model
edges.description: A human target has a mouse model of one of its phenotypes.

claims.text: A mouse model is recorded against one of this human target's phenotypes: the release maps the model's mouse gene to the human target and records an observed MP phenotype for the model.
targetFromSourceId|HAS_MOUSE_MODEL|biologicalModels.id: 37,474 distinct target-model pairs over the 256,254 model entries. The model id is the node key; rows repeating a pair only add phenotypes.

frames.text: targetFromSourceId is the human target: 11,869 distinct ENSG values and all of them resolve to a TargetNode. targetInModelEnsemblId is the mouse gene (11,467 ENSMUSG values) and targetInModelMgiId its MGI accession (11,467 values); neither is a human target id, so neither keys this edge. biologicalModels is an array: each element is one model, and 745 of the 256,254 elements have a null id and produce no edge.

limitations.text: No edge means the release records no mouse model for that target's phenotype. 745 of the 256,254 model entries carry a null model id and cannot be keyed.

The edge records the release's model curation, not that the mouse phenotype reproduces a human phenotype, and not that the target is validated in a mouse. One model can be attached to several human targets when the orthology mapping is not one-to-one.
A mouse model of a phenotype is model-organism evidence about the target's biology.
The mouse phenotype is the human phenotype, or that the model demonstrates the target's role in the human disease.

edges.name: target_has_prioritisation_profile
edges.description: The Target Engine's profile for a target.

claims.text: The target's prioritisation profile. The relation is 1:1 and total over the release's targets; all attributes are on the profile node.
targetId|HAS_PRIORITISATION_PROFILE|targetId: 78,733 edges, one per target.

frames.text: Read target -> profile -> attributes. The edge carries no property because the profile node key is the target id, so any attribute on the edge would be a target-level duplicate.

limitations.text: No edge means no profile was computed; none occur in 26.09.
The edge states that the release computed a profile for the target. It does not rank targets or compare profiles across releases: the Target Engine's scores are recomputed each build.

edges.name: target_has_protein_identifier
edges.description: A protein identifier that the target gene maps to.

claims.text: The target gene maps to the protein identifier.
target.id -> source:identifier: key = target::HAS_PROTEIN_IDENTIFIER::source:identifier.

frames.text: One edge per identifier; a gene can carry several, including retired UniProt accessions under uniprot_obsolete.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no protein identifier for the gene.
The edge reports a listed mapping, not an experimentally confirmed protein product or a stoichiometric claim.

edges.name: target_has_safety_event
edges.description: The target is associated with a safety observation.

claims.text: The target is associated with a safety observation reported by one datasource.
targetId|HAS_SAFETY_EVENT|safety event key: 4,387 edges, one per source row and unique.

frames.text: Read target -> observation. The observation node carries the event text, accession, datasource, citation and page.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no safety observation for the target; it is not evidence that the target is safe.

The edge repeats the source's association, not a causal adverse-effect finding, a clinical risk or a severity grade. 954 targets have at least one observation; the other targets were not assessed here.
No safety event for a target means the release has no row, not that the target has no safety liability.
A target absent from target_safety_event is safe.

edges.name: target_has_synonym
edges.description: A synonym string listed for a target.

claims.text: The target is known by the synonym under one synonym kind and source.
target.id -> (kind, source, label): key = target::HAS_SYNONYM::kind::source::label.

frames.text: kind names the array the string came from; the same label in two kinds produces two edges.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no such synonym for the target.
The edge is a naming fact. It does not mean the label is approved, current or unique to this target.

edges.name: target_has_tractability

claims.text: The release's boolean outcome for the target and bucket.

frames.text: True on 59,845 edges; false on 468,487. No value is null.

limitations.text: A null value would mean the source could not assess the bucket; none occur.
The boolean collapses whatever evidence the bucket summarises; it is not a quantity.

edges.description: The target's boolean assessment for one tractability bucket.

claims.text: The target's yes/no assessment for one tractability bucket.
targetId|HAS_TRACTABILITY|modality|category: 528,332 edges, one per target and bucket, unique.

frames.text: value is the release's boolean for the axis: 59,845 true and 468,487 false. Read modality and category on the bucket node.

limitations.text: Every assessed target has all 28 buckets, so a missing edge is a build gap rather than a negative assessment.

false is an asserted negative, not missing data. true is a source assessment, not demonstrated druggability, validated chemical matter or a clinical result. Do not count true buckets as a score or rank targets on the total.
A true bucket records the release's assessment for that axis only.
A target with several true buckets is more tractable than one with fewer; the buckets are independent evidence axes, not points.

edges.name: target_has_transcript
edges.description: A transcript belongs to a target gene.

claims.text: The transcript is annotated as a product of the target gene.
(targetId, transcriptId). 644,292 edges; every targetId resolves to target.id and transcriptId is unique, so 0 keys duplicate.

frames.text: Read target -> transcript. Exactly one transcript per target is the Ensembl canonical transcript; the rest are alternatives.

limitations.text: A target with no edge has no transcript rows in the release.
The edge asserts annotation, not expression. A transcript with no proteinId is non-coding, and sharing a target does not make two transcripts functionally equivalent.

edges.name: target_localised_in
edges.description: A localisation statement reported for a target.

claims.text: The target is reported at the subcellular location.

target.id -> (location, source, termSL, labelSL, targetModifier): key = target::LOCALISED_IN::subcellular_location::location::source::termSL::labelSL::targetModifier, with the empty string for a null component.

frames.text: The statement is on the location node. A target can have several edges for the same location when sources or isoforms differ.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no localisation for the target.
The edge repeats a resource's statement; it is not a measurement made in this release and not a claim about every cell type.

edges.name: target_participates_in_pathway

claims.text: The release's top-level Reactome category for the pathway.
A qualifier of the membership, not part of the edge key.

frames.text: Examples are Signal Transduction, Immune System and Metabolism.

limitations.text: The release's pathways array never carries a null topLevelTerm.

go.id; 48,340 rows and 48,340 distinct ids.

child go.id and parent go.id joined by '|'; 57,456 edges with 57,456 distinct pairs.

frames.text: The source row is the child and the array element the direct parent. Several parents on one row stay several edges.

limitations.text: An empty isA array emits no edge. Every emitted parent resolves to a go row, so this binding introduces no dangling endpoint.

limitations.text: An empty negativelyRegulates array emits no edge. Every emitted target resolves to a live go row.

claims.text: One GOTermPartOfEdge per element of go.partOf.
child go.id and parent go.id joined by '|'; 7,058 edges over 6,613 child terms, with unique pairs.

frames.text: The source row is the part and the array element the whole. Every emitted parent resolves to a go row.

limitations.text: An empty partOf array emits no edge; 41,727 rows are empty, which is normal for molecular-function terms.
Part-of is a separate predicate from is-a. 786 edges cross GO branches, so the edges are not confined to the child's namespace.

frames.text: Direction follows the column: the source row regulates the array element. The sign is absent here and carried by the negative and positive edge types.

speciesId|targetGeneId: 228,395 nodes from 3,817,240 rows. The binding reads every homology row, so a gene cited by many targets collapses to one node.

limitations.text: A row with a null speciesId or targetGeneId cannot be keyed and is dropped; the release carries none. A gene absent here was reported for no target.
The node is not a TargetNode and the binding does not resolve the accession: 207,485 of the 228,395 nodes are outside target.id.

frames.text: Read homologue gene -> target. 20,864 edges end at a TargetNode and 46 dangle, because 46 human homology gene ids are absent from target.id (8,181 rows).

limitations.text: No edge means the gene is one of the 207,485 non-human genes: the binding filters on speciesId 9606 and never mints a target for another species.

The filter is the species, not a resolution check: the binding cannot look up the target table, so the 46 unresolved human ids emit an edge that dangles. They are reported rather than silently joining or inventing a target.

limitations.text: interactionId is never null, so every row keys a node. A null scoring means the source database does not score interactions.

The node is not reduced to a target-target edge because one participant pair can carry several interaction ids and because the two-sided roles and species have no place on a single edge. The participants are edges.

limitations.text: A null targetA cannot key the edge; none occur.
The binding cannot verify target existence, so the non-human ids are emitted. The edge states the source's first participant, not a bait-prey or direction-of-effect role.

limitations.text: No edge means B was not resolved to a release target, not that the interaction has one participant. The 278,519 null-targetB rows still name a participant in intB.
A missing B edge is a resolution limit of the source's identifier mapping, not evidence about the interaction's biology.

source:identifier, the shared cross-reference key stated on CrossReferenceNode. A molecule's listing contributes one node; molecules sharing the pair share the node.

The node records a listed identifier. It does not verify the external record or assert identity between molecules that cite it. The shared key is case-sensitive and source spellings differ across datasets, so the same authority can yield two nodes (drugbank here, DrugBank on a target).

A name node does not assert that two molecules are the same substance or that the name is registered.
