trade_name::tradeNames.source::tradeNames.label. A trade name cited by several molecules is emitted once per citation and collapses to one node on this key.

frames.text: The node is the string and its authority; the trade_name:: key prefix and the TRADE_NAME edge both say the release recorded it as a trade name.

limitations.text: A pair with a null label or source cannot be keyed and is dropped; the release has no such rows for trade names.
A name node does not assert that two molecules are the same substance or that the product is marketed.

claims.text: One MouseModelNode per biologicalModels element of mouse_phenotype.
mouse_phenotype.biologicalModels.id, the MGI model accession; 35,929 distinct ids over 256,254 entries, 745 entries with a null id dropped.

frames.text: The same model is cited by many phenotype and IMPC evidence rows. The node carries its allelic composition and background.

limitations.text: A null model id cannot be keyed and emits no node. A model absent here is not in the release's mouse phenotype file.
Phenotypes are edges from IMPC evidence, not properties of the model. The mouse gene and mapped human phenotypes are separate records.

claims.text: The MP phenotype observed for each mouse model on the row.
biologicalModels.id|HAS_PHENOTYPE|modelPhenotypeId: 243,341 distinct model-phenotype pairs; repeated rows collapse.

frames.text: modelPhenotypeId is never null and is an MP accession in colon form; 10,584 distinct terms occur and each has a PhenotypeNode.

limitations.text: A null modelPhenotypeId cannot key the edge; none occur.
The edge pairs every model element of the row with the row's phenotype; a row listing several models attributes the phenotype to each of them, as the release does.

claims.text: One HAS_PHENOTYPE_CLASS edge per model element and modelPhenotypeClasses element of a row.
biologicalModels.id|HAS_PHENOTYPE_CLASS|modelPhenotypeClasses.id: 127,802 distinct model-class pairs from 344,055 expanded combinations; duplicate pairs collapse.

frames.text: modelPhenotypeClasses is a closed 28-term MP vocabulary with non-null ids and labels. The binding expands both arrays, so a row with several models and several classes produces the cross product; the collapse removes the repeats. 21 class ids also occur as observations and are already bound there with the same label.

limitations.text: A null class id cannot key the edge; none occur.
The class is a broad system label attached to the row's phenotype, not an ontology parent edge between the observed MP term and the class; the release supplies no MP hierarchy.

claims.text: One SUPPORTED_BY edge per PMID in a model entry's literature array.
biologicalModels.id|SUPPORTED_BY|pmid: 130,911 distinct model-pmid pairs from 1,249,431 PMID elements; duplicate pairs collapse.

frames.text: 23,437 of the 24,380 distinct PMIDs resolve to a PublicationNode, so 943 leave a dangling endpoint. The array holds 1-8 PMIDs per entry.

limitations.text: A null literature array emits no edge; 40,752 model entries have none.
The binding cannot verify publication existence, so PMIDs outside the release's literature corpus are emitted. The edge is the model record's citation, not the IMPC evidence citation.

claims.text: One ObsoleteTermNode per element of disease.obsoleteTerms.
obsolete_term::accession. The 9,852 elements are 9,838 distinct accessions, so 14 duplicates collapse.

frames.text: None of the elements is a disease.id or a disease_hpo.id, so the target is a term node and not a DISEASE node.

limitations.text: No element means the term lists no retired accession.
The node keeps a retired accession addressable; it carries no successor and no definition.

claims.text: One ObsoleteTermNode per element of disease_hpo.obsoleteTerms.
obsolete_term::accession, the node key shared with the disease binding. The 5,955 elements are 5,955 distinct accessions.

frames.text: None of the accessions is a disease_hpo.id, so the target is a term node. 297 of them are disease.id values but stay retired accessions rather than resolving to the DISEASE node with the same string.

limitations.text: No element means the phenotype term lists no retired accession.
The node keeps a retired accession addressable and carries no successor or definition.

claims.text: One PgxAnnotationNode per row of pharmacogenomics.

studyId|genotype|variantId|variantFunctionalConsequenceId|targetFromSourceId|pgxCategory|phenotypeText|phenotypeFromSourceId|drug set: 33,479 keys for 33,479 rows. The drug set is the sorted drugId|drugFromSource pairs, with the empty string for a null component. Every part is needed: dropping studyId leaves 32,551 distinct keys, phenotypeText 29,503, the drug set 26,558, targetFromSourceId 24,997, genotype 23,929, pgxCategory 32,495, variantId 33,366, variantFunctionalConsequenceId 33,473 and phenotypeFromSourceId 33,471.

frames.text: The node carries the annotation's scalars. The variant, gene, drugs, mapped phenotype and citations are edges; studyId is ClinPGx's annotation accession, not a study.

limitations.text: A row with a null studyId, genotype, pgxCategory or drugs array cannot be keyed and is dropped; the release carries none. Null nullable parts key as the empty string and stay null properties.

The key mixes text (genotype, phenotypeText) and a derived drug set, so a re-wording in a later release is a new node. genotypeId, variantRsId and haplotypeId do not discriminate and are properties only.

claims.text: One HAS_DRUG edge per drugs element with a ChEMBL id.
annotation key|HAS_DRUG|drugId: 29,613 edges over 29,391 rows; 532 distinct ids, 29,328 resolving.

frames.text: Each element of the drugs array (1-3 per row) is one edge. drugFromSource is the ClinPGx name on the edge.

limitations.text: Elements with a null drugId emit no edge: 4,094 elements on 4,088 rows. No row has an empty array.
285 edges (three ChEMBL ids) dangle because drug_molecule does not hold them; the binding reports rather than drops them.

claims.text: One HAS_MAPPED_PHENOTYPE edge per pharmacogenomics row with a mapped disease id.
annotation key|HAS_MAPPED_PHENOTYPE|phenotypeFromSourceId: 724 edges over 30 distinct ids, all resolving.

frames.text: MONDO_0018493 carries 581 edges; the other 29 terms carry the rest.

limitations.text: Null phenotypeFromSourceId (32,755 rows) emits no edge; phenotypeText is present on 31,625 of those rows, so the absence is a failed label match rather than an absent phenotype.
The binding does not derive a disease term from phenotypeText: the release's own mapping is the only supported join.

claims.text: One HAS_TARGET edge per pharmacogenomics row with a gene id.
annotation key|HAS_TARGET|targetFromSourceId: 31,910 edges over 1,152 distinct Ensembl ids.

frames.text: The id is used unchanged as the target node key: 1,101 of the 1,152 ids are target rows (25,295 edges).

limitations.text: No edge means targetFromSourceId is null on 1,569 rows. 6,615 edges (51 ids) name an Ensembl gene absent from target.id and therefore dangle.
The binding cannot consult the target table, so it cannot drop the 51 unresolved ids; it emits the release's own gene id and reports the dangling rate instead of inventing a target.

claims.text: One HAS_VARIANT edge per pharmacogenomics row with a variantId.
annotation key|HAS_VARIANT|variantId: 16,169 edges, one per non-null variantId; 2,882 distinct ids, all resolving.

frames.text: Rows with a null variantId are filtered out rather than pointed at a stand-in variant: 17,310 rows (51.7%), the 9,548 haplotype-anchored rows and 7,762 rsID-anchored genotypes that reduce to the reference.

limitations.text: No edge means the row states no derived variant.
variantRsId is not used as an alternative key: 14 of its 2,843 distinct values resolve to no variant row, and the release is not keyed by rsID.

claims.text: One SUPPORTED_BY edge per literature element of a pharmacogenomics row.
annotation key|SUPPORTED_BY|pmid: 140,757 edges; no pair repeats within a row.

frames.text: The literature array is never null or empty. 5,732 of the 5,952 distinct PMIDs are publication nodes, so 135,223 edges resolve.

limitations.text: No edge would mean the row cites nothing; none occur. 5,534 edges on 220 PMIDs dangle because the release's publication corpus does not hold them.
The same PMID is repeated on every row of one annotation, so edge counts are annotation-row counts, not distinct papers. A citation does not verify the claim it is attached to.

claims.text: One PhenotypeNode per row of disease_hpo.

phenotype::accession. The prefix keeps the key disjoint from DISEASE: 2,399 of these accessions (2,183 HP, 213 GO, 2 PATO, 1 UBERON) are also disease.id values, and a raw accession would silently resolve an edge to the DISEASE node of the same string.

frames.text: 32,082 rows carry 32,082 distinct ids, of which 19,836 are HP terms; the rest are the imported terms the phenotype hierarchy relies on (UBERON 5,641, GO 2,443, CHEBI 1,927, CL 1,187, PATO 571, PR 321, MPATH 75, NBO 64, HsapDv 16, RO 1).

limitations.text: A term absent here is outside the release's phenotype hierarchy. A null description (3,451 rows) is a vocabulary gap, not a missing term; disease_hpo.description is not carried because PhenotypeNode declares no description property in this build.

The node set is a phenotype hierarchy, not an HPO-only list: a non-HP accession is a term the hierarchy imports, not a phenotype annotation. The node key prefix is a build convention; the identity is the accession.

claims.text: One PhenotypeNode per MP term named by mouse_phenotype.
phenotype::MP:<accession>; 203,583 rows and 10,584 distinct MP accessions. The prefix matches the disease_hpo phenotype key convention and keeps the key disjoint from DISEASE.

frames.text: The MP accession is used as written (colon form). 10,368 of the 10,373 MP accessions cited by evidence_impc are present here.

limitations.text: A term absent here is outside the mouse_phenotype file; five evidence_impc MP accessions have no node.
An MP term is a mouse phenotype vocabulary term, not an HPO term. The two vocabularies are not merged.

claims.text: One PhenotypeNode per distinct modelPhenotypeClasses element, so the 28 MP class terms exist as terms.
modelPhenotypeClasses.id: 28 distinct MP accessions. 21 are also bound from modelPhenotypeId with the same label and collapse; 7 occur only here.

frames.text: The class ids are MP accessions in colon form (MP:0001186 pigmentation phenotype, MP:0005367 renal/urinary system phenotype) and the labels agree with the observation labels where both occur.

limitations.text: A null class id cannot key the node; none occur.
The class terms are broader than the observed phenotypes and have no published MP parent edges in this release, so their only relation is HAS_PHENOTYPE_CLASS from the model.

claims.text: One CrossReferenceNode per element of disease_hpo.dbXRefs.
source:identifier, the shared cross-reference key. The 43,966 elements are 43,966 distinct pairs within a term.

frames.text: source is the text before the first colon (FMA, CALOHA, MESH, GO, BTO, EMAPA, UBERON and others); identifier is the remainder. Every value carries a colon.

limitations.text: No element means the phenotype term lists no external identifier.
The shared node type means an identifier listed by a target, disease or phenotype is one node with several inbound edges. A listed identifier is not a verified external record.

claims.text: One HAS_CROSS_REFERENCE edge per element of disease_hpo.dbXRefs.
phenotype::accession::HAS_CROSS_REFERENCE::source:identifier; 43,966 distinct keys over 43,966 elements.

frames.text: Read term -> identifier; the edge carries no qualifier.

limitations.text: No element means the release lists no such identifier for the term.
A listed identifier does not merge two terms and is not verification of the external record.

claims.text: One HAS_OBSOLETE_TERM edge per element of disease_hpo.obsoleteTerms.
phenotype::accession::HAS_OBSOLETE_TERM::accession; 5,955 distinct keys.

frames.text: Read current term -> retired accession. All 5,955 targets resolve to the ObsoleteTermNode set populated from the same array.

limitations.text: No element means the term lists no retired accession.
The edge states no merge or replacement and cannot be traversed backwards to a current term.

claims.text: One IS_A edge per element of disease_hpo.parents.
phenotype::child::IS_A::parent. The 43,659 elements are 43,659 distinct pairs; the prefix keeps the key disjoint from a DISEASE IS_A edge over the same accession pair.

frames.text: Read child -> parent. 15 terms carry a null parents array and 0 carry an empty one, so no term is listed without a parent in this release.

limitations.text: No edge means the term lists no parent. All 43,659 parents resolve to a disease_hpo row (0 dangling).
The parents are not all HP terms, so one edge can leave the HPO branch. The disease_hpo dataset ships no ancestors, descendants or children arrays, so ancestors must be reached by traversal.

claims.text: One PrioritisationProfileNode per row of target_prioritisation, keyed by the target.
target_prioritisation.targetId: 78,733 rows and 78,733 distinct ids, all resolving to a TargetNode, so the node is 1:1 with the target universe.

frames.text: The integer flags are stored as integers, not booleans, because null is an unassessed state and because hasSafetyEvent and isCancerDriverGene encode true as -1 and never as 1. Null is the feature not being computed; -1 is a measured present for those two columns and a sentinel of unknown meaning on the distribution columns.

limitations.text: A null targetId cannot key the node; none occur. A missing profile would mean the target was not prioritised; none occur in 26.09.

The binding copies the release's encodings without converting them, so the reader must apply the per-property rules; no value is rescaled or re-signed. It does not join the profile back to tractability, safety, probe or expression rows.
The profile keys on the target, so it adds no entity the target does not already have.
The profile node can be used as an independent assessment, or that two profiles can be compared across releases.

claims.text: One ProteinNode per element of target.proteinIds.
source:identifier, the node key.

frames.text: The same accession listed for several targets yields one node with several inbound edges.

limitations.text: A null source or identifier cannot key the node and drops the row; the release carries none.
The binding does not check that the accession is current and does not create an edge to a transcript.

claims.text: One PublicationNode per literature entry in literature_entity_lut.

literature_entity_lut.pmid. The table's grain is (pmid, keywordId), so the binding emits one record per grounded mention, 173,137,629 of them, and the build's exact-duplicate collapse leaves one record per identifier: 21,938,364 distinct keys, one record per key. The source's date/year are not node properties because one key carries two dates; publication dates remain on study and evidence records.

frames.text: pmid is the release's literature key, not always a PubMed id: 899,451 of the 21,938,364 keys are not PubMed numbers, 895,626 prefixed PPR, PMC, IND, CAIN, ADL, FNI or c (preprints and Europe PMC records) and 3,825 sixteen-digit numbers above the PubMed range. Numeric keys top out at 42,701,903. 5,740,182 identifiers carry a pmcid and 16,198,182 do not; date and year are null on 16 rows.

limitations.text: pmid is never null in 26.09, so no placeholder identity is minted. A paper absent here is outside the release's text-mined corpus; that is not a claim that the paper does not exist.

The node set is the corpus the release mined for entities, not every publication the release cites: the 174 study PMIDs outside it keep no node although PUBLISHED_AS still names them. Month and day are not carried because the release's day is an upstream placeholder on most rows. literature_vector is a word-embedding table keyed by word and category, with no entity identifier, so it is not a graph relation and no node or edge binds it.
literature_vector does not add publication-entity edges; the mention layer comes from literature_entity_lut alone.
The embedding table supplies additional or stronger mentions.

claims.text: One MENTIONS_DISEASE edge per DS pair in literature_entity_lut.
pmid::MENTIONS_DISEASE::keywordId, from the 81,182,673 rows whose keywordType is DS.

frames.text: keywordId is used unchanged as the disease node key; all 81,182,673 pairs resolve to disease.id (14,069 distinct terms). relevance is copied from the row.

limitations.text: A pair with no DS grounding has no edge; dropping the row is not an assertion that the paper does not mention a disease.

The full set is emitted with no relevance cutoff: the release defines no threshold, and a cutoff would make 'no mention' indistinguishable from 'below threshold'. Filter on the relevance property at read time instead.

claims.text: One MENTIONS_MOLECULE edge per CD pair in literature_entity_lut.
pmid::MENTIONS_MOLECULE::keywordId, from the 36,002,868 rows whose keywordType is CD.

frames.text: keywordId is used unchanged as the molecule node key; all 36,002,868 pairs resolve to drug_molecule.id (14,043 distinct ChEMBL molecules). relevance is copied from the row.

limitations.text: A pair with no CD grounding has no edge; a drug named by a brand or code the matcher did not ground is not represented.
The full set is emitted with no relevance cutoff, as for the other mention classes; threshold on the relevance property at read time.

claims.text: One MENTIONS_TARGET edge per GP pair in literature_entity_lut.
pmid::MENTIONS_TARGET::keywordId, from the 55,952,088 rows whose keywordType is GP.

frames.text: keywordId is used unchanged as the target node key; all 55,952,088 pairs resolve to target.id (30,464 distinct Ensembl genes). relevance is copied from the row.

limitations.text: A pair with no GP grounding has no edge; a gene named only by an unmatched symbol is not represented.
The full set is emitted with no relevance cutoff, as for disease mentions; threshold on the relevance property at read time.

claims.text: One ReactomePathwayNode per row of reactome.
reactome.id; 2,883 rows and 2,883 distinct R-HSA- accessions.

frames.text: The node carries the pathway label only. The hierarchy is the PathwayIsPartOfEdge set.

limitations.text: A pathway absent from reactome is outside the release's pathway set. No id or label is null.
ancestors, descendants, children and path stay in the source: children is the reverse of parents, the closures repeat a walk, and path is an ordered route rather than a relation.

claims.text: One PathwayIsPartOfEdge per element of reactome.parents.
child reactome.id and parent reactome.id joined by '|'; 2,899 edges with 2,899 distinct pairs.

frames.text: The source row is the child and the array element the direct parent; up to 6 parents stay separate edges. All parent keys resolve to reactome rows, and parents and children are exact inverses here.

limitations.text: An empty parents array marks one of the 29 root pathways and emits no edge.
Ancestors and descendants are not expanded: they are transitive closures of this edge. path is not expanded because it is an ordered route per top-level branch, not a distinct predicate.

claims.text: One RegulatoryElementNode per row of enhancer_to_gene, keyed by intervalId.
enhancer_to_gene.intervalId: 48,808,491 rows and 48,806,245 distinct ids. The 2,246 rows that repeat an id are exact duplicates and collapse in the build.

frames.text: resourceScore is split into two parallel arrays because a graph property cannot hold an array of structs; the names are always [DNase, HiC_contacts] in that order, so position pairs the name with its value.

limitations.text: A null intervalId cannot key the node; none occur. A null pmid or biosampleId would only drop the corresponding edge, not the node.

The node is a study-specific prediction, not a distinct genomic element: 38,343,584 distinct coordinates exist and one interval-gene pair recurs once per study. The binding does not deduplicate across studies.

claims.text: The biosample each E2G prediction was made in.
intervalId|ACTIVE_IN|biosampleId: 48,806,245 edges, unique and 1:1 with the element node.

frames.text: All 322 distinct biosampleId values resolve to a BiosampleNode; the biosampleName on the same row is not carried because the node holds it.

limitations.text: A null biosampleId cannot key the edge; none occur.
The edge states the prediction's assay context, not measured activity in a sample; biosampleFromSourceId is null on every row.

claims.text: The gene each E2G prediction links to its regulatory element.
intervalId|REGULATES|geneId: 48,806,245 edges, unique and 1:1 with the element node.

frames.text: All 20,088 distinct geneId values resolve to a TargetNode, so the binding leaves no dangling endpoint.

limitations.text: A null geneId cannot key the edge; none occur.
The edge direction is element -> target even though the source row is gene-anchored; it is a prediction, and the source's score and distance stay on the element node.

claims.text: The publication cited by each E2G prediction row.
intervalId|SUPPORTED_BY|pmid: 48,806,245 edges; pmid is 38014075 on every row.

frames.text: 38014075 resolves to a PublicationNode, so the edge leaves no dangling endpoint.

limitations.text: A null or empty pmid cannot key the edge; none occur.
The edge is constant across the dataset and adds no discrimination; it records the citation, not per-element evidence.
Every E2G element cites the same publication in 26.09.
The paper supports each individual element-gene prediction, or that the edge distinguishes elements.

claims.text: One SafetyEventNode per row of target_safety_event.
targetId|event|datasource|eventId|url, with the empty string where eventId or url is null: 4,387 rows and 4,387 distinct keys.

frames.text: event is source free text; eventId is the source's ontology accession where supplied. The target is not stored on the node; the HAS_SAFETY_EVENT edge carries it.

limitations.text: A row with a null targetId, event or datasource cannot be keyed and is dropped; the release carries none. A null url keys as the empty string and stays a null property.

The node key contains the target even though the target is not a property, so two targets sharing an event row produce two nodes with identical properties. The node does not normalise the event to an ontology term.

claims.text: One HAS_EFFECT edge per effects element of a safety row.
safety event key|HAS_EFFECT|direction|dosing: 2,349 edges, unique per observation and descriptor.

frames.text: 2,314 rows carry effects; 35 carry two and therefore two edges. The 2,073 rows with a null effects array emit none.

limitations.text: No edge means the observation states no effect.
The edge does not rank multiple effects and does not assert a mechanism or a clinical direction.

claims.text: One OBSERVED_IN edge per non-null tissueId in a biosamples element.
safety event key|OBSERVED_IN|normalised tissueId: 5,072 edges over the 2,601 observations that name a tissue, unique per observation and tissue.

frames.text: The 31 elements written with a colon (UBERON:...) are normalised to the underscore form before the join, so every edge names a BiosampleNode. An observation lists up to six tissues.

limitations.text: No edge means the observation names no tissue: 438 biosample elements are cell-only and 1,786 rows have no biosamples array.
cellId is null on all 5,599 elements, so cell labels and cell formats do not become nodes or edges. The source tissueLabel is not carried; the biosample node's name is the vocabulary label.

claims.text: One SafetyEventEffectNode per distinct effects element.
direction|dosing, with the empty string for a null dosing: 9 nodes from 2,349 array elements. The binding reads every effects element, so the repeated descriptors collapse to nine records.

frames.text: direction is the signed statement; dosing is the context label.

limitations.text: A row with a null or empty effects array emits no effect record.
The node set is a closed nine-value vocabulary, not an entity set; the HAS_EFFECT edge, not the node, ties a descriptor to an observation.

claims.text: One SOTermNode per row of so.
so.id; 2,620 rows and 2,620 distinct SO: accessions.

frames.text: The node names a consequence class. Consequence columns elsewhere in the release write the underscore form and must be converted to join.

limitations.text: A term absent from so is outside the release's SO subset. No id or label is null.
The node carries no severity or impact; those are properties of the specific consequence edge.

claims.text: One StudyNode per row of study.
study.studyId.

frames.text: Publication fields are copied to the study; a publication can back several studies. The study is the analysis, not the paper.

limitations.text: Missing sample-size or publication fields are release gaps. A study with no summary statistics still exists as a study record.
Do not aggregate study rows by publication or by trait without stating the unit; molecular QTL studies are split by target and biosample.

claims.text: The study that produced each credible set.
studyId -> studyLocusId.

frames.text: A study can have many credible sets.

limitations.text: The edge does not assert a causal variant or a causal gene.

claims.text: One edge per study with a non-null biosampleId.
(studyId, biosampleId). 2,838,730 edges, 0 duplicates.

frames.text: Every QTL row has a biosampleId; all GWAS rows are filtered by drop_null. Every biosampleId resolves to biosample.biosampleId, over 128 distinct biosamples.

limitations.text: No edge for a GWAS study; it has no molecular assay context here.
The measurement context is coarse and is not evidence of expression in every condition.

claims.text: One edge per study with a non-null geneId.
(studyId, geneId). 2,838,730 edges, 0 duplicates.

frames.text: Every QTL row has a geneId; all 165,517 GWAS rows are filtered by drop_null. Every geneId resolves to target.id.

limitations.text: No edge for a GWAS study; it measures a trait, not a gene.
The measured gene is not an association, a causal gene or a drug target.

claims.text: The publication cited by each study record, one edge per study with a PubMed reference.
studyId::PUBLISHED_AS::pmid; a study has at most one pubmedId, and 3,001,294 of the 3,004,247 study rows carry one.

frames.text: Rows with a null pubmedId are dropped rather than pointed at a stand-in publication.

limitations.text: No edge means the study record has no PubMed reference, not that the study is unpublished elsewhere.

2,107,334 of the emitted edges name a PMID absent from literature_entity_lut (174 of 7,703 distinct PMIDs, mostly three large QTL papers), so those edges have no publication node to point at until the publication universe is widened beyond the text-mined corpus.

claims.text: One edge per study diseaseIds element.
(studyId, diseaseId). 194,151 edges, 0 duplicates.

frames.text: 165,517 GWAS studies carry the array; QTL studies carry an empty array and produce no edge. Every diseaseId resolves to disease.id.

limitations.text: No edge for a QTL study or a study with an unmapped trait.
The edge is the release's trait mapping, not a diagnosis and not a verified ontology equivalence.

claims.text: One SubcellularLocationNode per element of target.subcellularLocations.
subcellular_location::location::source::termSL::labelSL::targetModifier, with the empty string for a null component.

frames.text: The same location reported by two sources or for two isoforms is two nodes; a shared free-text location alone does not merge them.

limitations.text: The release never carries a null location or source; null termSL, labelSL and targetModifier are encoded as empty strings in the key but stay null as properties.
The node is a statement record, not an ontology term; termSL is the only normalized handle.

claims.text: One SynonymNode per element of target.synonyms.
synonym::synonym::source::label.

frames.text: The kind is the literal 'synonym' because the string came from the general synonym array, not from symbolSynonyms or nameSynonyms.

limitations.text: No element means the release lists no general synonym for the target.
The node is vocabulary-level; a label shared by two targets is one node with two inbound edges.

claims.text: One SynonymNode per element of target.symbolSynonyms.
synonym::symbolSynonym::source::label.

frames.text: kind separates alternative symbols from general synonyms and alternative names, so the same string in two arrays stays two nodes.

limitations.text: No element means the release lists no alternative symbol.
An alternative symbol is not the approvedSymbol property.

claims.text: One SynonymNode per element of target.nameSynonyms.
synonym::nameSynonym::source::label.

frames.text: kind separates alternative names from general synonyms and alternative symbols.

limitations.text: No element means the release lists no alternative name.
An alternative name is not the approvedName property.

claims.text: One TargetNode per row of target, keyed by the Ensembl gene id.
target.id

frames.text: The node carries the gene-level annotation. Protein, transcript, pathway, ontology and cross-reference facts are separate edges.

limitations.text: A row with a null id cannot be keyed and is dropped. The release's target rows otherwise have an id.
A TargetNode is not a protein structure, a transcript or a complex. Do not read a gene-level property as an isoform-specific fact.

claims.text: One edge per target-disease pair in association_overall_direct, carrying the release's direct aggregate.
The (targetId, diseaseId) pair; aggregationValue is constant 'None'.

frames.text: The score is a weighted aggregate over direct evidence. Evidence count counts contributing evidence rows, not independent studies.

limitations.text: No row means no direct aggregate for the pair; it is not a measured zero association.
The yearly timeseries is not carried on the edge; use currentNovelty only as a recent-growth signal. The score is not causal.

claims.text: One ASSOCIATED_WITH_BY_DATASOURCE_DIRECT edge per row of association_by_datasource_direct: a target, disease and datasource with the release's direct aggregate for that scope.

target::ASSOCIATED_WITH_BY_DATASOURCE_DIRECT::disease::datasource, which is (targetId, diseaseId, aggregationValue). The 7,522,466 rows give 7,522,466 distinct keys, so no row collapses; aggregationType is the constant 'datasourceId'.

frames.text: 7,225,847 pairs produce 1 to 13 edges each. Every edge stores aggregationValue as a categorical id, not a score. The pair set is the same as association_overall_direct, so this layer partitions the overall report.

limitations.text: A null targetId, diseaseId or aggregationValue would drop the row; the release carries none. No edge means the datasource reported no direct aggregate for the pair, not a measured zero.
Per-source scores are not shares of the overall score and are not comparable across datasources. The timeseries array is not carried on the edge; currentNovelty is the only temporal signal here.

claims.text: One ASSOCIATED_WITH_BY_DATASOURCE_INDIRECT edge per row of association_by_datasource_indirect: a target, disease and datasource with the release's descendant-inclusive aggregate for that scope.

target::ASSOCIATED_WITH_BY_DATASOURCE_INDIRECT::disease::datasource, which is (targetId, diseaseId, aggregationValue). The 20,852,416 rows give 20,852,416 distinct keys; aggregationType is the constant 'datasourceId'.

frames.text: 17,459,960 pairs produce 1 to 18 edges each. Evidence at a descendant disease term is copied to every ancestor before folding, so a score can rest on evidence that never cites this term. expression_atlas is the only source not propagated. Every direct (pair, source) key is also present here.

limitations.text: A null targetId, diseaseId or aggregationValue would drop the row; the release carries none. No edge means no indirect aggregate at this scope, not a measured zero and not an absent direct association.

Indirect scores are not comparable with direct scores, with another datasource's score, or with the overall indirect score, which applies the release's per-source weights. The timeseries array is not carried.

claims.text: One ASSOCIATED_WITH_BY_DATATYPE_DIRECT edge per row of association_by_datatype_direct: a target, disease and datatype with the release's direct aggregate for that evidence-type bucket.

target::ASSOCIATED_WITH_BY_DATATYPE_DIRECT::disease::datatype, which is (targetId, diseaseId, aggregationValue). The 7,495,759 rows give 7,495,759 distinct keys; aggregationType is the constant 'datatypeId'.

frames.text: 7,225,847 pairs produce 1 to 7 edges each, the same pair set as the overall direct and datasource layers. aggregationValue is one of eight datatype ids, a categorical label, not a score. A datatype can combine several datasources; clinical-precedence evidence is bucketed as known_drug.

limitations.text: A null targetId, diseaseId or aggregationValue would drop the row; the release carries none. No edge means the datatype reported no direct aggregate for the pair, not a measured zero.
A datatype score applies no datasource weight and is not the sum of the member datasource scores; the overall score applies the release's per-source weights. The timeseries array is not carried.

target::ASSOCIATED_WITH_BY_DATATYPE_INDIRECT::disease::datatype, which is (targetId, diseaseId, aggregationValue). The 20,453,173 rows give 20,453,173 distinct keys; aggregationType is the constant 'datatypeId'.

frames.text: 17,459,960 pairs produce 1 to 8 edges each. Evidence at a descendant disease term is copied to every ancestor before folding; rna_expression carries no inherited evidence because its only source is not propagated. Every direct (pair, datatype) key is also present here.

claims.text: One edge per target-disease pair in association_overall_indirect, carrying the release's ontology-propagated aggregate.
The (targetId, diseaseId) pair.

frames.text: The score includes evidence propagated through the disease ontology; it is not a direct observation for this pair.

limitations.text: No row means no propagated aggregate; it does not mean the direct association is absent.
Indirect and direct scores are different quantities and must not be compared or merged.

claims.text: One BELONGS_TO_CLASS edge per element of target.targetClass.
target::BELONGS_TO_CLASS::target_class::id::label::level.

frames.text: Each ancestor class of the target is a separate element and therefore a separate edge.

limitations.text: No element means the release does not classify the target.
The edge states membership in a curated class, not a functional assay.

claims.text: One edge per row of evidence_clinical_precedence, keyed by the evidence id rather than the target-disease pair.
evidence_clinical_precedence.id; 876,506 rows are 876,506 distinct ids, so several edges can join one target-disease pair.

frames.text: All 1,519 target ids resolve in target, all 3,115 disease ids in disease and all 4,460 drug ids in drug_molecule. Every row has a report, stage, score and trait direction. studyStartDate, evidenceDate and publicationDate stay source text; they are not parsed dates.

limitations.text: No row means no report-drug-target-disease combination; validation-flagged rows are diverted and their count is not recoverable.

The edge is inferred through the drug, so it is not mechanistic evidence for the target in the disease. qualityControls is empty on every published row, and datasourceId and datatypeId are constant (clinical_precedence, clinical), so neither is carried.

claims.text: One EXPRESSED_IN edge per row of baseline_expression: the row's distribution, attached to the cell-type biosample when the row has one and otherwise to the tissue biosample.

targetId|EXPRESSED_IN|datasourceId|tissueBiosampleId|celltypeBiosampleId|tissueBiosampleFromSource|celltypeBiosampleFromSource, with the empty string for a null id or label: 83,290,030 rows and 83,289,724 distinct keys.

frames.text: The endpoint is celltypeBiosampleId when present, else tissueBiosampleId; both ids are edge properties. All 1,239 distinct tissue ids and 1,286 distinct cell-type ids resolve exactly in biosample.biosampleId. A row without a targetId cannot key the edge; none occur.

limitations.text: No edge means the release has no baseline measurement for the target in that context. Rows with both biosample ids null would key an empty endpoint; none occur.

The binding does not resolve targetFromSourceId, which holds UniProt accessions on the 504,046 PRIDE rows. 306 rows share a key with another row and differ only in their quantiles, so they remain two edges with the same key.

claims.text: One HAS_CHEMICAL_PROBE edge per chemical_probe row with a ChEMBL drug id.
targetId|HAS_CHEMICAL_PROBE|drugId|drugFromSourceId: 1,199 edges. (targetId, drugId) has only 1,263 distinct values; both colliding pairs have a null drugId, so drugFromSourceId completes the key.

frames.text: The edge targets the MoleculeNode named by drugId. drugFromSourceId is the probe source's own id, not a ChEMBL id.

limitations.text: 66 rows have no drugId and emit no edge: they name a probe only by the source id, and a MoleculeNode is a ChEMBL molecule. All 1,199 non-null drug ids resolve to a molecule row.
urls stays in the source, and targetFromSourceId is not carried because targetId is the resolved Ensembl id. NaN in the two activity scores is a missing marker, not a score.

claims.text: One HAS_CONSTRAINT edge per element of target.constraint, carrying that family's metrics.
target::HAS_CONSTRAINT::constraint_type::constraintType; the release holds at most one row per target and family.

frames.text: Null metrics are carried as null; they are not coerced to zero. obs/exp and the oe bounds are counts and ratios, score is the release's ranking statistic.

limitations.text: No element means the family was not computed for the target.
The metrics are not comparable across families and do not establish essentiality or pathogenicity.

claims.text: One HAS_CROSS_REFERENCE edge per element of target.dbXrefs.
target::HAS_CROSS_REFERENCE::source:identifier.

frames.text: Read from the target to the identifier; the edge carries no qualifier.

limitations.text: No element means the release listed no such identifier for the target.
The edge asserts a listed identifier, not that the external record was verified or that two entities are the same.

claims.text: One CrossReferenceNode per element of target.dbXrefs.
source:identifier.

frames.text: Other domains may bind the same node type; the shared key space means an identifier listed by two entities is one node.

limitations.text: A null source or identifier cannot key the node and drops the row; the release carries none.
The binding only lists identifiers; it does not resolve them to external records or assert equivalence.

claims.text: One HAS_ESSENTIALITY_SCREEN edge per target_essentiality screen row.

targetId|HAS_ESSENTIALITY_SCREEN|depmapId|expression: 22,171,776 edges. 703,552 target-cell-line pairs occur twice and 29,448 three times, distinguished only by expression, so the expression value is part of the key.

frames.text: geneEffect is the per-line dependency score, expression the target's expression in the line, mutation the screen's mutation label, and isEssential the repeated target-level flag.

limitations.text: No edge means no screen row for the pair. A null expression (1,248,278 screens) or mutation (22,084,868) is a source gap, not a zero or a wild-type line.

The edge set is 22,171,776 rows over 1,208 lines. Read isEssential once per target, not per edge. diseaseCellLineId is not carried. A dependency is an in-vitro observation and does not establish human essentiality.

claims.text: One HAS_GO_ANNOTATION edge per element of target.go.
target::HAS_GO_ANNOTATION::go.id::source::evidence::aspect::geneProduct::ecoId, with the empty string for a null ecoId. The tuple is unique per target and term in the release.

frames.text: The GO term node is keyed by go.id only; the evidence tuple stays on the edge, so a term annotated twice produces two edges.

limitations.text: A null go.id cannot key an endpoint and drops the row; the release carries none. An empty go array produces no edge.
The binding does not expand GO ancestors and does not verify the cited reference. The GO term node itself is bound from the go dataset.

claims.text: One HAS_HALLMARK edge per element of target.hallmarks.attributes.
target::HAS_HALLMARK::hallmark::attribute::name::pmid::description.

frames.text: The statement fields are on the node; the edge records that the target carries the statement.

limitations.text: No element means no attribute hallmark statement for the target.
The edge adds no score, direction or confidence of its own.

target::HAS_HALLMARK::hallmark::cancerHallmark::label::pmid::impact::description.

frames.text: The statement fields are on the node; the edge records that the target carries the statement.

limitations.text: No element means no cancer-hallmark statement for the target.
The edge adds no score or confidence of its own.

claims.text: One HAS_HOMOLOGUE edge per row of homology.
targetId|HAS_HOMOLOGUE|speciesId|targetGeneId: 3,817,240 edges, one per source row; the row set is unique on (targetId, targetGeneId) and the species is determined by the gene.

frames.text: The edge points at the species gene node and carries the pair class, the text confidence flag and both directional identity values. All 25,537 target ids resolve to a TargetNode.

limitations.text: No edge means no compara pair for that target and gene. 53,196 targets have no row and therefore no edge.

The 3,817,240 edges are 3,817,240 source measurements, not 3,817,240 undirected pairs: human pairs are stored in both directions, so 1,772,033 human pairs account for 3,544,066 edges. The edge keeps both directions rather than choosing one, because the identity values differ by direction and 8,190 human rows have no reverse.

claims.text: One HAS_MOUSE_MODEL edge per biologicalModels element of a mouse_phenotype row, from the row's human target to the model.
targetFromSourceId|HAS_MOUSE_MODEL|biologicalModels.id: 37,474 distinct target-model pairs over 256,254 model entries; repeated rows collapse.

frames.text: targetFromSourceId is a human ENSG on every row (11,869 distinct) and all values resolve to a TargetNode. The mouse gene ids (targetInModelEnsemblId, ENSMUSG) and MGI ids on the same row identify the model's gene, not the target, so they are not the edge source.

limitations.text: The drop_null filter drops the 745 model entries with a null id; they cannot key a model node. A target with no edge has no curated mouse model in the release.
The edge does not resolve the mouse gene to a human orthologue beyond the release's targetFromSourceId mapping, and it says nothing about whether the model's phenotype matches a human phenotype.

claims.text: The target's prioritisation profile.
targetId|HAS_PRIORITISATION_PROFILE|targetId: 78,733 edges, one per target.

frames.text: The edge carries no property: every attribute is on the profile node, whose key is the same target id, so an edge property would duplicate a node property.

limitations.text: No edge means no profile was computed; none occur.
The edge adds no evidence and no score of its own; it exists so the profile is reachable from the target without putting 17 computed columns on TARGET.

targetId|HAS_SAFETY_EVENT|safety event key; 4,387 edges, unique.

false is an asserted negative, not a missing assessment, and true is the source's assessment rather than demonstrated druggability.

(targetId, transcriptId). 644,292 edges, 0 duplicates.

The edge is annotation, not expression, and alternative transcripts are not interchangeable isoforms.

target::PARTICIPATES_IN::pathwayId; unique per target.

limitations.text: A null pathwayId cannot key an endpoint and drops the row; none occur.
Pathway nodes are bound from the reactome dataset, not from this array; the edge adds no hierarchy of its own.

claims.text: One TargetClassNode per element of target.targetClass.
target_class::id::label::level.

frames.text: The numeric id is reused across levels, so label and level are in the key; the same class shared by many targets yields one node.

The binding does not infer parent-child class relations from level.

modality|category: 28 nodes from 528,332 rows. The binding reads every target row, so the repeated pairs collapse to 28 records.

frames.text: modality is a source code and category is the source's evidence label.

limitations.text: A bucket absent here is not an axis in this release.
The modality codes are not expanded in this dataset. The node collects source labels; it does not grade or order them.

claims.text: One TranscriptNode per row of transcript.
transcript.transcriptId, the ENST accession. All 644,292 rows have a distinct id, so no row is dropped.

frames.text: The row is one transcript. proteinId is the translation, null for non-coding biotypes. The target is bound as a separate edge, not as a node property.

limitations.text: A null transcriptId cannot be keyed and would be dropped; there are none in 26.09. A target with no transcript rows has no transcripts in the release.
The flags and exons arrays stay in the source: 5,078,384 exon intervals and four flag vocabularies are not published. The node is not a protein, a structure or an expression observation.

claims.text: One VariantNode per row of variant.
variant.variantId, the release's chromosome_position_ref_alt string.

frames.text: Use variantId for joins. rsIds, hgvsId and dbXrefs are separate cross-references, not alternative keys.

limitations.text: A variant absent here has no phenotypic information in the release. It is not absent from the genome.
The id is build- and allele-spelling-specific; a different representation is a different string. The node carries no effect; effects are target- and transcript-specific edges.

claims.text: One edge per variant with a non-null mostSevereConsequenceId, pointing at the normalized SO term.
variantId -> so.id after replacing SO_ with SO: in the consequence id.

frames.text: 7,886,761 edges; the one variant with a null id is filtered by drop_null. The rewrite is measured: all 26 distinct consequence ids fail to join so.id as written and all 26 resolve after it.

limitations.text: No edge for a variant whose mostSevereConsequenceId is null, not a variant with no consequence.
Only the SO vocabulary's id form is normalized; the term labels and severity ranking are the release's. The edge is variant-level and does not name a transcript or target.

claims.text: One edge per variantEffect array element that names a target, keyed by variant, target and method.
(variantId, targetId, method). assessment is omitted from the key because it is null on every GERP row and adds no discrimination: 0 duplicate triples and 0 duplicate four-tuples.

frames.text: 9,423,729 of 17,960,867 elements become edges. The 8,537,138 elements without a target are VEP (7,886,762) and FoldX (650,376) and are filtered by drop_null. Every targetId resolves to target.id (0 dangling of 76,496 distinct targets).

limitations.text: No edge means the element names no target or the variant has no variantEffect element; it does not mean the variant is neutral for the target.
Each method is a separate edge; there is no consensus edge. Scores are method-specific. VEP and FoldX predictions stay in the source with no target endpoint.

claims.text: One edge per variant transcript consequence whose impact is HIGH or MODERATE, pointing at the transcript node.
(variantId, transcriptId). 0 duplicate pairs in the published subset; the full source array has 280,906,222 elements and 0 duplicate pairs.

frames.text: 1,431,373 edges: HIGH 296,862 and MODERATE 1,134,511. Every transcriptId resolves to transcript.transcriptId and every targetId to target.id (0 dangling). All source elements have both ids.

limitations.text: LOW (667,184) and MODIFIER (278,807,665) elements are not published. No edge therefore means the consequence is not protein-altering at HIGH or MODERATE level, not that the variant has no transcript consequence.

This is a bounded subset of a 280.9M-element array: carrying all elements would add 279,474,849 mostly intronic/intergenic rows. siftPrediction and polyphenPrediction are null on every element, so the published edges carry no SIFT or PolyPhen value.
